## System info
- transformers 5.16.1 (also read 5.15.1 source), torch 2.11, CUDA (GB10 / DGX Spark); model type `qwen3_5` (hybrid: 48 Gated-DeltaNet layers `LinearAttentionLayer` + 16 attention layers `DynamicLayer` in `DynamicCache(config=...)`)

## Description
`Cache.crop(tokens_to_remove)` documents: "For layers that do not need to keep all the past states in memory, such as sliding window layers or linear attention layers, this will also restrict the size of the cached states back to their minimal working size", and `activate_past_recording()` says the cache "will wait for a call to `crop` … in order to be able to retrieve previous full states".

For `LinearAttentionCacheLayerMixin` this is only true for **conv states**. `crop` slices `conv_states` back by `tokens_to_remove`, but `recurrent_states` is never touched: the GDN layer (`modeling_qwen3_5.py`, `torch_chunk_gated_delta_rule` / `torch_recurrent_gated_delta_rule` → `cache_params.update_recurrent_state(last_recurrent_state, layer_idx)`) writes the state **after the whole forward** back into the cache, and there is no recorded pre-forward state to return to.

Consequence for any draft-and-verify loop that runs the target over a block of candidate tokens and then crops the rejected suffix (speculative decoding, lookahead, DFlash-style block verification): after every partially accepted block the recurrent state contains the rejected tokens. The target's later logits then depend on tokens that were never emitted, so greedy output depends on the drafter — the loop is not lossless.

## Measurement (Qwen3.5-class 27B hybrid, bf16)
Teacher-forced on one fixed token sequence with two different draft proposal patterns (i.e. different rejected suffixes), same model, same committed tokens, block size 16:
- rejection pattern A: target argmax equals the reference at **384/384** positions (the reference text was produced with this pattern);
- rejection pattern B: target argmax differs at **41/384, 12/384, 38/384, 15/384** positions on four prompts (3–11 %), with top-1 − top-2 logit margins of **0.6 – 2.4** at the first differing positions — a real distribution shift, not bf16 rounding (rounding-level flips have margins 0 – 0.25 here).
- HF `generate` (M=1, recurrent kernel) vs the block loop disagree in the same way; restoring the recurrent states before re-running only the accepted rows removes the effect.

## Minimal reproduction sketch
```python
cache = DynamicCache(config=model.config); cache.activate_past_recording()
model(prefix_ids, past_key_values=cache, use_cache=True)                                  # clean prefix
clean = copy.deepcopy(cache)
model(t1, past_key_values=clean, use_cache=True)                                          # reference: prefix, t1, t2
ref = model(t2, past_key_values=clean, use_cache=True).logits[0, -1]
blk = torch.cat([t1, wrong_ids[:, :k]], dim=1)                                            # "verify" t1 + k rejected drafts
model(blk, past_key_values=cache, use_cache=True); cache.crop(-k)                         # roll the k drafts back
new = model(t2, past_key_values=cache, use_cache=True).logits[0, -1]                      # same tokens as ref: prefix, t1, t2
# -> ref and new differ (argmax flips at moderate margins): cache.layers[i].recurrent_states still include wrong_ids;
#    with an attention-only model the two are identical.
```

## Expected behaviour / suggestions
- When `record_past` is active, record the recurrent state before each `update` (or per token) so `crop` can restore the state at the crop point (memory: one state tensor per recorded step per layer — fine for block sizes ≤ 64); or
- at minimum, make `LinearAttentionCacheLayerMixin.crop` raise (or warn) when `recurrent_states` is initialised, and fix the `Cache.crop` docstring so linear-attention layers are not described as rolled back.

Happy to open a PR for the record-and-restore variant if that direction is acceptable.

### System Info

| item | value |
| --- | --- |
| transformers | 5.17.0 (latest release); also reproduced on 4.57.6 |
| torch | 2.14.0 |
| Python | 3.11.16 |
| platform | macOS 26 (Darwin 25.6.0), Apple M5 Max, arm64 |
| devices tested | cpu and mps — same result on both |
| checkpoints | facebook/musicgen-small, -medium, -large (all three hub config.json files carry "decoder": {"dropout": 0.1, "attention_dropout": 0.0, "activation_dropout": 0.0}) |

### Who can help?

_No response_

### Information

- [ ] The official example scripts
- [x] My own modified scripts

### Tasks

- [ ] An officially supported task in the `examples` folder (such as GLUE/SQuAD, ...)
- [x] My own task or dataset (give details below)

### Reproduction

Self-contained script, no data needed, ~20 s on CPU:
https://github.com/KhalidIbrahem/somali-music-archive/blob/resume-v1/docs/oss/musicgen_dropout_repro.py

It loads `facebook/musicgen-small`, generates 5 s of audio, re-encodes it with the model's own EnCodec so the labels are in-distribution, then scores the same tokens with the same weights under four settings:

```
$ python musicgen_dropout_repro.py cpu        # transformers 5.17.0
transformers decoder config: dropout=0.1 attention_dropout=0.0 activation_dropout=0.0 layers=24
functional dropout attributes > 0: 37 total, 25 in decoder  (nn.Dropout modules: 37 total, 0 in decoder)
labels shape (1, 247, 4)
eval mode                        loss = 4.4363
train mode                       loss = 10.2944
train mode, nn.Dropout p=0       loss = 10.2059
train mode, functional attrs=0   loss = 4.4363
```

| transformers | device | eval | train | train, `nn.Dropout` p=0 | train, functional attrs=0 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 5.17.0 | cpu | 4.4363 | 10.2944 | 10.2059 | 4.4363 |
| 5.17.0 | mps | 4.6730 | 9.6468 | 9.7517 | 4.6730 |
| 4.57.6 | cpu | 4.8118 | 9.6970 | 9.5071 | 4.8118 |
| 4.57.6 | mps | 4.6730 | 9.6468 | 9.7517 | 4.6730 |

The eval/train gap is the same on every row. (CPU eval loss differs between versions only because the 5 s sample the script generates for itself differs; the mps rows are bit-identical across versions.)

Note: on 5.x + `mps` the script loads with `attn_implementation="eager"`, because T5 attention now goes through SDPA and torch's MPS SDPA kernel raises `NotImplementedError: ... does not support dropout` as soon as the text encoder runs in train mode. Eager gives the same losses as SDPA on CPU. That is a separate MPS limitation and not part of this issue.

### Actual behavior

`model.train()` on an unmodified checkpoint raises token cross-entropy from ~4.5 to ~10 nats, above the 7.6 nats of a uniform distribution over the 2048 codes. Setting every `nn.Dropout` module to `p=0` changes nothing, because the MusicGen decoder contains no `nn.Dropout` modules (all 37 in the model are in the T5 text encoder). Setting the 25 float attributes the decoder reads via `nn.functional.dropout(..., training=self.training)` to 0 makes train mode equal eval mode to four decimals.

Fine-tuning under the default config therefore fits a forward path that evaluation never sees. In our LoRA runs (r=16, decoder attention projections, three learning rates, two corpora) validation loss climbed from 4.5 to 6.7–7.2 by step 1000 while training loss "converged" toward 7.2; zeroing the attributes turned the identical recipe into a normal run (val 4.5132 → 4.4785 on unseen songs).

### Root cause

1. `MusicgenDecoderConfig` defaults `dropout=0.1` (`configuration_musicgen.py` line 41 in 5.17.0, `dropout: float | int = 0.1`; an `__init__` default in 4.x). `MusicgenMelodyDecoderConfig` does the same.
2. The conversion script did not override it, so every released hub config carries `dropout: 0.1`.
3. The original models were trained with **no dropout**: audiocraft's `config/model/lm/default.yaml` sets `dropout: 0.` for the transformer LM.
4. `modeling_musicgen.py` applies the value functionally at 25 sites in the decoder: on the summed codebook embeddings in `MusicgenDecoder.forward` (line 524 in 5.17.0; 594 in 4.57.6) and after self-attention, cross-attention and the FFN in each of the 24 `MusicgenDecoderLayer`s (lines 356, 371, 380 in 5.17.0; 385, 403, 412 in 4.57.6). The remaining 12 functional attributes are `T5Attention.dropout` in the text encoder and are harmless (train-mode text encoder alone: 4.6567 vs 4.6730 eval).

The weights are not robust to a perturbation they never met. A single site is enough: keeping only `MusicgenDecoder.dropout` at 0.1 gives 9.59; keeping only layer 0's dropout gives 8.17 (isolation run, mps).

(A second, unrelated gap surfaces in the same script — `forward(labels=...)` raises until `decoder_start_token_id` is set by hand, and on 5.x the outer config no longer has the attribute. I'll file that separately; the repro sets it so this issue reproduces on its own.)

### Proposed fix

The minimal, uncontroversial part is making the released checkpoints' configs say what they were trained with:

1. **Hub config PRs** for `facebook/musicgen-{small,medium,large,melody,...}` setting `"dropout": 0.0`. I'm happy to open these.

Two optional additions in `transformers` itself, if you'd like them — I'd rather ask than guess which you prefer:

2. **A one-time warning** in `MusicgenForConditionalGeneration.train()` (and the melody class) when any of `dropout`, `activation_dropout`, `attention_dropout` is non-zero, saying the train path will differ from the eval path and how to switch it off.
3. **Default `dropout=0.0`** in `MusicgenDecoderConfig` / `MusicgenMelodyDecoderConfig`, with a docstring noting the released models were trained without dropout. This only affects configs built without an explicit value.

Test sketch for (3), `tests/models/musicgen/test_modeling_musicgen.py`:

```python
def test_train_mode_matches_eval_mode_by_default(self):
    # The released MusicGen checkpoints were trained without dropout; a default
    # config must not turn any on, or fine-tuning optimises a path that
    # generation never uses.
    config, inputs = self.model_tester.prepare_config_and_inputs_for_common()
    model = MusicgenForCausalLM(config).eval()
    torch.manual_seed(0)
    eval_logits = model(**inputs).logits
    model.train()
    torch.manual_seed(0)
    train_logits = model(**inputs).logits
    torch.testing.assert_close(eval_logits, train_logits)
```

plus the same test parametrised over the melody model, and one asserting the warning in (2) fires exactly once for a config with `dropout=0.1`.

Tell me which of (2)/(3) you'd take and I'll open the PR against `main`.

### Why it matters

Every public "fine-tune MusicGen with LoRA" recipe on top of transformers calls `model.train()` on these checkpoints. Anyone who did not notice validation loss diverging from step ~250 will have concluded, as we first did, that their data was the problem.

### Expected behavior

With the pretrained weights, the train-mode forward pass should be a mildly regularised version of the eval-mode pass — a loss a few hundredths of a nat higher, not double. Fine-tuning the decoder (full or LoRA) should therefore optimise roughly the function that generate() uses.

### Actual behavior

`model.train()` on an unmodified checkpoint raises token cross-entropy from ~4.5 to ~10 nats, above the 7.6 nats of a uniform distribution over the 2048 codes. Setting the 25 float attributes the decoder reads via `nn.functional.dropout(..., training=self.training)` to 0 makes train mode equal eval mode to four decimals.

Fine-tuning under the default config therefore fits a forward path that evaluation never sees. In our LoRA runs (r=16, decoder attention projections, three learning rates, two corpora) validation loss climbed from 4.5 to 6.7–7.2 by step 1000 while training loss "converged" toward 7.2; zeroing the attributes turned the identical recipe into a normal run (val 4.5132 → 4.4785 on unseen songs).

1. `MusicgenDecoderConfig` defaults `dropout=0.1` (`configuration_musicgen.py` line 41 in 5.17.0, `dropout: float | int = 0.1`; an `__init__` default in 4.x). `MusicgenMelodyDecoderConfig` does the same.

4. `modeling_musicgen.py` applies the value functionally at 25 sites in the decoder: on the summed codebook embeddings in `MusicgenDecoder.forward` (line 524 in 5.17.0; 594 in 4.57.6) and after self-attention, cross-attention and the FFN in each of the 24 `MusicgenDecoderLayer`s (lines 356, 371, 380 in 5.17.0; 385, 403, 412 in 4.57.6). ### Tasks

### Reproduction

from huggingface_hub import hf_hub_download
from tokenizers import Tokenizer
from transformers import AutoTokenizer

repo, rev = "CohereLabs/tiny-aya-earth", "821f26a10f8e67a5b453f62d3091d5d4af14b1ae"
published = Tokenizer.from_file(hf_hub_download(repo, "tokenizer.json", revision=rev))
loaded = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(repo, revision=rev)

print(published.encode("1234567", add_special_tokens=False).tokens)
print(type(loaded).__name__, loaded.tokenize("1234567"))

Output:

# 5.17.0
['1', '234', '567']
CohereTokenizer ['1', '2', '3', '4', '5', '6', '7']

# 4.57.6
['1', '234', '567']
CohereTokenizerFast ['1', '234', '567']


Cause:
- The repo's tokenizer_config.json says "tokenizer_class": "CohereTokenizerFast", so v5 loads CohereTokenizer.
- CohereTokenizer.__init__ hard-codes a set of rules and uses them to replace the original pre-tokenization rules in tokenizer.json.
- tiny-aya's tokenizer.json splits digits into groups of three, so in v5 every number is split differently from pretraining.

Affected repos: CohereLabs/tiny-aya-base, -earth, -fire, -water, -global, all with model_type cohere2. tiny-aya-l2-thinker was already fixed by Cohere on September 25. Their fix, in commit e9feb287, changed tokenizer_class to PreTrainedTokenizerFast.

One more consequence: with save_pretrained in v5, the hard-coded rules are written into the saved tokenizer.json. So a tiny-aya model that is fine-tuned and saved in v5 still splits digits one by one, even when it is later loaded with 4.57.6.

Comparison with other models, and a possible fix: the same kind of problem in Qwen is #49066, already fixed by #49116, which added several model_types to MODELS_WITH_INCORRECT_HUB_TOKENIZER_CLASS. However, this approach does not work for Aya, because the class registered for cohere2 in transformers is CohereTokenizer itself, and there is no other Aya-specific class to switch to. One possible fix is to add "coherelabs/tiny-aya-*" to MODEL_IDS_TO_TOKENIZERS_BACKEND in tokenization_auto.py. I simulated this change locally, and the resulting ids are identical to tokenizer.json.
- I have also opened PRs to Cohere on the Hub (earth discussions/3, base discussions/1), with the same change as the l2-thinker one. 

### Expected behavior

Once fixed, the split produced by AutoTokenizer should match the repo's tokenizer.json, i.e. the v4 behavior: ['1', '234', '567'].

### System Info

> **Scope.** This is specific to the `transformers` BLT implementation and therefore to`itazap/blt-1b-hf`. The native-format checkpoints `facebook/blt-1b` and `facebook/blt-entropy` are *not* affected — they carry the correct fields and patch correctly under `facebookresearch/blt`.

## Summary

`BltPatcher` builds its attention with a plain causal mask, but BLT's entropy model is specified with a **local block-causal bias over a 512-token sliding window**. Because entropy is computed over unboundedly long context instead of a 512-token block, predicted entropies are systematically higher, far more bytes clear the shipped `patching_threshold`, and the model patches at roughly **1.15 bytes/patch instead of 4.07** on long inputs — close to byte level, i.e. ~3.5× more latent positions than BLT is designed to run at.

Inputs at or below 512 bytes are unaffected, which is what makes this easy to miss.

## Evidence 1 — the failure is a step at the window size

Bytes per patch at the shipped `patching_threshold = 1.335442066192627`, on 24 documents of wikitext-2 truncated to each length. This is exactly the output of the snippet below, so it can be verified in a couple of minutes on one GPU:

| input length | as shipped (plain causal) | with `sliding_window=512` |
|---|---|---|
| 256 B | 2.758 | 2.758 |
| 512 B | 3.064 | 3.067 |
| 1024 B | **1.694** | 3.332 |
| 2048 B | **1.267** | 3.535 |
| 3840 B | **1.142** | 3.596 |

Identical below the window, monotonically collapsing above it. The two columns can only agree below 512 tokens if the entropy model is meant to be windowed there — which is the point.

## Evidence 2 — the reference implementation agrees with the windowed version

Measured on 320 held-out DCLM windows (1,229,122 bytes), comparing against [`facebookresearch/blt`](https://github.com/facebookresearch/blt) run on the same bytes:

| | `itazap/blt-1b-hf` as shipped | + `sliding_window=512` | native `bytelatent` |
|---|---|---|---|
| bytes/patch at θ = 1.335442 | **1.151** | **4.0716** | **4.0710** |
| θ fitted to 4.53 bytes/patch | 2.84375 | 1.468750 | 1.46875 |
| entropy p50 / p75 / p90 / p99 | 2.4844 / 2.7969 / 3.0469 / 3.5 | 0.4062 / 1.3047 / 2.4062 / 3.2344 | 0.4062 / 1.3047 / 2.4062 / 3.2344 |

Adding the window — and changing nothing else — reproduces the reference implementation: bytes per patch to within 0.0006, threshold to the digit, and four of six entropy quantiles exactly (p10/p25 differ only at bf16 rounding).

## Root cause

`BltPatcher.forward` uses the unwindowed helper:

```python
# transformers/models/blt/modeling_blt.py, in BltPatcher.forward
causal_mask = create_causal_mask(
    config=self.config, inputs_embeds=inputs_embeds, attention_mask=attention_mask,
    past_key_values=past_key_values, position_ids=position_ids,
)
```

and `BltPatcherConfig` carries no `sliding_window` (nor `attn_bias_type`) field at all, so the
information needed to build the right mask is not in the config.

**The information is present upstream and was dropped in conversion.** The official entropy
checkpoint [`facebook/blt-entropy`](https://huggingface.co/facebook/blt-entropy) declares it in its
own `config.json`:

```json
{"args": {
  "attn_bias_type": "local_block_causal",
  "sliding_window": 512,
  "dim": 768, "n_layers": 14, "n_heads": 12, "vocab_size": 260, ...
}}
```

and `facebookresearch/blt` builds the model from exactly those fields:

```python
# bytelatent/entropy_model.py, load_entropy_model
entropy_model_args = LMTransformerArgs(
    ..., attn_bias_type="local_block_causal", sliding_window=512,
)
```

The architecture fields round-trip into `BltPatcherConfig` correctly (`hidden_size=768`,`num_hidden_layers=14`, `num_attention_heads=12`, `vocab_size=260`) — only the two attention-bias fields have no home in the target schema and are silently lost.

For what it's worth, [`facebook/blt-1b`](https://huggingface.co/facebook/blt-1b) also declares `"patch_size": 4.5` alongside `"patching_threshold": 1.335442066192627`, i.e. ~4.5 bytes/patch is the documented design point. The windowed run lands at 4.07 on held-out DCLM; the conversion as shipped lands at 1.15.

## Why it matters

`patching_threshold = 1.335442066192627` is shipped in `config.json` and is only meaningful together with the window it was calibrated under. Without the window, that same threshold puts the model at a completely different operating point, which changes sequence compression, the number of latent-transformer positions, and therefore compute, throughput and latency, as well as anything
measured through the patcher. Anyone evaluating BLT through this conversion on inputs longer than 512 bytes is silently running a different model configuration than the released checkpoint describes.

## Suggested fix

Both of these are required:

1. Add `sliding_window: int = 512` to `BltPatcherConfig` (and carry it in `config.json`).
2. In `BltPatcher.forward`, dispatch to `create_sliding_window_causal_mask` when it is set.

**Adding the config field alone does not fix it.** Setting `patcher_config.sliding_window = 512` propagates correctly (`m.model.patcher.config.sliding_window` reads `512`) and changes nothing — still 1.151 bytes/patch at 3840 B. `create_causal_mask` sets
`mask_factory_function = causal_mask_function` unconditionally and never reads `sliding_window`; only `create_sliding_window_causal_mask` does, at `masking_utils.py:1170`. So the field is inert until the call site dispatches on it.

`transformers.masking_utils.create_sliding_window_causal_mask` already exists and is a drop-in for this call site — the workaround below patches exactly that and reproduces the reference numbers.



### Who can help?

@ArthurZucker @Cyrilvallez @vasqu

### Information

- [ ] The official example scripts
- [x] My own modified scripts

### Tasks

- [ ] An officially supported task in the `examples` folder (such as GLUE/SQuAD, ...)
- [ ] My own task or dataset (give details below)

### Reproduction


## Reproduction

```python
import torch
from datasets import load_dataset
from transformers import AutoTokenizer, BltConfig, BltForCausalLM
import transformers.models.blt.modeling_blt as MB
from transformers.masking_utils import create_sliding_window_causal_mask
from transformers.models.blt.configuration_blt import BltPatcherConfig

MID = "itazap/blt-1b-hf"
_orig = MB.create_causal_mask

def enable_window(window=512):
    def dispatch(config=None, **kw):
        if isinstance(config, BltPatcherConfig):          # patcher only; trunks stay causal
            config.sliding_window = window
            return create_sliding_window_causal_mask(config=config, **kw)
        return _orig(config=config, **kw)
    MB.create_causal_mask = dispatch

# enable_window()            # <-- toggle this line to see the difference

tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(MID)
cfg = BltConfig.from_pretrained(MID)
if not hasattr(cfg, "num_hidden_layers"):
    cfg.num_hidden_layers = cfg.global_config.num_hidden_layers
m = BltForCausalLM.from_pretrained(MID, config=cfg, dtype=torch.bfloat16).eval()
m.model.patcher.cuda()
th = float(cfg.patching_threshold)

rows = [t for t in load_dataset("Salesforce/wikitext", "wikitext-2-raw-v1",
                                split="test")["text"] if t.strip()]
blob = "".join(rows)                       # wikitext rows are single paragraphs; concatenate
docs = [blob[i * 4000:(i + 1) * 4000] for i in range(24)]

with torch.inference_mode():
    for L in (256, 512, 1024, 2048, 3840):
        total = patches = 0
        for d in docs:
            ids = tok(d[:L], add_special_tokens=True)["input_ids"][:L]
            x = torch.tensor([ids], device="cuda")
            entropies, _, _ = m.model.patcher(
                x, patch_size=None, threshold=1e9, max_patch_length=None,
                patching_batch_size=1, device=x.device)
            e = entropies[0, 1:].float()
            patches += 2 + int((e > th).sum())   # BLT always opens patches at tokens 0 and 1
            total += len(ids)
        print(f"input {L:5d} B -> {total/patches:6.3f} bytes/patch")
```

Reproduces the Evidence 1 table: identical at 256 B, then 1.142 vs 3.596 bytes/patch at 3840 B with the window off vs on. (The tokenizer prints a `1025 > 1024` length warning; it comes from the tokenizer's `model_max_length` metadata and does not affect the patcher.)

## Environment

- `transformers` 5.14.1
- `itazap/blt-1b-hf`, bfloat16, single A5000
- reference: `facebookresearch/blt` @ `facebook/blt-1b` + `facebook/blt-entropy`

### Expected behavior

`BltPatcher` should reproduce the attention behavior of BLT's original entropy model. Specifically, the entropy model should use local block-causal attention with a 512-token sliding window, as specified by the original `facebook/blt-entropy` configuration.

Accordingly, `BltPatcherConfig` should preserve the `sliding_window=512` setting during checkpoint conversion, and `BltPatcher.forward` should construct a sliding-window causal mask rather than an unbounded causal mask. With this behavior, entropy estimates and patch boundaries should remain consistent with the reference `facebookresearch/blt` implementation, including for inputs longer than 512 bytes.

```python
import transformers.models.blt.modeling_blt as MB
from transformers.masking_utils import create_sliding_window_causal_mask
from transformers.models.blt.configuration_blt import BltPatcherConfig

MID = "itazap/blt-1b-hf"
_orig = MB.create_causal_mask

def enable_window(window=512):
    def dispatch(config=None, **kw):
        if isinstance(config, BltPatcherConfig):          # patcher only; trunks stay causal
            config.sliding_window = window
            return create_sliding_window_causal_mask(config=config, **kw)
        return _orig(config=config, **kw)
    MB.create_causal_mask = dispatch

# enable_window()            # <-- toggle this line to see the difference

tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(MID)
cfg = BltConfig.from_pretrained(MID)
if not hasattr(cfg, "num_hidden_layers"):
    cfg.num_hidden_layers = cfg.global_config.num_hidden_layers
m = BltForCausalLM.from_pretrained(MID, config=cfg, dtype=torch.bfloat16).eval()
m.model.patcher.cuda()
th = float(cfg.patching_threshold)

rows = [t for t in load_dataset("Salesforce/wikitext", "wikitext-2-raw-v1",
                                split="test")["text"] if t.strip()]
blob = "".join(rows)                       # wikitext rows are single paragraphs; concatenate
docs = [blob[i * 4000:(i + 1) * 4000] for i in range(24)]

with torch.inference_mode():
    for L in (256, 512, 1024, 2048, 3840):
        total = patches = 0
        for d in docs:
            ids = tok(d[:L], add_special_tokens=True)["input_ids"][:L]
            x = torch.tensor([ids], device="cuda")
            entropies, _, _ = m.model.patcher(
                x, patch_size=None, threshold=1e9, max_patch_length=None,
                patching_batch_size=1, device=x.device)
            e = entropies[0, 1:].float()
            patches += 2 + int((e > th).sum())   # BLT always opens patches at tokens 0 and 1
            total += len(ids)
        print(f"input {L:5d} B -> {total/patches:6.3f} bytes/patch")
```

Reproduces the Evidence 1 table: identical at 256 B, then 1.142 vs 3.596 bytes/patch at 3840 B with the window off vs on. (The tokenizer prints a `1025 > 1024` length warning; it comes from the tokenizer's `model_max_length` metadata and does not affect the patcher.)

## Environment

- `transformers` 5.14.1
- `itazap/blt-1b-hf`, bfloat16, single A5000
- reference: `facebookresearch/blt` @ `facebook/blt-1b` + `facebook/blt-entropy`

### Expected behavior

`BltPatcher` should reproduce the attention behavior of BLT's original entropy model. Specifically, the entropy model should use local block-causal attention with a 512-token sliding window, as specified by the original `facebook/blt-entropy` configuration.

Accordingly, `BltPatcherConfig` should preserve the `sliding_window=512` setting during checkpoint conversion, and `BltPatcher.forward` should construct a sliding-window causal mask rather than an unbounded causal mask. With this behavior, entropy estimates and patch boundaries should remain consistent with the reference `facebookresearch/blt` implementation, including for inputs longer than 512 bytes.", The reconditioning rate was observed to be directly related to this mask degeneration. - With `reconditioning_every_nth_frame` set to 1, this mask degeneration was consistently observed around the ~5th frame. - With `reconditioning_every_nth_frame` set to the library default of 16, the degeneration was observed at ~30th frame. - With reconditioning disabled, there was no observed mask degeneration. Left shows the ballooned bounding boxes (generated from the segmentation masks) + concept prompts. Right shows the segmented pixels (colour of the pixels isn't relevant), where you can see parts of the segmented masks growing on the leftmost side. ### Suspected cause `_prepare_recondition_masks` binarizes the detection mask in correction mode (`recondition_on_trk_masks=False`): [modeling_sam3_video.py:979-983](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/main/src/transformers/models/sam3_video/modeling_sam3_video.py#L979-L983) ```python else:     # Correction mode: detector corrects drift, replace tracker mask with detection mask     new_mask = det_out["mask"][det_idx : det_idx + 1].unsqueeze(1)     reconditioned_masks[obj_idx] = new_mask >= 0.5 ``` Eventually, it gets passed to a branch that expects logits, not the binarized mask. [modeling_sam3_video.py:1205-1206](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/main/src/transformers/models/sam3_video/modeling_sam3_video.py#L1205-L1206) [modeling_sam3_video.py:941-946](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/main/src/transformers/models/sam3_video/modeling_sam3_video.py#L941-L946) [modeling_sam3_tracker_video:2732-2737](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/main/src/transformers/models/sam3_tracker_video/modeling_sam3_tracker_video.py#L2732-L2737) ### Suggested Fix Drop the `>= 0.5` from `reconditioned_masks[obj_idx] = new_mask >= 0.5` so `_encode_new_memory` performs sigmoid on logits. For me, monkey patching the `_prepare_recondition_masks` function with this fixed the reconditioning for me. ### Who can help? _No response_ ### Information - [ ] The official example scripts - [x] My own modified scripts ### Tasks - [ ] An officially supported task in the `examples` folder (such as GLUE/SQuAD, ...) - [x] My own task or dataset (give details below) ### Reproduction This example directly calls the library's `_prepare_recondition_masks()` function with a small synthetic mask, then reproduces the two downstream operations applied before memory encoding: the `.float()` conversion and the `sigmoid(mask) * scale + bias` transform. ```python import torch from transformers.models.sam3_video.modeling_sam3_video import Sam3VideoModel # Minimal stand-ins so _prepare_recondition_masks() can run class _Session: def obj_id_to_idx(self, obj_id): return obj_id class _Model: recondition_on_trk_masks = False # correction mode high_conf_thresh = 0.8 # Fake detector output: one 2x2 mask represented as logits det_out = { "mask": torch.tensor([[[-8.0, 6.0], [ 6.0,-8.0]]]) } # Pretend the tracker predicted exactly the same mask trk_masks = det_out["mask"].clone() # Call the library reconditioning step recond, _ = Sam3VideoModel._prepare_recondition_masks( _Model(), _Session(), 0, det_out, trk_masks, {0: 0}, torch.tensor([0.95]), ) # Reproduce the next library step: # high_res_masks[obj_idx] = recond_mask.float() high_res = recond[0].float() # Simulate the transform used by the memory encoder SCALE = 20.0 BIAS = -10.0 # Current behavior (binary mask treated as logits) mem_current = torch.sigmoid(high_res) * SCALE + BIAS # Expected behavior if detector logits were preserved mem_logits = torch.sigmoid(det_out["mask"]) * SCALE + BIAS print("dtype:", recond[0].dtype) print(mem_current) print(mem_logits) ``` ### Expected behavior Output of the above code snippet: dtype: torch.bool tensor([[[[0.0000, 4.6212], [4.6212, 0.0000]]]]) tensor([[[-9.9933, 9.9505], [ 9.9505, -9.9933]]]) I expect that it should look closer to the second output because the first output means it reduces the contrast between the foreground and background logits which does not seem right.

body_text:
The `response_template` added to the Gemma 4 instruct checkpoints (for example in [google/gemma-4-E2B-it#40](https://huggingface.co/google/gemma-4-E2B-it/discussions/40)) parses the model's reasoning into a `thinking` field, following the convention of the [response parsing docs](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/chat_response_parsing). The chat template of these checkpoints, however, reads reasoning back only from `reasoning` or `reasoning_content`. A parsed tool-calling turn appended to the conversation is therefore re-rendered without its reasoning, although the template does render reasoning in tool-calling turns.

```python
from transformers import AutoProcessor

processor = AutoProcessor.from_pretrained("google/gemma-4-E2B-it")
tool_calls = [{"type": "function", "function": {"name": "multiply", "arguments": {"a": 3, "b": 4}}}]
user = {"role": "user", "content": [{"type": "text", "text": "What is 3*4?"}]}
assistant = {"role": "assistant", "content": [], "reasoning_content": "I should multiply.", "tool_calls": tool_calls}
tool = {"role": "tool", "name": "multiply", "content": [{"type": "text", "text": "12"}]}

prefix = processor.apply_chat_template([user], add_generation_prompt=True, enable_thinking=True, tokenize=True, return_dict=False)[0]
ids = processor.apply_chat_template([user, assistant], enable_thinking=True, tokenize=True, return_dict=False)[0]
parsed = processor.tokenizer.parse_response(ids[len(prefix):], prefix=prefix)
print(parsed)

text = processor.apply_chat_template([user, parsed, tool], add_generation_prompt=True, enable_thinking=True, tokenize=False)
print("I should multiply." in text)
```

```
{'role': 'assistant', 'thinking': 'I should multiply.', 'tool_calls': [{'function': {'arguments': {'a': 3, 'b': 4}, 'name': 'multiply'}, 'type': 'function'}]}
False
```

With the key renamed to `reasoning_content`, the reasoning is rendered. The fix is either a `response_template` that outputs `reasoning_content`, or a chat template that also reads `thinking`.

The same pair ships in the other Gemma 4 instruct checkpoints (`gemma-4-E4B-it`, `gemma-4-12B-it`, `gemma-4-26B-A4B-it`, `gemma-4-31B-it` and their QAT variants). Any loop that appends the parsed message and re-renders is affected: in TRL's async GRPO trainer, it keeps the tool-calling turns out of the loss (huggingface/trl#7503).

This is distinct from [google/gemma-4-E2B-it#44](https://huggingface.co/google/gemma-4-E2B-it/discussions/44), where the template stops rendering a tool-calling turn's reasoning once a later user message exists: here the reasoning is lost even in the turn right before the tool response, because the parsed message stores it under a key the template does not read.

The chat template of these checkpoints, however, reads reasoning back only from `reasoning` or `reasoning_content`. A parsed tool-calling turn appended to the conversation is therefore re-rendered without its reasoning, although the template does render reasoning in tool-calling turns.

```python
from transformers import AutoProcessor

processor = AutoProcessor.from_pretrained("google/gemma-4-E2B-it")
tool_calls = [{"type": "function", "function": {"name": "multiply", "arguments": {"a": 3, "b": 4}}}]
user = {"role": "user", "content": [{"type": "text", "text": "What is 3*4?"}]}
assistant = {"role": "assistant", "content": [], "reasoning_content": "I should multiply.", "tool_calls": tool_calls}
tool = {"role": "tool", "name": "multiply", "content": [{"type": "text", "text": "12"}]}

prefix = processor.apply_chat_template([user], add_generation_prompt=True, enable_thinking=True, tokenize=True, return_dict=False)[0]
ids = processor.apply_chat_template([user, assistant], enable_thinking=True, tokenize=True, return_dict=False)[0]
parsed = processor.tokenizer.parse_response(ids[len(prefix):], prefix=prefix)
print(parsed)

text = processor.apply_chat_template([user, parsed, tool], add_generation_prompt=True, enable_thinking=True, tokenize=False)
print("I should multiply." in text)
```

```
{'role': 'assistant', 'thinking': 'I should multiply.', 'tool_calls': [{'function': {'arguments': {'a': 3, 'b': 4}, 'name': 'multiply'}, 'type': 'function'}]}
False
```

With the key renamed to `reasoning_content`, the reasoning is rendered. The fix is either a `response_template` that outputs `reasoning_content`, or a chat template that also reads `thinking`.

The same pair ships in the other Gemma 4 instruct checkpoints (`gemma-4-E4B-it`, `gemma-4-12B-it`, `gemma-4-26B-A4B-it`, `gemma-4-31B-it` and their QAT variants). Any loop that appends the parsed message and re-renders is affected: in TRL's async GRPO trainer, it keeps the tool-calling turns out of the loss (huggingface/trl#7503).

This is distinct from [google/gemma-4-E2B-it#44](https://huggingface.co/google/gemma-4-E2B-it/discussions/44), where the template stops rendering a tool-calling turn's reasoning once a later user message exists: here the reasoning is lost even in the turn right before the tool response, because the parsed message stores it under a key the template does not read.

```

- Using distributed or parallel set-up in script?: No
- Using GPU in script?: No
- GPU type: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090
```

### Who can help?

**The documented route fails.** `model_kwargs` is an "Additional dictionary of keyword arguments passed along to the
model's `from_pretrained(..., **model_kwargs)` function" (`transformers/pipelines/__init__.py:821-822`), and
`AutoModel.from_pretrained` documents `code_revision` as the parameter for code in another repository. But `pipeline()`
already passes an explicit `code_revision=` to `AutoConfig.from_pretrained` at lines 901 and 934 and then expands
`**model_kwargs` into the same call, so the keyword arrives twice. Observed:

```
TypeError: transformers.models.auto.configuration_auto.AutoConfig.from_pretrained() got multiple values for keyword
argument 'code_revision'
```

raised before any Hub request. Expected: the pin forwarded to the model load, as the `model_kwargs` docstring implies.

**The undocumented route is honoured on one load out of three.** A top-level `code_revision` is popped at line 846 and
handed to those two `AutoConfig` calls and to custom pipeline class loading, but not to `load_model` at line 1035 and
not to the keyword arguments that reach the tokenizer and processor loads. The pipeline is constructed, the pipeline's
own `AutoConfig` call fetches the cross-repository configuration code at the pinned commit, and the model load and the
tokenizer load fetch the modeling code and that same configuration code again with `revision=None`.

What to expect on this second route is less clear, since the keyword is undocumented for `pipeline()` and the docstring
routes unknown arguments to the pipeline class initializer (lines 824-825). We therefore report it as a pin that is
partly honoured rather than as a broken promise. Accepting it properly, or rejecting it, would both be better than
honouring it on one load out of three.

**Suggested fix.** Two small edits in `transformers/pipelines/__init__.py`, which is what our verified repair did by
wrapping the function. First, at line 846, accept the documented route and take the key out of `model_kwargs` so only
one value reaches the `AutoConfig` calls:

```python
code_revision = kwargs.pop("code_revision", None) or model_kwargs.pop("code_revision", None)
```

`model_kwargs` is already defaulted to an empty dictionary a few lines above, so this is safe. Second, pass that value
to the loads that never see it, namely the `load_model` call at line 1035 and the keyword arguments handed to
`_resolve_tokenizer` at line 1053 and to the matching processor resolvers. With both in place the documented call loads
and the pinned commit is used for the configuration, model and tokenizer code.

An alternative to the first edit is to reject `code_revision` inside `model_kwargs` and point at the supported spelling,
but that spelling then needs documenting and still needs the second edit.

**Versions as tested.** transformers 5.18.0, huggingface_hub 1.33.0, torch 2.6.0+cu124, accelerate 1.15.0, on Windows.
Not tested on other transformers releases.

### Information

- [ ] The official example scripts
- [ ] My own modified scripts

### Tasks

- [ ] An officially supported task in the `examples` folder (such as GLUE/SQuAD, ...)
- [ ] My own task or dataset (give details below)

### Reproduction

**The `TypeError` needs only a local directory and no network.** Save any tiny model and its tokenizer into a directory,
then:

```python
from transformers import pipeline

pipeline("feature-extraction", model=local_dir, model_kwargs={"code_revision": "0" * 40})
```

Observed on 5.18.0: the `TypeError` quoted above. The same call with `code_revision="0" * 40` as a top-level keyword
succeeds, which confirms the duplicate-keyword diagnosis rather than a rejected value.

**The partial pin needs two small repositories**, because `code_revision` only applies to code outside the model's own
repository. Repository B holds `configuration_x.py` and `modeling_x.py` in two commits that differ observably.
Repository A is a tiny checkpoint whose `config.json` `auto_map` names `B--configuration_x.XConfig` and
`B--modeling_x.XModel`. Wrap `huggingface_hub.hf_hub_download` to record the `revision` of each request, then:

```python
pipeline(task, model="<A>", revision="<A commit>", code_revision="<B first commit>", trust_remote_code=True)
```

Observed: that configuration file at the pinned commit from the pipeline's own `AutoConfig` call, and the same file plus
the modeling file at `revision=None` from the model and tokenizer loads.

### Expected behavior

This is the loss of a caller-specified pin, not remote code execution on its own. Reaching remote code requires
`trust_remote_code=True`, and the refusal behaviour was correct in our runs.

The first half is a plain correctness defect: the documented call fails outright, before any fetch, so there is nothing
to exploit and nothing silently wrong, only a route that does not work. The second half weakens an integrity control
silently, because a caller who found the top-level keyword gets pinned configuration code and unpinned model and
tokenizer code in the same pipeline, with no warning.

Affected: callers who build a pipeline over a model whose `auto_map` names code in another repository and who try to pin
that code. Not affected: callers who use the auto classes directly, and callers who refuse remote code.

Its docstring states non-main ranks are expected to hold an empty meta model. So non-rank-0 should not materialize anything on CPU — transformers should leave them on meta and let the broadcast fill them.

### System Info

* `transformers` version: `5.19.0.dev0`
* Platform: `Linux-6.8.0-1069-gcp-x86_64-with-glibc2.35`
* Python version: `3.10.12`
* `huggingface_hub` version: `1.31.0`
* `safetensors` version: `0.8.0`
* `accelerate` version: `1.14.0`
* PyTorch version (accelerator?): `2.13.0+cu130 (CUDA)`
* GPU type: `NVIDIA L4`
* CUDA version: `13.0`

### Who can help?

@vasqu 

### Information

- [ ] The official example scripts
- [x] My own modified scripts

### Tasks

- [ ] An officially supported task in the `examples` folder (such as GLUE/SQuAD, ...)
- [x] My own task or dataset (give details below)

### Reproduction

→ In Section 3 under "Inference Costs", the [DSA paper](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp/blob/main/DeepSeek_V3_2.pdf) notes that the lightning indexer is `O(L²)`, so we expect `[B, S, T]` scores, which is all DeepSeek's reference [fp8_index](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp/blob/87e509a2e5a100d221c97df52c6e8be7835f0057/inference/kernel.py#L209-L249) writes. In Transformers though, the per-head scores `[B, S, H, T]` are materialized in fp32 [before the sum over heads](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/469230357aab0f2b303b0d638c1f8d06edb14184/src/transformers/models/deepseek_v32/modeling_deepseek_v32.py#L235-L240), and the out-of-place `* softmax_scale` [makes a second copy](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/469230357aab0f2b303b0d638c1f8d06edb14184/src/transformers/models/deepseek_v32/modeling_deepseek_v32.py#L235). So for a single prompt the peak memory is `2 · S² · H · 4` bytes, i.e. `2H` (128 with the default `index_n_heads=64`) times the `[B, S, T]` it's reduced to.
→ Measuring the peak memory shows 2.09 GiB at 2k and 8.16 GiB at 4k. The indexer alone then runs out of memory at 8k on an L4 (by the formula, ~12k on an empty 80 GB GPU), well below the context these models target, and with `device_map` or TP (the indexer isn't sharded) only what's left after the weights is available.
→ The same block is in [DeepSeek-V3.2](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/469230357aab0f2b303b0d638c1f8d06edb14184/src/transformers/models/deepseek_v32/modeling_deepseek_v32.py#L235-L240), [GLM-5](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/469230357aab0f2b303b0d638c1f8d06edb14184/src/transformers/models/glm_moe_dsa/modeling_glm_moe_dsa.py#L236-L241) and [AXK2](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/469230357aab0f2b303b0d638c1f8d06edb14184/src/transformers/models/axk2/modeling_axk2.py#L271-L276), and with small variations in [HY-V4](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/469230357aab0f2b303b0d638c1f8d06edb14184/src/transformers/models/hy_v4/modeling_hy_v4.py#L247-L257).

```python
import torch
from transformers import DeepseekV32Config
from transformers.models.deepseek_v32.modeling_deepseek_v32 import DeepseekV32Indexer

config = DeepseekV32Config(hidden_size=1024, q_lora_rank=1536, qk_rope_head_dim=64)
indexer = DeepseekV32Indexer(config, layer_idx=0).to("cuda", torch.bfloat16)
print(f"index_n_heads={config.index_n_heads} index_head_dim={config.index_head_dim} index_topk={config.index_topk}")
for seq_len in (2048, 4096, 8192, 16384):
    hidden_states = torch.randn(1, seq_len, config.hidden_size, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
    q_resid = torch.randn(1, seq_len, config.q_lora_rank, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
    angle = torch.randn(1, seq_len, config.qk_rope_head_dim // 2, device="cuda")
    emb = torch.cat((angle, angle), dim=-1)
    position_embeddings = (emb.cos().to(torch.bfloat16), emb.sin().to(torch.bfloat16))
    attention_mask = torch.ones(seq_len, seq_len, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bool).tril()[None]
    position_ids = torch.arange(seq_len, device="cuda")[None]
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    torch.cuda.reset_peak_memory_stats()
    base = torch.cuda.memory_allocated()
    try:
        topk_indices = indexer(hidden_states, q_resid, position_embeddings, attention_mask, position_ids)
        torch.cuda.synchronize()
        peak = (torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated() - base) / 2**30
        print(f"seq_len={seq_len:6d}  indexer peak extra memory {peak:6.2f} GiB  out {tuple(topk_indices.shape)}")
    except torch.OutOfMemoryError:
        print(f"seq_len={seq_len:6d}  OutOfMemoryError (would need ~{seq_len * seq_len * config.index_n_heads * 4 / 2**30:.0f} GiB for the [B, S, H, T] fp32 scores alone)")
    del hidden_states, q_resid, attention_mask
    torch.cuda.empty_cache()
```

```
index_n_heads=64 index_head_dim=128 index_topk=2048
seq_len=  2048  indexer peak extra memory   2.09 GiB  out (1, 2048, 2048)
seq_len=  4096  indexer peak extra memory   8.16 GiB  out (1, 4096, 2048)
seq_len=  8192  OutOfMemoryError (would need ~16 GiB for the [B, S, H, T] fp32 scores alone)
seq_len= 16384  OutOfMemoryError (would need ~64 GiB for the [B, S, H, T] fp32 scores alone)
```

### Expected behavior

→ The indexer shouldn't hold the per-head scores for every query at once.

→ In Section 3 under "Inference Costs", the [DSA paper](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp/blob/main/DeepSeek_V3_2.pdf) notes that the lightning indexer is `O(L²)`, so we expect `[B, S, T]` scores, which is all DeepSeek's reference [fp8_index](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp/blob/87e509a2e5a100d221c97df52c6e8be7835f0057/inference/kernel.py#L209-L249) writes. In Transformers though, the per-head scores `[B, S, H, T]` are materialized in fp32 [before the sum over heads](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/469230357aab0f2b303b0d638c1f8d06edb14184/src/transformers/models/deepseek_v32/modeling_deepseek_v32.py#L235-L240), and the out-of-place `* softmax_scale` [makes a second copy](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/469230357aab0f2b303b0d638c1f8d06edb14184/src/transformers/models/deepseek_v32/modeling_deepseek_v32.py#L235). So for a single prompt the peak memory is `2 · S² · H · 4` bytes, i.e. `2H` (128 with the default `index_n_heads=64`) times the `[B, S, T]` it's reduced to.
→ Measuring the peak memory shows 2.09 GiB at 2k and 8.16 GiB at 4k. The indexer alone then runs out of memory at 8k on an L4 (by the formula, ~12k on an empty 80 GB GPU), well below the context these models target, and with `device_map` or TP (the indexer isn't sharded) only what's left after the weights is available.
→ The same block is in [DeepSeek-V3.2](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/469230357aab0f2b303b0d638c1f8d06edb14184/src/transformers/models/deepseek_v32/modeling_deepseek_v32.py#L235-L240), [GLM-5](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/469230357aab0f2b303b0d638c1f8d06edb14184/src/transformers/models/glm_moe_dsa/modeling_glm_moe_dsa.py#L236-L241) and [AXK2](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/469230357aab0f2b303b0d638c1f8d06edb14184/src/transformers/models/axk2/modeling_axk2.py#L271-L276), and with small variations in [HY-V4](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/469230357aab0f2b303b0d638c1f8d06edb14184/src/transformers/models/hy_v4/modeling_hy_v4.py#L247-L257).

```python
import torch
from transformers import DeepseekV32Config
from transformers.models.deepseek_v32.modeling_deepseek_v32 import DeepseekV32Indexer

config = DeepseekV32Config(hidden_size=1024, q_lora_rank=1536, qk_rope_head_dim=64)
indexer = DeepseekV32Indexer(config, layer_idx=0).to("cuda", torch.bfloat16)
print(f"index_n_heads={config.index_n_heads} index_head_dim={config.index_head_dim} index_topk={config.index_topk}")
for seq_len in (2048, 4096, 8192, 16384):
    hidden_states = torch.randn(1, seq_len, config.hidden_size, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
    q_resid = torch.randn(1, seq_len, config.q_lora_rank, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
    angle = torch.randn(1, seq_len, config.qk_rope_head_dim // 2, device="cuda")
    emb = torch.cat((angle, angle), dim=-1)
    position_embeddings = (emb.cos().to(torch.bfloat16), emb.sin().to(torch.bfloat16))
    attention_mask = torch.ones(seq_len, seq_len, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bool).tril()[None]
    position_ids = torch.arange(seq_len, device="cuda")[None]
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    torch.cuda.reset_peak_memory_stats()
    base = torch.cuda.memory_allocated()
    try:
        topk_indices = indexer(hidden_states, q_resid, position_embeddings, attention_mask, position_ids)
        torch.cuda.synchronize()
        peak = (torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated() - base) / 2**30
        print(f"seq_len={seq_len:6d}  indexer peak extra memory {peak:6.2f} GiB  out {tuple(topk_indices.shape)}")
    except torch.OutOfMemoryError:
        print(f"seq_len={seq_len:6d}  OutOfMemoryError (would need ~{seq_len * seq_len * config.index_n_heads * 4 / 2**30:.0f} GiB for the [B, S, H, T] fp32 scores alone)")
    del hidden_states, q_resid, attention_mask
    torch.cuda.empty_cache()
```

### System Info

- Transformers: `5.19.0.dev0`
- Upstream commit: `4cc2aa8430`
- Python: `3.11` (Conda)
- PyTorch: `2.14.1+cpu`
- Platform: Windows
- Device: CPU
- Installation: Editable source checkout (`pip install -e ".[torch,testing]"`)

The issue is reproducible without model weights, datasets, GPU acceleration, or a training run.

### Who can help?

@SunMarc 


### Reproduction

`sort_checkpoints()` incorrectly recognizes directories such as `checkpoint-9.backup` as valid checkpoints. Consequently, `rotate_checkpoints()` can remove legitimate checkpoints while retaining an unrelated backup directory.

**Minimal reproduction:**

```python
from pathlib import Path
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory

from transformers.trainer_utils import (
    get_last_checkpoint,
    sort_checkpoints,
    rotate_checkpoints,
)

with TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
    root = Path(tmp)

    for name in (
        "checkpoint-1",
        "checkpoint-2",
        "checkpoint-9.backup",
    ):
        (root / name).mkdir()

    print("Last checkpoint:",
          Path(get_last_checkpoint(tmp)).name)

    print("Sorted checkpoints:",
          [Path(p).name for p in sort_checkpoints(tmp)])

    rotate_checkpoints(tmp, save_total_limit=1)

    print("After rotation:",
          sorted(p.name for p in root.iterdir()))
```

**Observed output:**

```text
Last checkpoint: checkpoint-2
Sorted checkpoints: ['checkpoint-1', 'checkpoint-2', 'checkpoint-9.backup']
After rotation: ['checkpoint-9.backup']
```

Both valid checkpoints are removed, leaving only the backup directory.

**Suspected cause:**

In `src/transformers/trainer_utils.py`, `sort_checkpoints()` uses:

```python
re.match(f".*{checkpoint_prefix}-([0-9]+)", path)
```

This expression accepts partial matches instead of validating the complete directory name. The `use_mtime=True` path also lacks checkpoint-name validation.

By contrast, `get_last_checkpoint()` uses an anchored pattern and correctly identifies `checkpoint-2`.

The reproduction operates entirely within a temporary directory.

### Expected behavior

Only directories matching the complete `checkpoint-<step>` naming convention should participate in checkpoint sorting and rotation.

With `save_total_limit=1`, the expected surviving directories are:

```text
['checkpoint-2', 'checkpoint-9.backup']
```

Checkpoint validation should be consistent across step-based and modification-time-based sorting. Unrelated directories must neither influence retention decisions nor be deleted.

### Reproduction

Hi, I found an inconsistency between the sequence scan and cached single-token update in Mamba2 and Zamba2.

In `Mamba2Mixer.forward()`, the scan path receives `dt_limit=self.time_step_limit` and applies:

```python
dt = softplus(dt + dt_bias)
dt = clamp(dt, min=dt_limit[0], max=dt_limit[1])
```

The cached decoding path passes the unprocessed `dt`, `dt_bias`, and `dt_softplus=True` to `mamba2_selective_state_update()`, but does not apply the same runtime limits. I checked both the caller and the update function; the clamp is missing from this path.

Consequently, processing a sequence in one pass and processing its prefix followed by cached decoding can use different state-update equations.

For a scalar SSM with `A=-1`, `x=B=C=1`, and `D=0`, the recurrence is:

```text
state = exp(-dt) * state + dt
```

Starting from zero state, the following FP32 examples reproduce the difference. The listed time steps are the positive values before applying the runtime limits. The cached path scans the first two tokens, then applies a single-token update to the third:

| Time steps | Runtime limit | Full scan | Prefix + cached update | Cached update with the same limit |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `[0.1, 0.1, 1.0]` | Maximum `0.1` | 0.27235684 | 1.07007504 | 0.27235684 |
| `[0.0001, 0.0001, 0.0001]` | Minimum `0.001` | 0.00299700 | 0.00209880 | 0.00299700 |

The second case is relevant to Zamba2's default configuration: its mixer sets `time_step_limit` to `(config.time_step_min, inf)`, with `time_step_min=0.001`. Initialization within a particular range does not guarantee that input-dependent time steps remain within it.

I found this through source review and targeted reproductions. I have not measured its effect on a pretrained model's generated outputs. The current-source PyTorch function bodies reproduce the mismatch on both CPU and CUDA, tested independently of accelerated-kernel dispatch; unrestricted controls remain consistent.

Source checked: Transformers commit `90ef040d400e94c771edb8b806c9c294e1b6a13f`:

- [Mamba2 selective state update](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/90ef040d400e94c771edb8b806c9c294e1b6a13f/src/transformers/models/mamba2/modeling_mamba2.py#L192)
- [Mamba2 scan preprocessing](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/90ef040d400e94c771edb8b806c9c294e1b6a13f/src/transformers/models/mamba2/modeling_mamba2.py#L254)
- [Mamba2 recurrent and scan call sites](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/90ef040d400e94c771edb8b806c9c294e1b6a13f/src/transformers/models/mamba2/modeling_mamba2.py#L542)
- [Zamba2 runtime limit](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/90ef040d400e94c771edb8b806c9c294e1b6a13f/src/transformers/models/zamba2/modeling_zamba2.py#L669)

### Expected behavior

For fixed inputs and parameters, sequence scan and prefix-plus-cached decoding should apply the same runtime time-step limits and agree on outputs and final recurrent states within the numerical tolerance of the implementations.

My proposed fix is to apply the same **bias → softplus → runtime clamp** preprocessing before the single-token kernel call, then disable the kernel's corresponding preprocessing to avoid applying it twice. This should cover both the PyTorch fallback and accelerated implementations while preserving the existing scan and fused-training semantics.

A possible change in the single-token branch, after `dt` and `dt_bias` have been expanded to the kernel shapes:

```python
dt_softplus = True
if self.time_step_limit[0] > 0.0 or self.time_step_limit[1] < float("inf"):
    dt = F.softplus(dt.float() + dt_bias.float())
    dt = dt.clamp(*self.time_step_limit)
    dt_bias = torch.zeros_like(dt_bias)
    dt_softplus = False

scan_output = mamba2_selective_state_update(
    recurrent_state, hidden_states, dt, A, B, C, D,
    z=None, dt_bias=dt_bias, dt_softplus=dt_softplus, **kwargs,
)
```

Preprocessing is conditional on an active bound. The zero bias avoids reapplying the learned bias and supports older kernel wrappers that do not handle `dt_bias=None`. This is a proposed implementation; full-model and accelerated-backend checks would still be needed before a PR.

I would like to contribute a minimal fix. Could a maintainer confirm whether this approach fits the intended behavior? I'm happy to address feedback and validate the affected model paths before submitting a PR.

- PyTorch: 2.12.1+cu130
- CUDA: 13.0
- GPU: NVIDIA RTX A1000 Laptop GPU; CPU checks also performed

body_text:
I would like to discuss how Transformers should represent configurable decoder loops. For experiments with pretrained decoder-only models, it is useful to load the original checkpoint, repeat a layer or a range of layers, share its parameters, and keep separate state histories for each logical execution.

I have implemented this in an unofficial fork, [transformers_loop](https://github.com/bebetterest/transformers_loop). The purpose of this discussion and the linked draft PR is to make the implementation available for inspection and reuse, and let maintainers decide whether any part belongs upstream. Possible outcomes include an external extension, separate loop-specific model definitions, or a smaller core interface.

**Reference implementation:** https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/49489 (draft).

## Behavior and example

On a four-layer decoder, the following plans illustrate the intended behavior:

| Plan | Execution order, using zero-based indices |
|---|---|
| Repeat the second layer twice in total | `0, 1, 1, 2, 3` |
| Repeat layers 1 through 2 as a block | `0, 1, 2, 1, 2, 3` |
| Repeat the whole stack twice | `0, 1, 2, 3, 0, 1, 2, 3` |

After installing the fork, its API can be used as follows:

```python
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, RepeatRange

model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained("Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B", dtype="auto")
model.set_layer_execution_plan(repeats=[RepeatRange(1, 2, total_passes=2)])

# model(...) and Hugging Face model.generate(...) follow this plan.
# model.set_layer_execution_plan(None) restores native execution.
```

This checkpoint requires appropriate memory and hardware. Range boundaries are half-open; `total_passes=2` includes the first execution. Explicit plans can also reorder or omit layers.

Repeated visits call the original layer modules. Parameter identities and checkpoint weight keys are preserved, and gradients from all visits accumulate into the shared parameters. Each logical execution has its own KV/recurrent state history; token positions advance once per model forward. The plan is saved in the model configuration.

## Implemented scope

- Built-in adapters for Llama, dense Qwen3.5 text, Gemma3n text, and RecurrentGemma. Other constant-width decoders require an adapter for their masks, arguments, state, and outputs; constant width alone is insufficient.
- Execution-local KV and recurrent caches, dynamic/static/offloaded cache paths, and architecture-specific integration for native KV dependencies and multiple state streams.
- Hugging Face generation, selected compiled paths, portable continuous batching, and supported attention-only paged scheduling.
- Native distributed integrations, standalone sequential pipeline execution, and Trainer checkpoint handling.
- Selected SFT/DPO/GRPO, LoRA/QLoRA, DDP, and ZeRO-2/3 paths with unmodified TRL and Accelerate. The loop and Trainer changes live in the fork's Transformers code.

The [loop guide](https://github.com/bebetterest/transformers_loop/blob/cf2d29f84c9b9449ac639a687737b9d957bc9fc2/loop_readme.md) documents installation, usage, checkpoint rules, implementation, and individual support boundaries. The [maintenance record](https://github.com/bebetterest/transformers_loop/blob/cf2d29f84c9b9449ac639a687737b9d957bc9fc2/MAINTENANCE.md) pins validation to source revisions and dependency versions.

## Validation and limits

Recorded checks cover CPU and two NVIDIA H20 GPUs, including original Qwen3.5-9B weights and selected training/resume controls. These are correctness and short integration checks, not evidence of improved model quality, convergence, production throughput, or compatibility with every trainer/backend combination.

vLLM is not integrated, including its Transformers backend and TRL server/colocate modes; GRPO uses `use_vllm=False`. Real physical multi-host execution is unverified. Pipeline scheduling is sequential, and combined parallel layouts have not been established. Encoder-decoder and changing-width stacks are outside the current scope.

For automatic TRL reference-model loading and later adapter reloads, save and reload a base checkpoint containing the plan before saving only the adapter. An adapter-only checkpoint does not automatically preserve an execution plan configured only in memory.

## Questions for maintainers

1. Should this remain an external extension, use distinct loop-specific model definitions, or expose a small core execution interface?
2. If an interface is useful, how should physical parameter ownership and logical cache/state indices be represented?
3. What would be an appropriate first scope, if any, before considering recurrent state, batching, or distributed integrations?

Related discussions include [native Nanbeige4.2-3B support](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/issues/47667), [KV-sharing standardization](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/47290), and [heterogeneous layer configuration](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/45332). Weight reuse across depth and native KV-sharing dependencies need to compose, and any core proposal would need coordination with these interfaces.

**AI assistance disclosure:** Code agents were used substantially for the implementation, tests, documentation, and these submission drafts. The repository's current code-agent policy is relevant to this submission, including its first-time contributor restriction. Sharing the fork or marking the PR as draft does not create an exemption from that policy.

- Python: 3.12.14
- PyTorch: 2.10.0

@Cyrilvallez 

### Information

- [ ] The official example scripts
- [x] My own modified scripts

### Tasks

- [ ] An officially supported task in the `examples` folder (such as GLUE/SQuAD, ...)
- [x] My own task or dataset (give details below)

### Reproduction

### Background

I encountered this while preparing a DeepSpeed ZeRO-3 LoRA training run for GLM-5.3-Flash. During checkpoint loading, host memory usage grew substantially despite model parameters already being partitioned by ZeRO-3. 

While investigating, I found that every rank reads the full checkpoint into a CPU state dict and performs the same weight conversions, although only rank 0 subsequently copies checkpoint parameters into the model.

This duplicates checkpoint loading and conversion work across ranks.

### Steps to reproduce

I reduced the duplicated-loading behavior to a randomly initialized, two-layer Qwen3 MoE. No pretrained model download, dataset, or training loop is required.

1. Use Transformers commit `e598fbad926d80bc356c0c4d96532030e3dfdb62` in an environment with PyTorch and DeepSpeed configured for your devices.
2. Save the script below as `repro_zero3_duplicate_loading.py`.
3. Run on one node with two visible accelerator devices:

```bash
OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 torchrun --standalone --nproc_per_node=2 \
  repro_zero3_duplicate_loading.py ./zero3-repro-checkpoint
```

The checkpoint directory must be shared by the two local processes.

The script creates a tiny checkpoint with separate expert weights distributed across three safetensors files. It then calls `from_pretrained()` with ZeRO-3 enabled and counts checkpoint payload reads and weight-conversion calls on each rank.

The wrappers only count calls and delegate to the original functions without changing their behavior. Metadata-only reads with `map_location="meta"` are excluded.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction script</summary>

```python
import json
import os
import sys
from pathlib import Path
from unittest.mock import patch

import deepspeed
import torch
import torch.distributed as dist
from deepspeed.accelerator import get_accelerator
from safetensors.torch import save_file

from transformers import Qwen3MoeConfig, Qwen3MoeForCausalLM, modeling_utils
from transformers.integrations import deepspeed as ds_integration
from transformers.integrations.deepspeed import HfDeepSpeedConfig


def main():
    accelerator = get_accelerator()
    accelerator.set_device(int(os.environ["LOCAL_RANK"]))
    deepspeed.init_distributed(
        dist_backend=accelerator.communication_backend_name()
    )
    rank = dist.get_rank()
    checkpoint = Path(sys.argv[1])
    config = Qwen3MoeConfig(
        vocab_size=32,
        hidden_size=16,
        intermediate_size=32,
        moe_intermediate_size=8,
        num_hidden_layers=2,
        num_attention_heads=2,
        num_key_value_heads=2,
        num_experts=2,
        num_experts_per_tok=1,
    )
    if rank == 0:
        torch.manual_seed(42)
        reference = Qwen3MoeForCausalLM(config)
        source = {}
        # Store separate expert weights to exercise checkpoint-to-model fusion.
        for key, value in reference.state_dict().items():
            if key.endswith("experts.gate_up_proj"):
                prefix = key.removesuffix("gate_up_proj")
                for i, expert in enumerate(value):
                    gate, up = expert.chunk(2, dim=0)
                    source[f"{prefix}{i}.gate_proj.weight"] = gate.contiguous()
                    source[f"{prefix}{i}.up_proj.weight"] = up.contiguous()
            elif key.endswith("experts.down_proj"):
                prefix = key.removesuffix("down_proj")
                for i, expert in enumerate(value):
                    source[f"{prefix}{i}.down_proj.weight"] = expert.contiguous()
            else:
                source[key] = value.contiguous()
        checkpoint.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        config.save_pretrained(checkpoint)
        weight_map = {}
        for i in range(3):
            shard = dict(list(source.items())[i::3])
            filename = f"model-{i:05d}.safetensors"
            save_file(shard, checkpoint / filename, metadata={"format": "pt"})
            weight_map.update(dict.fromkeys(shard, filename))
        (checkpoint / "model.safetensors.index.json").write_text(
            json.dumps({"metadata": {}, "weight_map": weight_map})
        )
        del source, reference
    dist.barrier()

    # Keep this object alive so from_pretrained sees the ZeRO-3 configuration.
    ds_config = HfDeepSpeedConfig(
        {
            "train_batch_size": dist.get_world_size(),
            "zero_optimization": {"stage": 3},
        }
    )
    counts = {"payload_reads": 0, "conversions": 0}
    original_read = modeling_utils.load_state_dict
    original_convert = ds_integration._apply_weight_conversions_to_state_dict

    def read(*args, **kwargs):
        if kwargs.get("map_location", "cpu") != "meta":
            counts["payload_reads"] += 1
        return original_read(*args, **kwargs)

    def convert(*args, **kwargs):
        counts["conversions"] += 1
        return original_convert(*args, **kwargs)

    with (
        patch.object(modeling_utils, "load_state_dict", read),
        patch.object(
            ds_integration, "_apply_weight_conversions_to_state_dict", convert
        ),
    ):
        model = Qwen3MoeForCausalLM.from_pretrained(
            checkpoint,
            config=config,
            dtype=torch.float32,
            use_safetensors=True,
        )
    print(f"RESULT rank={rank} {json.dumps(counts)}", flush=True)
    dist.barrier()
    del model, ds_config
    dist.destroy_process_group()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

</details>

### Observed behavior

On the unmodified commit, both ranks read all three checkpoint files and perform the conversion:

```text
RESULT rank=0 {"payload_reads": 3, "conversions": 1}
RESULT rank=1 {"payload_reads": 3, "conversions": 1}
```

The small reproduction finishes successfully. It demonstrates redundant loading and conversion without requiring an out-of-memory failure.

These counters measure function calls, not physical disk traffic or an exact RSS multiplier. Memory mapping and the page cache can affect those measurements.

### Relevant code path

In the non-quantized ZeRO-3 branch of `_load_pretrained_model`, all ranks read the checkpoint files with `map_location="cpu"` and merge them into a state dict:

https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/e598fbad926d80bc356c0c4d96532030e3dfdb62/src/transformers/modeling_utils.py#L4422

Then `_load_state_dict_into_zero3_model` applies the weight conversions on every rank. Only the later parameter copy is restricted to rank 0 inside `GatheredParameters(..., modifier_rank=0)`:

https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/e598fbad926d80bc356c0c4d96532030e3dfdb62/src/transformers/integrations/deepspeed.py#L441

The checkpoint and conversion tensors are separate from the model parameters managed by ZeRO-3, so partitioning the model does not partition those temporary tensors.

### Expected behavior

Nonzero ranks should not need to read and convert a complete checkpoint to participate in ZeRO-3 parameter loading.

One possible approach is to let rank 0 read and convert the checkpoint, distribute the converted keys/shapes/dtypes to the other ranks, and retain the existing ZeRO-3 parameter synchronization. Replicated buffers would also need their checkpoint values distributed to all ranks.

I have a local patch following this approach. With the same reproduction, rank 0 reports three payload reads and one conversion, while rank 1 reports zero for both. Separate two-device regression tests also checked the loaded parameters and persistent buffers against reference values.

### Reproduction

Assigning the v4-style `rope_scaling` alias to an initialized config replaces `rope_parameters`, dropping the existing `rope_theta` and other base parameters ([setter](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/ea9259355388f518240f96a8c2dee7311b1c5911/src/transformers/configuration_utils.py#L714-L716)).
The CPU-only example below starts with a base of 500000 and raises `KeyError: 'rope_type'` after the assignment; using the canonical `rope_type` key also loses the base.

```python
from transformers import LlamaConfig
from transformers.models.llama.modeling_llama import LlamaRotaryEmbedding

config = LlamaConfig(rope_theta=500000.0)
config.rope_scaling = {"type": "linear", "factor": 2.0}
print(config.rope_parameters)
LlamaRotaryEmbedding(config)
```

Output from the unmodified revision:

```text
{'type': 'linear', 'factor': 2.0}
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "report-repro.py", line 28, in <module>
    LlamaRotaryEmbedding(config)
  File "src/transformers/models/llama/modeling_llama.py", line 80, in __init__
    self.rope_type = self.config.rope_parameters["rope_type"]
                     ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~^^^^^^^^^^^^^
KeyError: 'rope_type'
```

Saving and reloading that assigned config restores the constructor default base of 10000 instead of the original 500000.
This also affects real downstream overrides: [sgl-project/sglang#41227](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/41227) reports a 500000 → 10000 fallback and a GSM8K result change from 161 to 106 on the first 200 examples; the [review of sgl-project/sglang#43067](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/43067#pullrequestreview-5488908845) confirms that the affected override is used in documented long-context recipes.

### Expected behavior

The setter should normalize legacy parameter names and preserve existing base parameters unless the assignment explicitly overrides them.
PR #49515 provides a fix: ten new regressions fail on the unmodified revision, all 45 RoPE tests pass with the fix, and the current PR CI has no failed checks.

### System Info

- transformers 5.18.0 (the same `_tied_weights_keys` in 5.19.0 and on main)
- torch 2.14.1+cu130, Python 3.10.12, Ubuntu 22.04

### Who can help?

@molbap @guarin @CyrilVallez

### Information

- [ ] The official example scripts
- [x] My own modified scripts

### Tasks

- [ ] An officially supported task in the `examples` folder (such as GLUE/SQuAD, ...)
- [x] My own task or dataset (give details below)

### Reproduction

`MMGroundingDinoForObjectDetection._tied_weights_keys` ties every decoder layer's box head and class head to layer 0:

```python
_tied_weights_keys = {
    r"bbox_embed.(?![0])\d+": r"bbox_embed.0",
    r"class_embed.(?![0])\d+": r"^class_embed.0",
    "model.decoder.bbox_embed": "bbox_embed",
    "model.decoder.class_embed": "class_embed",
}
```

`GroundingDinoForObjectDetection.__init__` drops the box-head entry when `config.decoder_bbox_embed_share` is False. The MM Grounding DINO class does not look at the config.

The checkpoints I checked all set `decoder_bbox_embed_share: false` and `decoder_cls_embed_share: false` (iSEE-Laboratory/llmdet_tiny, llmdet_base, llmdet_large; openmmlab-community/mm_grounding_dino_tiny_o365v1_goldg_v3det and mm_grounding_dino_tiny_o365v1_goldg_grit_v3det) and store a separate head for each decoder layer (`model.decoder.bbox_embed.{1..5}.*`, `model.decoder.class_embed.{1..5}.bias`). These heads really differ: in llmdet_large the first linear layer of heads 1 to 5 differs from head 0 by 1.1 to 1.4 times the norm of head 0, and the class biases run from -4.64 (layer 0) to -4.73. After loading, layers 1 to 5 use head 0, and the boxes come out wrong.

The comment in `__init__` says "class embed has no weights so nothing to tie", but `MMGroundingDinoContrastiveEmbedding` has a learnable `bias`.

In v4.57.1 `_tied_weights_keys` was a list and every layer kept its own head, so this seems to have come with the v5 weight-tying change.

The model card example of LLMDet tiny, once as loaded and once with each layer's heads put back from the checkpoint:

```python
from urllib.request import urlopen

import torch
from huggingface_hub import hf_hub_download
from PIL import Image
from safetensors.torch import load_file
from transformers import AutoModelForZeroShotObjectDetection, AutoProcessor

model_id = "iSEE-Laboratory/llmdet_tiny"
processor = AutoProcessor.from_pretrained(model_id)
model = AutoModelForZeroShotObjectDetection.from_pretrained(model_id).eval()

image = Image.open(urlopen("http://images.cocodataset.org/val2017/000000039769.jpg"))
text_labels = [["a cat", "a remote control"]]


def detect():
    inputs = processor(images=image, text=text_labels, return_tensors="pt")
    with torch.no_grad():
        outputs = model(**inputs)
    result = processor.post_process_grounded_object_detection(
        outputs, threshold=0.4, target_sizes=[(image.height, image.width)])[0]
    for box, score, label in zip(result["boxes"], result["scores"], result["text_labels"]):
        print(f"  {label}: {score.item():.2f} {[round(v, 1) for v in box.tolist()]}")


print("config decoder_bbox_embed_share:", model.config.decoder_bbox_embed_share)
print("bbox_embed[1] is bbox_embed[0]:", model.bbox_embed[1].layers[0].weight is model.bbox_embed[0].layers[0].weight)
print("as loaded:")
detect()

# Put each decoder layer's own heads back from the checkpoint.
weights = load_file(hf_hub_download(model_id, "model.safetensors"))
for i in range(1, model.config.decoder_layers):
    model.bbox_embed[i] = type(model.bbox_embed[0])(model.config.d_model, model.config.d_model, 4, 3)
    model.bbox_embed[i].load_state_dict({k.split(f"bbox_embed.{i}.")[1]: v for k, v in weights.items()
                                         if k.startswith(f"model.decoder.bbox_embed.{i}.")})
    model.class_embed[i] = type(model.class_embed[0])(model.config)
    model.class_embed[i].bias.data = weights[f"model.decoder.class_embed.{i}.bias"].clone()
model.model.decoder.bbox_embed = model.bbox_embed
model.model.decoder.class_embed = model.class_embed
print("with each layer's own heads:")
detect()
```

Output (CPU, fp32):

```
config decoder_bbox_embed_share: False
bbox_embed[1] is bbox_embed[0]: True
as loaded:
  a cat: 0.49 [345.4, -41.4, 472.2, 366.7]
  a cat: 0.44 [69.9, 59.5, 140.3, 521.9]
  a remote control: 0.51 [14.4, 88.4, 72.1, 139.1]
with each layer's own heads:
  a cat: 0.53 [342.1, 22.9, 637.3, 374.5]
  a cat: 0.47 [10.5, 51.4, 317.6, 471.5]
  a remote control: 0.59 [38.3, 70.5, 176.9, 118.2]
```

As loaded, the first cat's box starts 41 px above the image and stops at x = 472, though that cat reaches the right edge of the 640 px image; the second ends at y = 522 on a 480 px image. With the heads put back, the boxes fit both cats and the remote.

### Expected behavior

The heads are tied only when the config says they are shared (`decoder_bbox_embed_share`, `decoder_cls_embed_share`), as `GroundingDinoForObjectDetection` already does for the box head, so LLMDet and MM Grounding DINO checkpoints load each decoder layer's own heads.
