### Reproduction

`MMGroundingDinoForObjectDetection._tied_weights_keys` ties every decoder layer's box head and class head to layer 0:

```python
_tied_weights_keys = {
    r"bbox_embed.(?![0])\d+": r"bbox_embed.0",
    r"class_embed.(?![0])\d+": r"^class_embed.0",
    "model.decoder.bbox_embed": "bbox_embed",
    "model.decoder.class_embed": "class_embed",
}
```

`GroundingDinoForObjectDetection.__init__` drops the box-head entry when `config.decoder_bbox_embed_share` is False. The MM Grounding DINO class does not look at the config.

The checkpoints I checked all set `decoder_bbox_embed_share: false` and `decoder_cls_embed_share: false` (iSEE-Laboratory/llmdet_tiny, llmdet_base, llmdet_large; openmmlab-community/mm_grounding_dino_tiny_o365v1_goldg_v3det and mm_grounding_dino_tiny_o365v1_goldg_grit_v3det) and store a separate head for each decoder layer (`model.decoder.bbox_embed.{1..5}.*`, `model.decoder.class_embed.{1..5}.bias`). These heads really differ: in llmdet_large the first linear layer of heads 1 to 5 differs from head 0 by 1.1 to 1.4 times the norm of head 0, and the class biases run from -4.64 (layer 0) to -4.73. After loading, layers 1 to 5 use head 0, and the boxes come out wrong.

The comment in `__init__` says "class embed has no weights so nothing to tie", but `MMGroundingDinoContrastiveEmbedding` has a learnable `bias`.

In v4.57.1 `_tied_weights_keys` was a list and every layer kept its own head, so this seems to have come with the v5 weight-tying change.

The model card example of LLMDet tiny, once as loaded and once with each layer's heads put back from the checkpoint:

```python
from urllib.request import urlopen

import torch
from huggingface_hub import hf_hub_download
from PIL import Image
from safetensors.torch import load_file
from transformers import AutoModelForZeroShotObjectDetection, AutoProcessor

model_id = "iSEE-Laboratory/llmdet_tiny"
processor = AutoProcessor.from_pretrained(model_id)
model = AutoModelForZeroShotObjectDetection.from_pretrained(model_id).eval()

image = Image.open(urlopen("http://images.cocodataset.org/val2017/000000039769.jpg"))
text_labels = [["a cat", "a remote control"]]


def detect():
    inputs = processor(images=image, text=text_labels, return_tensors="pt")
    with torch.no_grad():
        outputs = model(**inputs)
    result = processor.post_process_grounded_object_detection(
        outputs, threshold=0.4, target_sizes=[(image.height, image.width)])[0]
    for box, score, label in zip(result["boxes"], result["scores"], result["text_labels"]):
        print(f"  {label}: {score.item():.2f} {[round(v, 1) for v in box.tolist()]}")


print("config decoder_bbox_embed_share:", model.config.decoder_bbox_embed_share)
print("bbox_embed[1] is bbox_embed[0]:", model.bbox_embed[1].layers[0].weight is model.bbox_embed[0].layers[0].weight)
print("as loaded:")
detect()

# Put each decoder layer's own heads back from the checkpoint.
weights = load_file(hf_hub_download(model_id, "model.safetensors"))
for i in range(1, model.config.decoder_layers):
    model.bbox_embed[i] = type(model.bbox_embed[0])(model.config.d_model, model.config.d_model, 4, 3)
    model.bbox_embed[i].load_state_dict({k.split(f"bbox_embed.{i}.")[1]: v for k, v in weights.items()
                                         if k.startswith(f"model.decoder.bbox_embed.{i}.")})
    model.class_embed[i] = type(model.class_embed[0])(model.config)
    model.class_embed[i].bias.data = weights[f"model.decoder.class_embed.{i}.bias"].clone()
model.model.decoder.bbox_embed = model.bbox_embed
model.model.decoder.class_embed = model.class_embed
print("with each layer's own heads:")
detect()
```
```

bbox_embed[1] is bbox_embed[0]: True
as loaded:

  a cat: 0.44 [69.9, 59.5, 140.3, 521.9]
  a remote control: 0.51 [14.4, 88.4, 72.1, 139.1]
with each layer's own heads:
  a cat: 0.53 [342.1, 22.9, 637.3, 374.5]
  a cat: 0.47 [10.5, 51.4, 317.6, 471.5]
  a remote control: 0.59 [38.3, 70.5, 176.9, 118.2]
```

As loaded, the first cat's box starts 41 px above the image and stops at x = 472, though that cat reaches the right edge of the 640 px image; the second ends at y = 522 on a 480 px image. With the heads put back, the boxes fit both cats and the remote.

### Expected behavior

The heads are tied only when the config says they are shared (`decoder_bbox_embed_share`, `decoder_cls_embed_share`), as `GroundingDinoForObjectDetection` already does for the box head, so LLMDet and MM Grounding DINO checkpoints load each decoder layer's own heads.

### Reproduction

Hi, I found that Mamba2's non-fused gated RMSNorm normalizes the entire intermediate dimension, while the upstream fused training path normalizes each SSM group separately. With `n_groups > 1`, these are different functions, with different outputs and gradients even in FP32.

This is independent of the time-step-limit issue in #49465. Both sides below use the same gate-before-norm order (`norm_before_gate=False`) to isolate grouping.

**I would like to contribute this fix myself as my first code contribution to Transformers.** I am reporting the reproduction and proposed approach first and would appreciate maintainer feedback before opening a focused PR. I plan to work on this; please coordinate here before opening a parallel PR.

Source checked: Transformers `d03beeda40302d507c0106371ac469b5d55adcb1`, with upstream Mamba references pinned to `e9594ce1c732d97440f0332fdc43170a2294dbfa`.

The relevant paths are:

| Path | Normalization scope |
|---|---|
| Transformers `MambaRMSNormGated.forward()` | Whole last dimension: `hidden_states.pow(2).mean(-1, keepdim=True)` |
| Upstream fused training kernel called with `ngroups=self.n_groups` | `group_size=dim // ngroups` |
| Upstream Mamba2 non-fused model | `group_size=self.d_ssm // ngroups` |

Source links:

- [Transformers gated RMSNorm](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/d03beeda40302d507c0106371ac469b5d55adcb1/src/transformers/models/mamba2/modeling_mamba2.py#L105): no grouping parameter or grouped reduction.
- [Mixer construction](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/d03beeda40302d507c0106371ac469b5d55adcb1/src/transformers/models/mamba2/modeling_mamba2.py#L427): `self.n_groups` is not passed to the norm.
- [Fused training call](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/d03beeda40302d507c0106371ac469b5d55adcb1/src/transformers/models/mamba2/modeling_mamba2.py#L470): passes `ngroups=self.n_groups` and `norm_before_gate=False`.
- [Upstream fused normalization](https://github.com/state-spaces/mamba/blob/e9594ce1c732d97440f0332fdc43170a2294dbfa/mamba_ssm/ops/triton/ssd_combined.py#L872) and [upstream ordinary norm construction](https://github.com/state-spaces/mamba/blob/e9594ce1c732d97440f0332fdc43170a2294dbfa/mamba_ssm/modules/mamba2.py#L142) both explicitly use group size.

Minimal reproduction, using the official `rms_norm_ref` rather than a handwritten replacement (requires Transformers and mamba-ssm; this calculation runs on CPU):

```python
import torch
from transformers.models.mamba2.modeling_mamba2 import MambaRMSNormGated
from mamba_ssm.ops.triton.layernorm_gated import rms_norm_ref

x = torch.arange(1.0, 9.0).repeat_interleave(2).view(1, 16).requires_grad_()
gate = torch.ones_like(x)
norm = MambaRMSNormGated(16, eps=1e-5)

actual = norm(x, gate)
reference = rms_norm_ref(
    x, norm.weight, None, z=gate, eps=1e-5,
    group_size=2, norm_before_gate=False,
)

dx_actual = torch.autograd.grad(actual[0, 0], x)[0]
dx_reference = torch.autograd.grad(reference[0, 0], x)[0]
print("first output:", actual[0, 0].item(), reference[0, 0].item())
print("max output difference:", (actual - reference).abs().max().item())
print("cross-group derivative:", dx_actual[0, 2].item(), dx_reference[0, 2].item())
```

Observed output:

```text
first output: 0.19802942872047424 0.9999906420707703
max output difference: 0.8019611835479736
cross-group derivative: -0.0009707316639833152 0.0
```

The last check isolates the structural difference: output channel 0 belongs to the first group, so its derivative with respect to input channel 2, in the next group, should be zero for grouped RMSNorm.

Additional local checks:

- For ordinary random FP32 inputs and gates of shape `[2, 16, 8192]`, 8 groups and seed 7 on CPU, the current norm differs from the official grouped reference by **2.48113632** in maximum absolute output error.
- Both the small example and the 8192-wide example were checked on CPU and CUDA, with single-group controls. The official CUDA `rmsnorm_fn` forward/backward was also executed directly from the pinned upstream `layernorm_gated.py`: across these CUDA checks, its maximum absolute difference from the official PyTorch reference was about **2.86e-6** for outputs and **5.72e-6** for input, gate and norm-weight gradients.
- `Mamba2Config.n_groups` defaults to 8, so the affected grouping is not an invalid architecture. The public [Mamba-Codestral configuration](https://huggingface.co/mistralai/Mamba-Codestral-7B-v0.1/blob/main/config.json) also has width 8192 and 8 groups. This only establishes that those dimensions are used publicly: that checkpoint additionally specifies `norm_before_gate=true`, which is a separate alignment question and is not covered by this gate-before-norm reproducer.

Validation scope: the normalization mismatch was executed and checked numerically. The fused-training versus ordinary-forward discrepancy is additionally established by the call sites above. I have **not** run a full pretrained model, the complete fused convolution/SSM training operation, or a generation-quality evaluation, and am not claiming a measured task-quality regression.

### Expected behavior

For the same grouping, gate order, inputs and weights, ordinary forward/cached decoding and fused training should use the same RMSNorm definition and agree within numerical tolerance.

The proposed fix is to give `MambaRMSNormGated` a group-size or group-count parameter, pass the mixer's actual grouping, and reduce over each group's channels. The one-dimensional norm weight and checkpoint keys/shapes can remain unchanged. The existing gate order, epsilon, dtype behavior and single-group behavior should be preserved and tested separately. Replacing RMSNorm with mean-subtracting GroupNorm, or changing `n_groups` to 1, would not implement the same model.

### Suggested minimal patch

Latest `main` rechecked: `d03beeda40302d507c0106371ac469b5d55adcb1`; the grouping omission is still present. This follows the grouped-reduction approach already used by [Zamba2RMSNormGated](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/d03beeda40302d507c0106371ac469b5d55adcb1/src/transformers/models/zamba2/modeling_zamba2.py#L50), retaining Mamba2's existing gate order, dtype handling and weight layout.

```diff
--- a/src/transformers/models/mamba2/modeling_mamba2.py
+++ b/src/transformers/models/mamba2/modeling_mamba2.py
@@ -103,10 +103,11 @@
 
 
 class MambaRMSNormGated(torch.nn.Module):
-    def __init__(self, hidden_size, eps=1e-6):
+    def __init__(self, hidden_size, eps=1e-6, group_size=None):
         super().__init__()
         self.weight = nn.Parameter(torch.ones(hidden_size))
         self.variance_epsilon = eps
+        self.group_size = hidden_size if group_size is None else group_size
 
     def forward(self, hidden_states, gate=None):
         input_dtype = hidden_states.dtype
@@ -114,8 +115,11 @@
 
         if gate is not None:
             hidden_states = hidden_states * nn.functional.silu(gate.to(torch.float32))
+        input_shape = hidden_states.shape
+        hidden_states = hidden_states.reshape(*input_shape[:-1], -1, self.group_size)
         variance = hidden_states.pow(2).mean(-1, keepdim=True)
         hidden_states = hidden_states * torch.rsqrt(variance + self.variance_epsilon)
+        hidden_states = hidden_states.reshape(input_shape)
 
         return self.weight * hidden_states.to(input_dtype)
 
@@ -424,7 +428,11 @@
         # S4D real initialization. These are not discretized!
         # The core is to load them, compute the discrete states, then write the updated state. Keeps the memory bounded
         self.A_log = nn.Parameter(torch.empty(self.num_heads))
-        self.norm = MambaRMSNormGated(self.intermediate_size, eps=self.layer_norm_epsilon)
+        self.norm = MambaRMSNormGated(
+            self.intermediate_size,
+            eps=self.layer_norm_epsilon,
+            group_size=self.intermediate_size // self.n_groups,
+        )
         self.D = nn.Parameter(torch.empty(self.num_heads))
         if initialize_mixer_weights and self.dt_bias.device.type != "meta":
             self.init_mamba2_weights()
```

Local validation of this proposed patch:

- **24 FP32 reference comparisons passed**: CPU/CUDA, 1/2/4/8 groups, three seeds, non-contiguous inputs of shape `[16, 2, 8192]`; outputs and input/gate/norm-weight gradients compared with the pinned official `rms_norm_ref`. Maximum absolute errors: **2.86e-6** for outputs and **7.63e-6** for gradients.
- **12 single-group compatibility checks passed**: CPU/CUDA × FP32/FP16/BF16 × with/without a gate. Outputs and gradients are elementwise identical to the original implementation, and the original state dict loads strictly.
- Validation above is for the proposed normalization change. Full-model and complete fused-SSM integration checks are still needed before a PR.

Could a maintainer confirm this grouping alignment approach before I prepare the PR?

### System Info

- Transformers source checked: `d03beeda40302d507c0106371ac469b5d55adcb1`; installed version used for the copy-paste reproducer: **5.5.0**. The inspected norm class has the same implementation.
- Upstream Mamba source checked for the reference/kernel comparison: `e9594ce1c732d97440f0332fdc43170a2294dbfa`; installed mamba-ssm for the copy-paste reproducer: **2.3.2.post1**.
- Python **3.12.13**, PyTorch **2.12.1+cu130**, CUDA **13.0**.
- Linux **7.0.0-38-generic**, x86_64, glibc **2.43**.
- NVIDIA **RTX A1000 Laptop GPU**, with CPU checks as described above.

{"repository": "huggingface/transformers", "task_candidate_id": 8926, "repository_id": 129, "issue_number": 49536, "github_issue_id": 5816950895, "html_url": "https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/issues/49536", "created_at": "2026-10-12T16:18:02+00:00", "author_association": null, "title": "Mamba2: non-fused gated RMSNorm ignores n_groups and disagrees with fused training", "body_text": "### Reproduction

Hi, I found that Mamba2's non-fused gated RMSNorm normalizes the entire intermediate dimension, while the upstream fused training path normalizes each SSM group separately. With `n_groups > 1`, these are different functions, with different outputs and gradients even in FP32.

This is independent of the time-step-limit issue in #49465. Both sides below use the same gate-before-norm order (`norm_before_gate=False`) to isolate grouping.

**I would like to contribute this fix myself as my first code contribution to Transformers.** I am reporting the reproduction and proposed approach first and would appreciate maintainer feedback before opening a focused PR. I plan to work on this; please coordinate here before opening a parallel PR.

Source checked: Transformers `d03beeda40302d507c0106371ac469b5d55adcb1`, with upstream Mamba references pinned to `e9594ce1c732d97440f0332fdc43170a2294dbfa`.

The relevant paths are:

| Path | Normalization scope |
|---|---|
| Transformers `MambaRMSNormGated.forward()` | Whole last dimension: `hidden_states.pow(2).mean(-1, keepdim=True)` |
| Upstream fused training kernel called with `ngroups=self.n_groups` | `group_size=dim // ngroups` |
| Upstream Mamba2 non-fused model | `group_size=self.d_ssm // ngroups` |

Source links:

- [Transformers gated RMSNorm](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/d03beeda40302d507c0106371ac469b5d55adcb1/src/transformers/models/mamba2/modeling_mamba2.py#L105): no grouping parameter or grouped reduction.
- [Mixer construction](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/d03beeda40302d507c0106371ac469b5d55adcb1/src/transformers/models/mamba2/modeling_mamba2.py#L427): `self.n_groups` is not passed to the norm.
- [Fused training call](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/d03beeda40302d507c0106371ac469b5d55adcb1/src/transformers/models/mamba2/modeling_mamba2.py#L470): passes `ngroups=self.n_groups` and `norm_before_gate=False`.
- [Upstream fused normalization](https://github.com/state-spaces/mamba/blob/e9594ce1c732d97440f0332fdc43170a2294dbfa/mamba_ssm/ops/triton/ssd_combined.py#L872) and [upstream ordinary norm construction](https://github.com/state-spaces/mamba/blob/e9594ce1c732d97440f0332fdc43170a2294dbfa/mamba_ssm/modules/mamba2.py#L142) both explicitly use group size.

Minimal reproduction, using the official `rms_norm_ref` rather than a handwritten replacement (requires Transformers and mamba-ssm; this calculation runs on CPU):

```python
import torch
from transformers.models.mamba2.modeling_mamba2 import MambaRMSNormGated
from mamba_ssm.ops.triton.layernorm_gated import rms_norm_ref

x = torch.arange(1.0, 9.0).repeat_interleave(2).view(1, 16).requires_grad_()
gate = torch.ones_like(x)
norm = MambaRMSNormGated(16, eps=1e-5)

actual = norm(x, gate)
reference = rms_norm_ref(
    x, norm.weight, None, z=gate, eps=1e-5,
    group_size=2, norm_before_gate=False,
)

dx_actual = torch.autograd.grad(actual[0, 0], x)[0]
dx_reference = torch.autograd.grad(reference[0, 0], x)[0]
print("first output:", actual[0, 0].item(), reference[0, 0].item())
print("max output difference:", (actual - reference).abs().max().item())
print("cross-group derivative:", dx_actual[0, 2].item(), dx_reference[0, 2].item())
```

Observed output:

```text
first output: 0.19802942872047424 0.9999906420707703
max output difference: 0.8019611835479736
cross-group derivative: -0.0009707316639833152 0.0
```

The last check isolates the structural difference: output channel 0 belongs to the first group, so its derivative with respect to input channel 2, in the next group, should be zero for grouped RMSNorm.

Additional local checks:

- For ordinary random FP32 inputs and gates of shape `[2, 16, 8192]`, 8 groups and seed 7 on CPU, the current norm differs from the official grouped reference by **2.48113632** in maximum absolute output error.
- Both the small example and the 8192-wide example were checked on CPU and CUDA, with single-group controls. The official CUDA `rmsnorm_fn` forward/backward was also executed directly from the pinned upstream `layernorm_gated.py`: across these CUDA checks, its maximum absolute difference from the official PyTorch reference was about **2.86e-6** for outputs and **5.72e-6** for input, gate and norm-weight gradients.
- `Mamba2Config.n_groups` defaults to 8, so the affected grouping is not an invalid architecture. The public [Mamba-Codestral configuration](https://huggingface.co/mistralai/Mamba-Codestral-7B-v0.1/blob/main/config.json) also has width 8192 and 8 groups. This only establishes that those dimensions are used publicly: that checkpoint additionally specifies `norm_before_gate=true`, which is a separate alignment question and is not covered by this gate-before-norm reproducer.

Validation scope: the normalization mismatch was executed and checked numerically. The fused-training versus ordinary-forward discrepancy is additionally established by the call sites above. I have **not** run a full pretrained model, the complete fused convolution/SSM training operation, or a generation-quality evaluation, and am not claiming a measured task-quality regression.

### Expected behavior

For the same grouping, gate order, inputs and weights, ordinary forward/cached decoding and fused training should use the same RMSNorm definition and agree within numerical tolerance.

The proposed fix is to give `MambaRMSNormGated` a group-size or group-count parameter, pass the mixer's actual grouping, and reduce over each group's channels. The one-dimensional norm weight and checkpoint keys/shapes can remain unchanged. The existing gate order, epsilon, dtype behavior and single-group behavior should be preserved and tested separately. Replacing RMSNorm with mean-subtracting GroupNorm, or changing `n_groups` to 1, would not implement the same model.

### Suggested minimal patch

Latest `main` rechecked: `d03beeda40302d507c0106371ac469b5d55adcb1`; the grouping omission is still present. This follows the grouped-reduction approach already used by [Zamba2RMSNormGated](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/d03beeda40302d507c0106371ac469b5d55adcb1/src/transformers/models/zamba2/modeling_zamba2.py#L50), retaining Mamba2's existing gate order, dtype handling and weight layout.

```diff
--- a/src/transformers/models/mamba2/modeling_mamba2.py
+++ b/src/transformers/models/mamba2/modeling_mamba2.py
@@ -103,10 +103,11 @@
 
 
 class MambaRMSNormGated(torch.nn.Module):
-    def __init__(self, hidden_size, eps=1e-6):
+    def __init__(self, hidden_size, eps=1e-6, group_size=None):
         super().__init__()
         self.weight = nn.Parameter(torch.ones(hidden_size))
         self.variance_epsilon = eps
+        self.group_size = hidden_size if group_size is None else group_size
 
     def forward(self, hidden_states, gate=None):
         input_dtype = hidden_states.dtype
@@ -114,8 +115,11 @@
 
         if gate is not None:
             hidden_states = hidden_states * nn.functional.silu(gate.to(torch.float32))
+        input_shape = hidden_states.shape
+        hidden_states = hidden_states.reshape(*input_shape[:-1], -1, self.group_size)
         variance = hidden_states.pow(2).mean(-1, keepdim=True)
         hidden_states = hidden_states * torch.rsqrt(variance + self.variance_epsilon)
+        hidden_states = hidden_states.reshape(input_shape)
 
         return self.weight * hidden_states.to(input_dtype)
 
@@ -424,7 +428,11 @@
         # S4D real initialization. These are not discretized!
         # The core is to load them, compute the discrete states, then write the updated state. Keeps the memory bounded
         self.A_log = nn.Parameter(torch.empty(self.num_heads))
-        self.norm = MambaRMSNormGated(self.intermediate_size, eps=self.layer_norm_epsilon)
+        self.norm = MambaRMSNormGated(
+            self.intermediate_size,
+            eps=self.layer_norm_epsilon,
+            group_size=self.intermediate_size // self.n_groups,
+        )
         self.D = nn.Parameter(torch.empty(self.num_heads))
         if initialize_mixer_weights and self.dt_bias.device.type != "meta":
             self.init_mamba2_weights()
```

- **12 single-group compatibility checks passed**: CPU/CUDA × FP32/FP16/BF16 × with/without a gate. Outputs and gradients are elementwise identical to the original implementation, and the original state dict loads strictly.
- Validation above is for the proposed normalization change. Full-model and complete fused-SSM integration checks are still needed before a PR.

Could a maintainer confirm this grouping alignment approach before I prepare the PR?

body_text:
### Feature request

On CPU, `use_gqa_in_sdpa` only returns True when `attention_mask is None`, so any masked call (padded batches, most `generate` calls) goes through `repeat_kv` and copies K/V up to full head count. Since torch 2.9 the CPU flash kernel takes `enable_gqa=True` with a mask, so for inference that copy can go: CPU + torch >= 2.9, no grad on K/V, not compiling/tracing, equal K/V head dims. Everything else keeps the current path.

### Motivation

Llama with SmolLM2-135M shapes (9 q / 3 kv heads), bf16, batch 2, 2048-token left-padded prefix, 4 CPU threads, torch 2.14.1: median decode step 71.5 -> 59.3 ms (1.21x, every round faster). A second machine gave 1.06x. Logits and greedy tokens are identical. Existing Llama/Qwen3 sdpa, cache, generate and training tests pass.

### Your contribution

Patch is ready (about 12 lines in `use_gqa_in_sdpa` plus a test): https://github.com/ToukoUrsin/transformers/tree/cpu-native-gqa-sdpa. It's CPU-only, so it doesn't overlap #45776 / #49521 (CUDA) or the `force_gqa` flag in #49459. Want a PR?

AI-assisted; I reviewed and tested it.

### System Info

- `transformers` version: 5.19.0.dev0 (main @ 22cfdfa)
- Platform: Linux-6.8.0-138-generic-x86_64-with-glibc2.35
- Python version: 3.12.12

- Accelerate version: 1.15.0
- PyTorch version (accelerator?): 2.14.1+cu130 (CUDA)
- GPU type: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090

### Who can help?

@SunMarc

### Information

- [ ] The official example scripts
- [x] My own modified scripts

### Tasks

- [ ] An officially supported task in the `examples` folder (such as GLUE/SQuAD, ...)
- [x] My own task or dataset (give details below)

### Reproduction

Was trying `/v1/systemone` (#49322) with Qwen3.5 and a few Qwen3.5-based decision models and hit two 500s. Server is just `transformers serve`.

**1. `chat_template_kwargs` with a key the handler already passes → 500**

```shell
curl localhost:8000/v1/systemone -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{
  "model": "Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B",
  "state": "I was charged twice.",
  "chat_template_kwargs": {"tokenize": true},
  "questions": {"refund": {"type": "noul"}}
}'
# Internal Server Error
# TypeError: transformers.processing_utils.ProcessorMixin.apply_chat_template() got multiple values for keyword argument 'tokenize'
```

Same with `add_generation_prompt`, and both keys do the same on `/v1/chat/completions`, which merges `chat_template_kwargs` the same way. Without `chat_template_kwargs` the request returns 200.

**2. Model without a chat template → 500**

`Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B-Base` has no chat template, and neither does the decision fine-tune `shgao/rsi-jev-v6.1-vl-4b` (its processor raises the same error):

```shell
curl localhost:8000/v1/systemone -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{
  "model": "Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B-Base",
  "state": "I was charged twice.",
  "questions": {"refund": {"type": "noul", "instructions": "Is a refund requested?"}}
}'
# Internal Server Error
# ValueError: Cannot use apply_chat_template because this processor does not have a chat template.
```

The same model works once a template is supplied through `--decision-config` (`{"chat_template": "<|im_start|>user\n{{ messages[0]['content'] }}<|im_end|>\n<|im_start|>assistant\n"}` returns 200), so it's only the error that's the problem.

### Expected behavior

1. Keys the handler sets itself (`tokenize`, `add_generation_prompt`, ...) in `chat_template_kwargs` get a 400 or are dropped with a warning, on all endpoints.
2. A 400 saying the model has no chat template and pointing to `chat_template` in `--decision-config`.

Happy to send a PR for both. I'd wait for #49534 to land first since it changes the same `_prepare_inputs` code.

### System Info

Since 5.18, `tencent/WeMM-Embedding-2B` loads as `Qwen3_5Tokenizer` instead of the generic fast tokenizer. The new class ignores the normalizer in the model's `tokenizer.json`. That normalizer removes a trailing newline, so now every input keeps an extra newline token at the end.

To reproduce:

```python
from transformers import AutoTokenizer
tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("tencent/WeMM-Embedding-2B")
print(tok("<|im_start|>user\nhello<|im_end|>\n", add_special_tokens=False).input_ids)
```

On 5.17: `[248045, 846, 198, 14556, 248046]`
On 5.19: `[248045, 846, 198, 14556, 248046, 198]`

This is an embedding model that reads the last token, so the extra token changes every embedding. I'd expect the normalizer from `tokenizer.json` to be kept.

### System Info
- `transformers` version: 5.19.0 (same code on main @5602e09)
- Platform: macOS-26.6.2-arm64-arm-64bit
- Python version: 3.12.13
- Huggingface_hub version: 2.2.0
- Safetensors version: 0.8.0
- PyTorch version (accelerator?): 2.14.1 (NA)
- Using distributed or parallel set-up in script?: No

### Who can help?
@yonigozlan (SAM 3 port), @molbap @guarin

### Description
For text-only prompts, `Sam3Model` skips the geometry encoder, so the DETR encoder and decoder only see the text tokens. Meta's reference implementation always runs the geometry encoder, also for text-only prompts, and appends its learned CLS token to the text tokens. From the public code, the checkpoint was trained with that token always present.

### Reproduction
```python
import requests
import torch
from PIL import Image
from transformers import Sam3Model, Sam3Processor

model = Sam3Model.from_pretrained("facebook/sam3").eval()
processor = Sam3Processor.from_pretrained("facebook/sam3")
url = "http://images.cocodataset.org/val2017/000000077595.jpg"
image = Image.open(requests.get(url, stream=True).raw).convert("RGB")

calls, prompt_len = [], []
model.geometry_encoder.register_forward_hook(lambda module, args, output: calls.append(1))
model.detr_encoder.register_forward_pre_hook(
    lambda module, args, kwargs: prompt_len.append(kwargs["text_features"].shape[1]), with_kwargs=True
)

def run(**prompt):
    calls.clear()
    prompt_len.clear()
    with torch.no_grad():
        model(**processor(images=image, return_tensors="pt", **prompt))
    return len(calls), prompt_len[0]

print("text only : geometry encoder calls = %d, prompt tokens = %d" % run(text="ear"))
print("text + box: geometry encoder calls = %d, prompt tokens = %d" % run(
    text="ear", input_boxes=[[[100.0, 100.0, 300.0, 300.0]]], input_boxes_labels=[[1]]))
```
Output:
```
text only : geometry encoder calls = 0, prompt tokens = 32
text + box: geometry encoder calls = 1, prompt tokens = 34
```

### Expected behavior
As in Meta's implementation, the geometry encoder also runs for text-only prompts, so the DETR encoder receives the text tokens plus the CLS token (33 instead of 32 above).

### References
**Meta (facebookresearch/sam3 @0570b3a)**
- Text-only prompts get an empty dummy geometric prompt: [sam3_image_processor.py#L124](https://github.com/facebookresearch/sam3/blob/0570b3a5be9c4e694f23d85232fb55f4a6f1f7fc/sam3/model/sam3_image_processor.py#L124)
- `_encode_prompt` always calls the geometry encoder, and the training forward uses the same path: [sam3_image.py#L190](https://github.com/facebookresearch/sam3/blob/0570b3a5be9c4e694f23d85232fb55f4a6f1f7fc/sam3/model/sam3_image.py#L190), [forward](https://github.com/facebookresearch/sam3/blob/0570b3a5be9c4e694f23d85232fb55f4a6f1f7fc/sam3/model/sam3_image.py#L557)
- The encoder appends the CLS whenever `cls_embed` exists: [geometry_encoders.py#L821-L829](https://github.com/facebookresearch/sam3/blob/0570b3a5be9c4e694f23d85232fb55f4a6f1f7fc/sam3/model/geometry_encoders.py#L821-L829). The released model is built with [`add_cls=True`](https://github.com/facebookresearch/sam3/blob/0570b3a5be9c4e694f23d85232fb55f4a6f1f7fc/sam3/model_builder.py#L296), the text-only training config sets [`add_cls: true`](https://github.com/facebookresearch/sam3/blob/0570b3a5be9c4e694f23d85232fb55f4a6f1f7fc/sam3/train/configs/odinw13/odinw_text_only_train.yaml#L152), and the encoder asserts *"It's currently highly recommended to add a CLS when using a transformer"* ([L576-L578](https://github.com/facebookresearch/sam3/blob/0570b3a5be9c4e694f23d85232fb55f4a6f1f7fc/sam3/model/geometry_encoders.py#L576-L578)).

**transformers (main @5602e09)**
- Gate: [modeling_sam3.py#L2371-L2376](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/5602e09ee03d1be78dbff52bc9715e9863c44bd1/src/transformers/models/sam3/modeling_sam3.py#L2371-L2376)
- Text-only branch: [L2427](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/5602e09ee03d1be78dbff52bc9715e9863c44bd1/src/transformers/models/sam3/modeling_sam3.py#L2427)

**Related.** #46128 (SAM 3.1, open) removes this gate. Its code comment says skipping the call "produces a different prompt structure than the pretrained checkpoint was trained with". That PR has been inactive since June, and the issue affects SAM 3 on main independently of SAM 3.1. #45059 (closed) shows a related symptom: adding a dummy box, which runs the geometry encoder, changes text-only results.

### Suggestion
Always run the geometry encoder, as #46128 does, or make the behaviour explicit with a flag and document that text-only outputs otherwise differ from Meta's reference.

### System Info
transformers 5.19.0 (also main @ e24eb546fe), tokenizers 0.23.3, Python 3.12, Windows. Compared against transformers 4.57.6.

### Reproduction

```python
from transformers import AutoTokenizer

tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("microsoft/deberta-v3-base")
print(tok.convert_ids_to_tokens(tok("ﬁ Ⅻ ① ｆｕｌｌｗｉｄｔｈ").input_ids))
```

- 5.19.0: `['[CLS]', '▁', '[UNK]', '▁', '[UNK]', '▁', '[UNK]', '▁', '[UNK]', '[SEP]']`
- 4.57.6 (fast and slow), and the original SentencePiece model: `['[CLS]', '▁fi', '▁XII', '▁1', '▁full', 'width', '[SEP]']`

Same for deberta-v3-small/large, mdeberta-v3-base, deberta-v2-xlarge, and fine-tunes that ship a `tokenizer.json` (e.g. `protectai/deberta-v3-base-prompt-injection-v2`). For mdeberta this hits ordinary CJK text: fullwidth letters and digits (`ＴＯＫＹＯ２０２６年`), halfwidth katakana, `①`. On 10 such realistic lines, 5.19.0 disagrees with SentencePiece on 10/10.

### Cause
The v5 loader passes the SentencePiece precompiled charsmap as `_spm_precompiled_charsmap` (`convert_slow_tokenizer.py`, and from `tokenizer.json` in `tokenization_utils_tokenizers.py`). `XLMRobertaTokenizer`, `T5Tokenizer` and `AlbertTokenizer` accept it and add `normalizers.Precompiled(...)`. `DebertaV2Tokenizer.__init__` doesn't. The kwarg is swallowed by `**kwargs` and then popped in `TokenizersBackend.__init__`, and the class hardcodes `Replace` + `NFC` + `Strip`. NFC doesn't fold compatibility characters; DeBERTa's `nmt_nfkc` charsmap does. v4's `DebertaV2Converter` included the `Precompiled` normalizer.

### Proposed fix (verified locally)
Accept `_spm_precompiled_charsmap` in `DebertaV2Tokenizer.__init__` and add `normalizers.Precompiled(_spm_precompiled_charsmap)` when it's set, the same way `AlbertTokenizer` does:


### System Info

transformers 5.19.0, tokenizers 0.23.3, Python 3.11, macOS. Tokenizer-only: no PyTorch needed to reproduce.

### The problem

Loading `microsoft/deberta-v3-base` from local files prints the Mistral regex warning, and **following that warning changes the tokenizer** -- on plain English text:

```python
from transformers import AutoTokenizer

name = "microsoft/deberta-v3-base"
plain   = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(name, local_files_only=True)
patched = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(name, local_files_only=True, fix_mistral_regex=True)

s = "The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog."
print(plain.tokenize(s))
print(patched.tokenize(s))
```

```
plain  : ['▁The', '▁quick', '▁brown', '▁fox', '▁jumps', '▁over', '▁the', '▁lazy', '▁dog', '.']
patched: ['The', ' ', 'quick', ' ', 'brown', ' ', 'fox', ' ', 'jump', 's', ' ', 'over', ' ', 'the', ' ', 'lazy', ' ', 'dog', '.']
```

The Mistral pre-tokenizer replaces DeBERTa's: the `▁` space marker is gone and `jumps` becomes `jump` + `s`. No exception -- just different ids, silently.

### Why it is taken for Mistral

Both early exits for non-Mistral models in `_patch_mistral_regex` require `transformers_version` to be present:

```python
if transformers_version and version.parse(transformers_version) < version.parse("5.0.0"):
    if (is_local and transformers_model_type is not None
            and transformers_model_type not in ["mistral", "mistral3", "voxtral", "ministral", "pixtral"]):
        return tokenizer
elif transformers_version and version.parse(transformers_version) >= version.parse("5.0.0"):
    return tokenizer

mistral_config_detected = True      # <- fallthrough
```

`microsoft/deberta-v3-base` is a 2021 checkpoint and its `config.json` has no `transformers_version` key at all, so neither branch runs and control reaches the fallthrough. #45444 lifted the non-Mistral early exit out of the version *comparison*, but it is still gated on the field *existing*.

### Scope

Four conditions have to line up, which is both why this is narrow and why it is easy to hit:

1. `vocab_size > 100000` (the entry condition, line 511 of `tokenization_utils_tokenizers.py`)
2. `pre_tokenizer` is not None
3. loaded locally (`local_files_only=True` or `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1`) -- an online load never enters the path for this checkpoint, since `is_base_mistral()` is False
4. `config.json` without `transformers_version`

Condition 4 correlates with age, so this is older large-vocab checkpoints. `albert-base-v2` has the same missing field and is unaffected: its vocab is 30000, so it never enters `_patch_mistral_regex`. I checked both directions.

Offline loading is a normal path (CI, air-gapped hosts, Hub outages), which is how I hit it.

### Suggested fix

A missing `transformers_version` means "older than the field", not "unknown, so assume Mistral":

```python
if transformers_version is None or version.parse(transformers_version) < version.parse("5.0.0"):
    if (is_local and transformers_model_type is not None
            and transformers_model_type not in ["mistral", "mistral3", "voxtral", "ministral", "pixtral"]):
        return tokenizer
```

I have not opened a PR -- this is the reproduction, the trace, and the check on a control model. Glad to open one if the diagnosis holds up.

1. `vocab_size > 100000` (the entry condition, line 511 of `tokenization_utils_tokenizers.py`)
2. `pre_tokenizer` is not None
3. loaded locally (`local_files_only=True` or `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1`) -- an online load never enters the path for this checkpoint, since `is_base_mistral()` is False
4. `config.json` without `transformers_version`

Condition 4 correlates with age, so this is older large-vocab checkpoints. `albert-base-v2` has the same missing field and is unaffected: its vocab is 30000, so it never enters `_patch_mistral_regex`. I checked both directions.

Offline loading is a normal path (CI, air-gapped hosts, Hub outages), which is how I hit it.

### Suggested fix

A missing `transformers_version` means "older than the field", not "unknown, so assume Mistral":

```python
if transformers_version is None or version.parse(transformers_version) < version.parse("5.0.0"):
    if (is_local and transformers_model_type is not None
            and transformers_model_type not in ["mistral", "mistral3", "voxtral", "ministral", "pixtral"]):
        return tokenizer
```

I have not opened a PR -- this is the reproduction, the trace, and the check on a control model. Glad to open one if the diagnosis holds up.

### System Info
transformers main @ e24eb546fe (2026-10-15), torch 2.11, torchvision 0.26, Python 3.12, Windows, CPU.

### Reproduction

```python
from transformers import AutoImageProcessor, JanusImageProcessor, JanusImageProcessorPil

# 1. default construction: the two backends disagree
print(JanusImageProcessor().background_color, JanusImageProcessorPil().background_color)
# (127, 127, 127) (122, 116, 104)

# 2. an explicit colour is ignored
print(JanusImageProcessor(background_color=(0, 0, 0)).background_color)
# (127, 127, 127)

# 3. a real checkpoint: preprocessor_config.json saves "background_color": [122, 116, 104]
p = AutoImageProcessor.from_pretrained("deepseek-community/deepseek-vl-7b-chat")
print(p.background_color, p.high_res_background_color)
# (127, 127, 127) (122, 116, 104)
```

The same holds for `DeepseekVLImageProcessor(Pil)` and `DeepseekVLHybridImageProcessor(Pil)`, in both backends.

### Cause
The `__init__` of these six classes recomputes the padding colour from the mean and never reads `background_color` / `high_res_background_color` from kwargs. The torchvision classes also use `kwargs.get("image_mean")`, which only sees values passed in, while the PIL classes use `getattr(self, "image_mean")`, which also sees class defaults. That's why a default-constructed processor gives grey in one backend and the CLIP mean in the other, and why a `save_pretrained` -> `from_pretrained` round trip changes the torchvision colour.

### Which colour is right
The original code (`deepseek-ai/Janus` and `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-VL`, `image_processing_vlm.py`) pads with `tuple(int(x * 255) for x in image_mean)`, i.e. a colour derived from the mean of the processor that pads. For Janus-Pro-1B/7B and deepseek-vl-1.3b-chat (mean 0.5) that gives 127, and transformers already loads 127 for them, so they're unaffected.

deepseek-vl-7b-chat is different. DeepSeek's original `deepseek-ai/deepseek-vl-7b-chat` uses a single processor at 1024 px with the CLIP mean and `"background_color": [122, 116, 104]`, and pads once before the hybrid vision tower downsamples to 384 for the SigLIP branch. So both branches originally see (122, 116, 104) padding. The converted checkpoint saves that colour, but transformers drops it and pads the low-res branch with 127. The effect is small (the padding grey differs by about 0.04 after normalization, and only on non-square images), but it doesn't match the original model.

### Proposed fix (verified locally)
Let an explicit or saved colour win, and otherwise derive it from the mean read from `self`, in all six classes. For Janus:

```diff
     def __init__(self, **kwargs: Unpack[JanusImageProcessorKwargs]):
         super().__init__(**kwargs)
-        if kwargs.get("image_mean") is None:
-            background_color = (127, 127, 127)
-        else:
-            background_color = tuple(int(x * 255) for x in kwargs.get("image_mean"))
+        # An explicit (or saved) `background_color` wins; otherwise pad with the normalisation mean, as the
+        # original Janus preprocessing does. Read the mean from `self` so class defaults count too.
+        background_color = kwargs.get("background_color")
+        if background_color is None:
+            image_mean = getattr(self, "image_mean", None)
+            background_color = (127, 127, 127) if image_mean is None else tuple(int(x * 255) for x in image_mean)
         self.background_color = tuple(background_color)
```

DeepSeek-VL is the same change; DeepSeek-VL-Hybrid also handles `high_res_background_color` and is edited in `modular_deepseek_vl_hybrid.py`. The full patch (8 files, including a regression test) is below.

With it, on main:
- default construction gives the same colour in both backends for all six classes; an explicit colour is respected; save/load round-trips;
- deepseek-vl-7b-chat loads (122, 116, 104) for both branches; Janus-Pro-1B/7B and deepseek-vl-1.3b-chat still load 127 (unchanged);
- the new test `test_background_color_default_explicit_and_round_trip` fails on main and passes with the fix;
- janus / deepseek_vl / deepseek_vl_hybrid image-processing tests: 69 passed with the fix; on main the only failure is the new test;
- `utils/check_modular_conversion.py` passes.

I didn't run the slow `deepseek_vl_hybrid` integration tests (7B on GPU). Since the low-res padding changes for that checkpoint, their expected outputs could shift slightly on non-square images.

### Reproduction

```python
from transformers import AutoImageProcessor, JanusImageProcessor, JanusImageProcessorPil

# 1. default construction: the two backends disagree
print(JanusImageProcessor().background_color, JanusImageProcessorPil().background_color)
# (127, 127, 127) (122, 116, 104)

# 2. an explicit colour is ignored
print(JanusImageProcessor(background_color=(0, 0, 0)).background_color)
# (127, 127, 127)

# 3. a real checkpoint: preprocessor_config.json saves "background_color": [122, 116, 104]
p = AutoImageProcessor.from_pretrained("deepseek-community/deepseek-vl-7b-chat")
print(p.background_color, p.high_res_background_color)
# (127, 127, 127) (122, 116, 104)
```

The same holds for `DeepseekVLImageProcessor(Pil)` and `DeepseekVLHybridImageProcessor(Pil)`, in both backends.

### Cause
The `__init__` of these six classes recomputes the padding colour from the mean and never reads `background_color` / `high_res_background_color` from kwargs. The torchvision classes also use `kwargs.get("image_mean")`, which only sees values passed in, while the PIL classes use `getattr(self, "image_mean")`, which also sees class defaults. That's why a default-constructed processor gives grey in one backend and the CLIP mean in the other, and why a `save_pretrained` -> `from_pretrained` round trip changes the torchvision colour.

### Which colour is right
The original code (`deepseek-ai/Janus` and `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-VL`, `image_processing_vlm.py`) pads with `tuple(int(x * 255) for x in image_mean)`, i.e. a colour derived from the mean of the processor that pads. For Janus-Pro-1B/7B and deepseek-vl-1.3b-chat (mean 0.5) that gives 127, and transformers already loads 127 for them, so they're unaffected.

deepseek-vl-7b-chat is different. DeepSeek's original `deepseek-ai/deepseek-vl-7b-chat` uses a single processor at 1024 px with the CLIP mean and `"background_color": [122, 116, 104]`, and pads once before the hybrid vision tower downsamples to 384 for the SigLIP branch. So both branches originally see (122, 116, 104) padding. The converted checkpoint saves that colour, but transformers drops it and pads the low-res branch with 127. The effect is small (the padding grey differs by about 0.04 after normalization, and only on non-square images), but it doesn't match the original model.

### Proposed fix (verified locally)
Let an explicit or saved colour win, and otherwise derive it from the mean read from `self`, in all six classes. For Janus:

```diff
     def __init__(self, **kwargs: Unpack[JanusImageProcessorKwargs]):
         super().__init__(**kwargs)
-        if kwargs.get("image_mean") is None:
-            background_color = (127, 127, 127)
-        else:
-            background_color = tuple(int(x * 255) for x in kwargs.get("image_mean"))
+        # An explicit (or saved) `background_color` wins; otherwise pad with the normalisation mean, as the
+        # original Janus preprocessing does. Read the mean from `self` so class defaults count too.
+        background_color = kwargs.get("background_color")
+        if background_color is None:
+            image_mean = getattr(self, "image_mean", None)
+            background_color = (127, 127, 127) if image_mean is None else tuple(int(x * 255) for x in image_mean)
         self.background_color = tuple(background_color)
```

DeepSeek-VL is the same change; DeepSeek-VL-Hybrid also handles `high_res_background_color` and is edited in `modular_deepseek_vl_hybrid.py`. The full patch (8 files, including a regression test) is below.

With it, on main:
- default construction gives the same colour in both backends for all six classes; an explicit colour is respected; save/load round-trips;
- deepseek-vl-7b-chat loads (122, 116, 104) for both branches; Janus-Pro-1B/7B and deepseek-vl-1.3b-chat still load 127 (unchanged);
- the new test `test_background_color_default_explicit_and_round_trip` fails on main and passes with the fix;
- janus / deepseek_vl / deepseek_vl_hybrid image-processing tests: 69 passed with the fix; on main the only failure is the new test;
- `utils/check_modular_conversion.py` passes.

I didn't run the slow `deepseek_vl_hybrid` integration tests (7B on GPU). Since the low-res padding changes for that checkpoint, their expected outputs could shift slightly on non-square images.

body_text:
Hi!

The previous Urdu tracker (#33139) was closed as dormant, with an invitation to open a fresh issue if someone picked Urdu docs back up. I'd like to do that.

I'm an NLP Engineer at Proxima AI, working on Urdu language technologies, including language models, speech recognition, text-to-speech, and datasets. As a Pakistani Urdu speaker working on open-source language technology, I'd like to help make the Transformers documentation more accessible to Urdu speaking developers and researchers.

I've reviewed the translated content myself against the original English documentation to check accuracy, technical meaning, and terminology.

Let's bring the documentation to the Urdu speaking community.

## Plan

1. A first small PR with `ur/_toctree.yml` and the Get Started pages (`index.md`, `quicktour.md`, `installation.md`). It's ready on my fork: `mwzkhalil:docs/urdu-get-started`.
2. The remaining pages in small batches, following the order of the English `_toctree.yml`.

The first PR also adds `ur` to the `languages` lists in `.github/workflows/build_documentation.yml` and `.github/workflows/pr_build_doc_with_comment.yml` so the docs build. Happy to drop that change if you'd prefer to handle it yourselves.

## Terminology

To keep terms consistent:

- Library, product, and code names stay in Latin script: Transformers, Accelerate, `torch.compile`, CPU, GPU, Apple Silicon.
- Everyday nouns are translated: image → تصویر, text → متن, speech → تقریر, language → زبان, classification → درجہ بندی.
- Established ML terms are transliterated: model → ماڈل, tokenizer → ٹوکنائزر, inference → انفرنس, fine-tuning → فائن ٹیوننگ, generation → جنریشن.

Feedback from other Urdu speakers on these choices is very welcome.

## Get Started section

- [ ] [index.md](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/main/docs/source/en/index.md) (@mwzkhalil)
- [ ] [quicktour.md](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/main/docs/source/en/quicktour.md) (@mwzkhalil)
- [ ] [installation.md](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/main/docs/source/en/installation.md) (@mwzkhalil)

## Planned next (@mwzkhalil)

- [ ] Tutorials: `pipeline_tutorial.md`, `training.md`, `accelerate.md`, `peft.md`, `model_sharing.md`, `llm_tutorial.md`
- [ ] Task guides (NLP, audio, computer vision, multimodal), `generation_strategies.md`, `tasks/prompting.md`
- [ ] Developer guides: `fast_tokenizers.md`, `custom_models.md`, `chat_templating.md`, `serialization.md`, `troubleshooting.md`
- [ ] Performance: `perf_train_cpu.md`, `perf_train_special.md`, `perf_hardware.md`, `hpo_train.md`, `perf_torch_compile.md`

Others are welcome to join; just comment here with the page you'd like to take.

@stevhliu Would you be able to review the first PR once it's up?

Thanks!

### System Info

- `transformers` version: 5.21.0.dev0 (main at b0cdc61e60)
- Platform: macOS-26.6.2-arm64-arm-64bit
- Python version: 3.12.13
- Huggingface_hub version: 2.2.0
- Tokenizers version: 0.23.2
- PyTorch version: 2.13.0

### Who can help?

@SunMarc (follow-up from #49400)

### Reproduction

Found while adding the LFM2 GGUF tokenizer test in #49400. With the default encoding, the GGUF tokenizer drops BOS:

```python
from transformers import AutoTokenizer

g = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("LiquidAI/LFM2.5-230M-GGUF", gguf_file="LFM2.5-230M-Q4_K_M.gguf")
r = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("LiquidAI/LFM2.5-230M")
g("The capital of France is Paris.").input_ids[:4]  # [1098, 5706, 803, 4481]
r("The capital of France is Paris.").input_ids[:4]  # [1, 1098, 5706, 803]
```

The file already has `tokenizer.ggml.add_bos_token = True`, but `GGUF_TOKENIZER_MAPPING` never reads it. This is not LFM2-specific. `tokenizer.ggml.add_eos_token` is not mapped either, but EOS is not impacted today: only T5 and FlanT5 set it to `True`, and they get the token from their tokenizer.

The existing `GgufTokenizerTesterMixin` does not catch this, because every encoding check uses `add_special_tokens=False`.

Default encodings (`tokenizer(text).input_ids`) against the reference, for every `*GgufTokenizerTest` in `tests/quantization/ggml/test_gguf_integration.py`:

| Test | `add_bos_token` in file | main | with mapping |
|---|---|---|---|
| Lfm2 (LFM2.5-230M) | True | BOS missing | match |
| Llama (3.1-8B-Instruct) | True | BOS missing | match |
| Mistral (Ministral-8B) | True | BOS missing | match |
| Gemma (3-1B) | True | BOS missing | match |
| Gemma4 (E4B) | True | match | **extra BOS** |
| TinyLlama | not set | BOS missing | BOS missing |
| Qwen3, Qwen2.5, Phi3, T5, FlanT5 | False | match | match |

### Expected behavior

The default encoding should match the reference tokenizer: BOS is added when the file sets `tokenizer.ggml.add_bos_token = True`.

The fix is to map both flags into `tokenizer_config`:

```python
    "tokenizer_config": {
        "chat_template": "chat_template",
        "ggml.add_bos_token": "add_bos_token",
        "ggml.add_eos_token": "add_eos_token",
    },
```

This affects only plain `tokenizer(prompt)` + `generate`, not chat templates.

Two special cases stay as they are for now:

- Gemma 4: the file says `add_bos_token = True`, but the reference post-processor adds no BOS (its chat template writes `<bos>` itself). With the mapping, the GGUF tokenizer adds an extra BOS. Which one should win?
- TinyLlama: the file has no `add_bos_token` flag, so the mapping cannot help.

I will open a PR with the mapping and a test that compares the default encoding against the reference.

- `transformers` version: 5.21.0.dev0 (main at b0cdc61e60)
- Platform: macOS-26.6.2-arm64-arm-64bit
- Python version: 3.12.13
- Huggingface_hub version: 2.2.0
- Tokenizers version: 0.23.2
- PyTorch version: 2.13.0

### Who can help?

@SunMarc (follow-up from #49400)

### Reproduction

Found while adding the LFM2 GGUF tokenizer test in #49400. With the default encoding, the GGUF tokenizer drops BOS:

```python
from transformers import AutoTokenizer

g = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("LiquidAI/LFM2.5-230M-GGUF", gguf_file="LFM2.5-230M-Q4_K_M.gguf")
r = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("LiquidAI/LFM2.5-230M")
g("The capital of France is Paris.").input_ids[:4]  # [1098, 5706, 803, 4481]
r("The capital of France is Paris.").input_ids[:4]  # [1, 1098, 5706, 803]
```

The file already has `tokenizer.ggml.add_bos_token = True`, but `GGUF_TOKENIZER_MAPPING` never reads it. This is not LFM2-specific. `tokenizer.ggml.add_eos_token` is not mapped either, but EOS is not impacted today: only T5 and FlanT5 set it to `True`, and they get the token from their tokenizer.

The existing `GgufTokenizerTesterMixin` does not catch this, because every encoding check uses `add_special_tokens=False`.

Default encodings (`tokenizer(text).input_ids`) against the reference, for every `*GgufTokenizerTest` in `tests/quantization/ggml/test_gguf_integration.py`:

| Test | `add_bos_token` in file | main | with mapping |
|---|---|---|---|
| Lfm2 (LFM2.5-230M) | True | BOS missing | match |
| Llama (3.1-8B-Instruct) | True | BOS missing | match |
| Mistral (Ministral-8B) | True | BOS missing | match |
| Gemma (3-1B) | True | BOS missing | match |
| Gemma4 (E4B) | True | match | **extra BOS** |
| TinyLlama | not set | BOS missing | BOS missing |
| Qwen3, Qwen2.5, Phi3, T5, FlanT5 | False | match | match |

### Expected behavior

The default encoding should match the reference tokenizer: BOS is added when the file sets `tokenizer.ggml.add_bos_token = True`.

The fix is to map both flags into `tokenizer_config`:

```python
    "tokenizer_config": {
        "chat_template": "chat_template",
        "ggml.add_bos_token": "add_bos_token",
        "ggml.add_eos_token": "add_eos_token",
    },
```

This affects only plain `tokenizer(prompt)` + `generate`, not chat templates.

Two special cases stay as they are for now:

- Gemma 4: the file says `add_bos_token = True`, but the reference post-processor adds no BOS (its chat template writes `<bos>` itself). With the mapping, the GGUF tokenizer adds an extra BOS. Which one should win?
- TinyLlama: the file has no `add_bos_token` flag, so the mapping cannot help.

I will open a PR with the mapping and a test that compares the default encoding against the reference.

For tokenizers that load through `TokenizersBackend` (Hub repos with `tokenizer_class: PreTrainedTokenizerFast`, e.g. Llama 3, GLM-4.x, Granite, OLMo-2), `convert_to_native_format` builds the Rust tokenizer with `TokenizerFast.from_file` and passes it as `tokenizer_object`. `__init__` then runs `copy.deepcopy(tokenizer_object)`, which pickles and re-parses the whole backend. On Llama 3 that copy is about 0.46 s of a 0.75 s `AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained` from the local cache.

Since the object is created internally, the copy doesn't protect anything. Passing `tokenizer_file` instead lets `__init__` load it once through its existing `from_file` branch, and loading gets 2-2.9x faster (Llama 3: 646 ms -> 224 ms, GLM-4.5-Air: 850 -> 397 ms) with byte-identical tokenizers, encodings and saved files. Users who pass `tokenizer_object=` themselves would still get a copy.

I have a one-line PR for this if it sounds good.

### Reproduction

The `json` content parser's `string_delims` captures up to the first closing delimiter and never decodes escapes, so a template that escapes its string delimiter (LFM2.5, e.g. `LiquidAI/LFM2.5-24B-A2B`, renders `'` as `\'`, and escapes `\` and newlines) can't round-trip its own tool-call arguments:

```python
from transformers.utils.chat_parsing.content_parsers import parse_content

args = {"string_delims": [["'", "'"]], "allow_non_json": True}
for raw in [r"'Paris'", r"'Saint-Jean-d\'Angély'", r"'Paris\nFrance'", r"'C:\\Users'"]:
    print(f"{raw!s:28} -> {parse_content(raw, 'json', args)!r}")
```

```
'Paris'                      -> 'Paris'
'Saint-Jean-d\'Angély'       -> "'Saint-Jean-d\\'Angély'"
'Paris\nFrance'              -> 'Paris\\nFrance'
'C:\\Users'                  -> 'C:\\\\Users'
```

The tool then gets called with different arguments than the model wrote.

`Saint-Jean-d'Angély`, `Paris` + newline + `France`, `C:\Users`: an escape option on `string_delims` (e.g. `"string_escape": "\\"`) that skips escaped delimiters when capturing and decodes the escapes.

### System Info

```
- `transformers` version: 5.20.1
- Platform: Linux-7.1.5-76070105-generic-x86_64-with-glibc2.39
- Python version: 3.12.3
- Huggingface_hub version: 2.2.0
- Safetensors version: 0.8.0
- Accelerate version: not installed

- DeepSpeed version: not installed
- PyTorch version (accelerator?): 2.14.1+cpu (NA)
- Using distributed or parallel set-up in script?: No
```

### Who can help?

@zucchini-nlp @Cyrilvallez

### Reproduction

Since 5.20.0, `generate()` crashes for encoder-decoder models and for vision-language models that pass `mm_encoder_outputs` whenever the ids driving the loop are on a different device than the model. The new `move_to_device` helper used in `prepare_inputs_for_generation` rebuilds every mapping as a plain `dict`, so `ModelOutput` values such as `encoder_outputs` and the entries of `mm_encoder_outputs` lose their type and attributes.

The script below runs on CPU only. It patches `PreTrainedModel.device` to report `cpu:0`, which makes the `input_tensor.device != self.device` branch fire the same way it does on a GPU when `input_ids` are kept on the host.

```python
"""generate() fails when the ids driving the loop are on a different device than the model.

No accelerator is needed: `PreTrainedModel.device` is patched to report `cpu:0`, so the
`input_tensor.device != self.device` branch in `prepare_inputs_for_generation` fires on a
CPU-only machine exactly as it does on a GPU when `input_ids` are left on the host.
"""

import platform
import traceback

import torch

import transformers
from transformers import (
    BartConfig,
    BartForConditionalGeneration,
    CLIPVisionConfig,
    LlamaConfig,
    LlavaConfig,
    LlavaForConditionalGeneration,
    PreTrainedModel,
)
from transformers.modeling_outputs import BaseModelOutput
from transformers.pytorch_utils import move_to_device


print("python:", platform.python_version())
print("transformers:", transformers.__version__)
print("torch:", torch.__version__)
print()

torch.manual_seed(0)

# 1. The helper itself
out = BaseModelOutput(last_hidden_state=torch.zeros(1, 2, 4))
moved = move_to_device(out, torch.device("cpu"))
print("move_to_device(BaseModelOutput) returns:", type(moved).__name__)
print("expected:                               BaseModelOutput")
print()

# 2. generate(), first as a control, then with the host-input branch active


def run(name, fn):
    try:
        res = fn()
        print(f"{name}: OK, output shape {tuple(res.shape)}")
    except Exception as e:
        frame = traceback.extract_tb(e.__traceback__)[-1]
        print(f"{name}: {type(e).__name__}: {e}")
        print(f"    raised at {frame.filename.split('site-packages/')[-1]}:{frame.lineno}")


bart = BartForConditionalGeneration(
    BartConfig(
        vocab_size=64,
        d_model=16,
        encoder_layers=1,
        decoder_layers=1,
        encoder_attention_heads=2,
        decoder_attention_heads=2,
        encoder_ffn_dim=32,
        decoder_ffn_dim=32,
        max_position_embeddings=64,
    )
).eval()
ids = torch.tensor([[0, 5, 6, 7, 2]])

llava_cfg = LlavaConfig(
    vision_config=CLIPVisionConfig(
        hidden_size=16,
        intermediate_size=32,
        num_hidden_layers=1,
        num_attention_heads=2,
        image_size=8,
        patch_size=4,
        projection_dim=16,
    ),
    text_config=LlamaConfig(
        vocab_size=64,
        hidden_size=16,
        intermediate_size=32,
        num_hidden_layers=1,
        num_attention_heads=2,
        num_key_value_heads=2,
        max_position_embeddings=64,
        pad_token_id=0,
    ),
    image_token_index=63,
    vision_feature_layer=-1,
    vision_feature_select_strategy="full",
)
llava = LlavaForConditionalGeneration(llava_cfg).eval()
n_img_tokens = (8 // 4) ** 2 + 1  # patches + CLS with the "full" strategy
input_ids = torch.tensor([[1] + [63] * n_img_tokens + [5, 6]])
pixel_values = torch.randn(1, 3, 8, 8)


def bart_gen():
    return bart.generate(ids, max_new_tokens=3, do_sample=False)


def llava_gen():
    return llava.generate(input_ids=input_ids, pixel_values=pixel_values, max_new_tokens=3, do_sample=False)


print("ids on the model device:")
run("  bart generate", bart_gen)
run("  llava generate", llava_gen)

PreTrainedModel.device = property(lambda self: torch.device("cpu", 0))
print("ids on another device (model reports cpu:0):")
run("  bart generate", bart_gen)
run("  llava generate", llava_gen)
print()
print("expected: both generate calls return tokens, as they do when the ids are already on the model device")
```

Output:

```
python: 3.12.3
transformers: 5.20.1
torch: 2.14.1+cpu

move_to_device(BaseModelOutput) returns: dict
expected:                               BaseModelOutput

ids on the model device:
  bart generate: OK, output shape (1, 4)
  llava generate: OK, output shape (1, 11)
ids on another device (model reports cpu:0):
  bart generate: KeyError: 0
    raised at transformers/models/bart/modeling_bart.py:768
  llava generate: AttributeError: 'dict' object has no attribute 'pooler_output'
    raised at transformers/models/llava/modeling_llava.py:253

expected: both generate calls return tokens, as they do when the ids are already on the model device
```

On a real accelerator the Llava case is the one the new branch is meant for: `input_ids` on the host, `pixel_values` on the device. For encoder-decoder models, a BART-style model with host `decoder_input_ids` fails earlier at the decoder start token check (unrelated to this change), but Donut-style `VisionEncoderDecoderModel` and Whisper skip that check, so `pixel_values` on the device with a host task prompt in `decoder_input_ids` reaches the branch and hits the same `encoder_outputs[0]` lookup in `modeling_vision_encoder_decoder.py`. I have not run that on a GPU, the path is from reading the code.

Cause, at main (d4804f9, same lines in v5.20.1):

- `src/transformers/pytorch_utils.py:216`, `move_to_device` returns `{k: move_to_device(v, device) for k, v in value.items()}` for any `dict` instance. `ModelOutput` subclasses `OrderedDict` (`src/transformers/utils/generic.py:419`), so it comes back as a plain `dict`.
- `src/transformers/generation/utils.py:785` calls it on the whole `model_inputs` when the input tensor is off the model device. Before #49317 only top-level tensors were moved there, and the `ModelOutput` values produced by the model's own encoder passed through unchanged.
- The consumers depend on the type: `models/bart/modeling_bart.py:766-768` takes the `not isinstance(encoder_outputs, BaseModelOutput)` path and indexes `encoder_outputs[0]` (`KeyError: 0`), and `models/llava/modeling_llava.py:253` reads `mm_encoder_outputs["image"].pooler_output` (`AttributeError`).

The test added in #49317 for this path (`test_generate_with_inputs_on_cpu_moves_tensors_in_dict_inputs`) needs an accelerator and uses a decoder-only model whose nested dict holds only tensors, so it does not cover this.

### Expected behavior

`generate()` returns tokens for both models, as it does when the ids are already on the model device, and `move_to_device(BaseModelOutput(...))` returns a `BaseModelOutput`.

Proposed fix: keep the container type in `move_to_device` for mappings, for example by copying the mapping and assigning the moved values back (`ModelOutput` supports item assignment), or by building `type(value)(**moved)` for `ModelOutput`. Skipping `ModelOutput` values would also work, since the model produces them on its own device. A CPU unit test for `move_to_device` with a `ModelOutput`, plus a generate test that forces the branch for one encoder-decoder and one `mm_encoder_outputs` model, would catch this. I'm happy to open a PR for it.

```python
print("transformers:", transformers.__version__)
print("torch:", torch.__version__)
print()
```

```
python: 3.12.3
transformers: 5.20.1
torch: 2.14.1+cpu

move_to_device(BaseModelOutput) returns: dict
expected:                               BaseModelOutput

ids on the model device:
  bart generate: OK, output shape (1, 4)
  llava generate: OK, output shape (1, 11)
ids on another device (model reports cpu:0):
  bart generate: KeyError: 0
    raised at transformers/models/bart/modeling_bart.py:768
  llava generate: AttributeError: 'dict' object has no attribute 'pooler_output'
    raised at transformers/models/llava/modeling_llava.py:253

expected: both generate calls return tokens, as they do when the ids are already on the model device
```

On a real accelerator the Llava case is the one the new branch is meant for: `input_ids` on the host, `pixel_values` on the device. For encoder-decoder models, a BART-style model with host `decoder_input_ids` fails earlier at the decoder start token check (unrelated to this change), but Donut-style `VisionEncoderDecoderModel` and Whisper skip that check, so `pixel_values` on the device with a host task prompt in `decoder_input_ids` reaches the branch and hits the same `encoder_outputs[0]` lookup in `modeling_vision_encoder_decoder.py`. I have not run that on a GPU, the path is from reading the code.

Cause, at main (d4804f9, same lines in v5.20.1):

- `src/transformers/pytorch_utils.py:216`, `move_to_device` returns `{k: move_to_device(v, device) for k, v in value.items()}` for any `dict` instance. `ModelOutput` subclasses `OrderedDict` (`src/transformers/utils/generic.py:419`), so it comes back as a plain `dict`.
- `src/transformers/generation/utils.py:785` calls it on the whole `model_inputs` when the input tensor is off the model device. Before #49317 only top-level tensors were moved there, and the `ModelOutput` values produced by the model's own encoder passed through unchanged.
- The consumers depend on the type: `models/bart/modeling_bart.py:766-768` takes the `not isinstance(encoder_outputs, BaseModelOutput)` path and indexes `encoder_outputs[0]` (`KeyError: 0`), and `models/llava/modeling_llava.py:253` reads `mm_encoder_outputs["image"].pooler_output` (`AttributeError`).

The test added in #49317 for this path (`test_generate_with_inputs_on_cpu_moves_tensors_in_dict_inputs`) needs an accelerator and uses a decoder-only model whose nested dict holds only tensors, so it does not cover this.

### Expected behavior

`generate()` returns tokens for both models, as it does when the ids are already on the model device, and `move_to_device(BaseModelOutput(...))` returns a `BaseModelOutput`.

Proposed fix: keep the container type in `move_to_device` for mappings, for example by copying the mapping and assigning the moved values back (`ModelOutput` supports item assignment), or by building `type(value)(**moved)` for `ModelOutput`. Skipping `ModelOutput` values would also work, since the model produces them on its own device. A CPU unit test for `move_to_device` with a `ModelOutput`, plus a generate test that forces the branch for one encoder-decoder and one `mm_encoder_outputs` model, would catch this. I'm happy to open a PR for it.

### Reproduction

With `prefill_chunk_size` set, a vision-language model never receives the image during prefill. Every chunked forward is called without `pixel_values` or `mm_encoder_outputs`, so the output does not depend on the image at all, and nothing warns about it.

Tiny Llava built from a config, one image, `max_new_tokens=6`, runs on CPU:

```python
"""With prefill_chunk_size set, a vision-language model generates without ever seeing the image."""

import platform

import torch

import transformers
from transformers import CLIPVisionConfig, LlamaConfig, LlavaConfig, LlavaForConditionalGeneration


print("python:", platform.python_version())
print("transformers:", transformers.__version__)
print("torch:", torch.__version__)
print()

torch.manual_seed(3)
cfg = LlavaConfig(
    vision_config=CLIPVisionConfig(
        hidden_size=16,
        intermediate_size=32,
        num_hidden_layers=1,
        num_attention_heads=2,
        image_size=8,
        patch_size=4,
        projection_dim=16,
    ),
    text_config=LlamaConfig(
        vocab_size=64,
        hidden_size=16,
        intermediate_size=32,
        num_hidden_layers=1,
        num_attention_heads=2,
        num_key_value_heads=2,
        max_position_embeddings=64,
        pad_token_id=0,
    ),
    image_token_index=63,
    vision_feature_layer=-1,
    vision_feature_select_strategy="full",
)
model = LlavaForConditionalGeneration(cfg).eval()

n_img_tokens = (8 // 4) ** 2 + 1  # patches + CLS with the "full" strategy
input_ids = torch.tensor([[1] + [63] * n_img_tokens + [5, 6, 7, 8]])  # 10 tokens, 3 chunks of 4
image_a = torch.randn(1, 3, 8, 8)
image_b = torch.randn(1, 3, 8, 8) * 5

seen = []


def record(module, args, kwargs):
    if kwargs["input_ids"].shape[-1] > 1:  # prefill forwards only
        seen.append(sorted(k for k in ("pixel_values", "mm_encoder_outputs") if kwargs.get(k) is not None))


model.register_forward_pre_hook(record, with_kwargs=True)


def gen(pixel_values, **kwargs):
    seen.clear()
    out = model.generate(
        input_ids=input_ids,
        pixel_values=pixel_values,
        max_new_tokens=6,
        do_sample=False,
        output_scores=True,
        return_dict_in_generate=True,
        **kwargs,
    )
    return out.sequences[0, input_ids.shape[-1] :].tolist(), torch.stack(out.scores), list(seen)


tok_full, sc_full, seen_full = gen(image_a)
tok_chunk, sc_chunk, seen_chunk = gen(image_a, prefill_chunk_size=4)
tok_chunk_b, sc_chunk_b, _ = gen(image_b, prefill_chunk_size=4)
tok_full_b, sc_full_b, _ = gen(image_b)

print("image inputs seen by prefill forwards, unchunked:", seen_full)
print("image inputs seen by prefill forwards, chunked:  ", seen_chunk)
print("tokens unchunked:           ", tok_full)
print("tokens unchunked, other image:", tok_full_b)
print("tokens chunked:             ", tok_chunk)
print("tokens chunked, other image:", tok_chunk_b)
print("max |scores| diff unchunked image A vs unchunked image B:", (sc_full - sc_full_b).abs().max().item())
print("max |scores| diff unchunked vs chunked:          ", (sc_full - sc_chunk).abs().max().item())
print("max |scores| diff chunked image A vs chunked image B:", (sc_chunk - sc_chunk_b).abs().max().item())
print()
print("expected: one chunked prefill forward receives the image, the chunked tokens match the unchunked")
print("tokens, and changing the image changes the chunked output")
```

Output:

```
python: 3.12.3
transformers: 5.20.1
torch: 2.14.1+cpu

image inputs seen by prefill forwards, unchunked: [['mm_encoder_outputs']]
image inputs seen by prefill forwards, chunked:   [[], [], []]
tokens unchunked:            [52, 45, 10, 49, 57, 2]
tokens unchunked, other image: [52, 45, 10, 49, 57, 2]
tokens chunked:              [52, 45, 10, 20, 51, 46]
tokens chunked, other image: [52, 45, 10, 20, 51, 46]
max |scores| diff unchunked image A vs unchunked image B: 0.009460583329200745
max |scores| diff unchunked vs chunked:           0.2285766303539276
max |scores| diff chunked image A vs chunked image B: 0.0

expected: one chunked prefill forward receives the image, the chunked tokens match the unchunked
tokens, and changing the image changes the chunked output
```

The unchunked run passes the image features (`mm_encoder_outputs`, built from `pixel_values` before prefill) on its first forward, and a different image changes its scores. The chunked run passes them on none of its three prefill forwards, its tokens diverge from the unchunked ones at the fourth step, and swapping in a different image gives exactly the same scores (difference 0.0).

Cause, at main (d4804f9, same lines in v5.20.1): the chunked branch of `_prefill` calls `self.prepare_inputs_for_generation(input_chunk, **model_kwargs)` at `src/transformers/generation/utils.py:4330` without `is_first_iteration`, so it takes the default `False` (line 668). With `use_cache=True`, `prepare_inputs_for_generation` then skips every key in `MULTIMODAL_INPUTS_TO_DROP_OUTSIDE_PREFILL` (lines 761-763, list at 156), which includes `pixel_values` and `mm_encoder_outputs`. The unchunked branch passes `is_first_iteration=is_first_iteration` (line 4297). The chunked code dates from #40652 (v5.0.0). Existing chunked prefill tests only pass `input_ids`, so this is not covered.

### Expected behavior

Chunked and unchunked prefill give the same tokens for the same image, and a different image changes the output.

Proposed fix: pass `is_first_iteration` to the chunked `prepare_inputs_for_generation` call so the multimodal inputs reach the forward that processes their placeholder tokens, or, since the encoder already runs once before prefill, forward `mm_encoder_outputs` on every chunk. A vision-language case in the chunked prefill tests that compares against the unchunked output would cover it. I'm happy to open a PR for it.

### System Info

- `transformers` version: 5.20.1
- Platform: Linux-7.1.5-76070105-generic-x86_64-with-glibc2.39
- Python version: 3.12.3
- Huggingface_hub version: 2.2.0
- Safetensors version: 0.8.0
