body_text:
### Description

The new Keycloak integration test framework (`@KeycloakIntegrationTest`) does not currently expose a clean API to restart the Keycloak server mid-test. Legacy Arquillian tests used `ContainerController` for this.

Several migrated tests previously relied on a mid-test restart. For example, `EntitlementAPITest#testOfflineRequestingPartyToken` used to verify that offline tokens / RPTs survive a server restart. Without a restart API, that coverage is reduced to RPT issuance / introspection / re-authorization with an `offline_access` token only.

### Value Proposition

- Enables migrating tests that require verifying state survival across server restart (offline tokens, caches, persisted sessions, etc.)
- Avoids permanently dropping coverage when moving suites off Arquillian
- Provides a shared capability that multiple test migrations will need

### Goals

- Provide a supported way for integration tests to restart the managed Keycloak server mid-test
- Preserve enough server/test state (or document what is reset) so tests can assert post-restart behavior
- Keep the API usable from Jupiter-based `@KeycloakIntegrationTest` tests

### Non-Goals

- Reintroducing Arquillian `ContainerController` into `tests/base`
- Guaranteeing identical lifecycle semantics to every legacy Arquillian restart scenario without documentation

### Discussion

Raised in https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/pull/51836#discussion_r4105805078

### Notes

Other test migrations are expected to hit the same gap and will either need this API or have to drop coverage.

### Description

`JWSHeader` deserializes `alg` into the closed `org.keycloak.jose.jws.Algorithm` enum (already `@Deprecated`). `JWSInput` therefore fails on any algorithm that is not in the enum, even when a matching `SignatureProvider` / `ClientSignatureVerifierProvider` is deployed.

To reproduce: deploy a `SignatureProviderFactory` + `KeyProvider` for an algorithm `X` that is not in the enum, make it the realm default signature algorithm and obtain a token. Introspection returns `active=false`, userinfo returns 401, logout with `id_token_hint` returns 400. A request object or `private_key_jwt` client assertion signed with `X` is rejected the same way.

### Value Proposition

The `signature`, `keys` and `client-signature` SPIs already look providers up by the string `getRawAlgorithm()`. Only the parsing of the header blocks them. With this change, a new JWS algorithm (national algorithms such as GOST R 34.10-2012 per RFC 7091, or algorithms not yet added to the enum) can be implemented entirely in a provider, without patching `keycloak-core`.

### Goals

- `JWSHeader` keeps `alg` as a string.
- `getAlgorithm()` returns the enum value, or `null` for algorithms not in the enum; `getRawAlgorithm()` returns the original value.
- `TokenVerifier.verifySignature()` without a `SignatureVerifierContext` reports "Unknown or unsupported token algorithm" instead of an NPE.
- Serialization of the header is unchanged.

### Non-Goals

- Adding any new algorithm to Keycloak.
- Removing or changing the `Algorithm` enum.
- Changes to `JWEHeader`.

### Discussion

https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/discussions/53407

### Notes

Overlaps with #50358 (ML-DSA), which also moves header handling to a string algorithm name; happy to rebase on it.

body_text:
### Description

`AccessToken.Confirmation` maps only `x5t#S256`, `jkt` and `kc-jkt-type`, and Keycloak's `ObjectMapper` fails on unknown properties. If a `TokenPostProcessor` adds another confirmation member to `cnf`, Keycloak cannot parse its own token afterwards (introspection, userinfo, refresh): `UnrecognizedPropertyException`.

### Value Proposition

RFC 7800 §3.1 defines `cnf` as extensible, with an IANA "JWT Confirmation Methods" registry. Keeping unknown members lets providers add confirmation methods (for example, a certificate thumbprint computed with a different hash function) without patching `keycloak-core`.

### Goals

- `AccessToken.Confirmation` keeps unknown members in `Map<String, Object> otherClaims` with `@JsonAnySetter` / `@JsonAnyGetter`, the same pattern as `JsonWebToken`.
- Unknown members survive a deserialize → serialize round trip.

### Non-Goals

- Validating or enforcing any additional confirmation method.
- Changes to existing `cnf` members.

### Discussion

https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/discussions/53407

### Notes

body_text: ### Before reporting an issue - [x] I have read and understood the above terms for submitting issues, and I understand that my issue may be closed without action if I do not follow them. ### Area admin/ui ### Describe the bug When `Full Scope Allowed` is disabled for a client, the `Clients → Client Scopes → Evaluate → Effective role scope mappings` tab does not display roles belonging to other clients, even when those roles are granted through an assigned client scope. The following configuration reproduces the issue: - Clients: `test1` and `test2`. - Client roles: `test1/test1` and `test2/test2`. - Realm role: `test`. - User: `test-user`, with all three roles assigned. - Client scope: `test1`, with all three roles added in its Scope tab. The `test1` client scope is assigned to the `test1` client as **Default**. **Full Scope Allowed** is disabled in the dedicated scope of the `test1` client. The user `test-user` has all three roles assigned. When opening `Clients → test1 → Client scopes → Evaluate`, selecting user `test-user`, and checking **Effective role scope mappings**, only the following roles are displayed: - Client role: `test1/test1`. - Realm role: `test`. The client role `test2/test2` is missing. However, the **Generated access token** tab in the same Evaluate view contains all three roles, including the missing `test2/test2`: ```json { "realm_access": { "roles": ["test"] }, "resource_access": { "test2": { "roles": ["test2"] }, "test1": { "roles": ["test1"] } } } ``` This makes the Effective role scope mappings table incomplete: the role from another client is correctly taken into account during token generation but is absent from the displayed scope mappings. ### Version 26.8.0 ### Regression - [ ] The issue is a regression ### Expected behavior Effective role scope mappings should include all roles granted through the assigned client scope: `test1/test1`, `test2/test2`, and realm role `test`. ### Actual behavior Only `test1/test1` and realm role `test` are displayed. `test2/test2` is missing, although it is included in the generated access token. ### How to Reproduce? 1. Create clients `test1` and `test2`. 2. Create client role `test1` in `test1` and client role `test2` in `test2`. 3. Create realm role `test`. 4. Create client scope `test1` and add all three roles in its `Scope` tab. 5. Create user `test-user` and assign all three roles. 6. Assign client scope `test1` to client `test1` as `Default`. 7. Disable `Full Scope Allowed` in the dedicated scope of client `test1`. 8. Open `Clients → test1 → Client Scopes → Evaluate` and select user `test`. 9. Check `Effective role scope mappings`: `test2/test2` is missing. 10. Check Generated access token: all three roles are present. ### Anything else? Related to #53002, which addressed missing roles of the evaluated client. In [EvaluateScopes.tsx](https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/blob/26.8.0/js/apps/admin-ui/src/clients/scopes/EvaluateScopes.tsx#L191-L206), effective role scope mappings are requested only with `roleContainer: realm` and `roleContainer: clientId`. The backend iterates over `roleContainer.getRolesStream()`, so these requests do not return roles belonging to other clients, even when those roles are granted through an assigned client scope.

### Description

### Before reporting an issue

- [x] I searched open and closed issues and reproduced this on the latest release.

### Area

import-export

### Describe the issue

Importing a realm containing a large number of clients can result in significant performance degradation during client creation.

The clients are currently created sequentially while keeping the persistence context active throughout the import. As the number of imported clients increases, the persistence context can grow significantly, affecting the import performance.

This becomes particularly noticeable for realms containing thousands of clients.

### Version

26.4.11 and 26.6.7

### Regression

### Expected behavior

Realm imports containing a large number of clients should maintain reasonable performance as the number of clients increases, without unnecessary growth of the persistence context during client creation.

### Actual behavior

Client creation during realm import is performed using the same persistence context for all clients.

For large realm exports, this can result in significant performance degradation.

### How to Reproduce?

1. Create a realm containing a large number of clients.
2. Export the realm.
3. Import the realm using:

```text
kc.sh import --file=<realm-export.json>
```

4. Observe the time required to complete the client import as the number of clients increases.

### Anything else?

The client import is currently performed in `DefaultExportImportManager.importRealm()` through `createClients()`.

The current implementation processes all clients in a single loop:

```java
for (ClientRepresentation resourceRep : rep.getClients()) {
    ClientModel app = RepresentationToModel.createClient(session, realm, resourceRep, mappedFlows);
    ...
}
```

The user import implementation already uses `EntityManagers.runInBatch(...)` with nested entity managers to keep the parent persistence context clean during large imports.

A similar batching approach for client creation can significantly reduce the persistence context growth while preserving the existing import ordering, since clients must be available before client-dependent data such as role definitions are imported.

The proposed change is to process clients in batches during realm import, using the existing `EntityManagers.runInBatch(...)` mechanism.


### Value Proposition

Improve the performance and scalability of realm imports containing a large number of clients.

This would reduce the impact of persistence context growth during client creation and make large realm imports more predictable as the number of clients increases.

### Goals

- Improve realm import performance when importing large numbers of clients.
- Avoid persistence context growth during client creation.
- Preserve the existing realm import behavior and resulting realm configuration.
- Ensure client-dependent data, such as roles and role mappings, continues to be imported correctly.

### Non-Goals

- Change the behavior or structure of the exported realm representation.
- Change the semantics of client creation or client configuration.
- Change the import order of client-dependent data unless required to preserve the existing behavior.
- Optimize unrelated parts of the realm import process.
- Introduce a new persistence or transaction management mechanism.

### Discussion

_No response_

### Notes

### Description

Currently, it's not possible to enable connection pooling on a ldap user federation, when StartTLS is used.

This means, you can either use plain, unencrypted LDAP or use LDAPS which has long been deprecated in favor of startTLS.

Connection pooling and use of LDAPS/StartTLS should be independent from each other. Connection pooling should work with officially supported StartTLS connection and not only with deprecated LDAPS connections.

### Value Proposition

Support of connection pooling with StartTLS on LDAP

### Goals

Acknowledging deprecation of LDAPS.

### Non-Goals

N/A

### Discussion

_No response_

body_text:
## Description

Keycloak deployments sometimes use database connection proxies (PgBouncer, AWS RDS Proxy, Aurora RDS Proxy) between Keycloak and PostgreSQL. These proxies introduce configuration complexity and trade-offs that are not well documented, leading to hard-to-diagnose issues like those reported in #49515.

This enhancement requests official documentation covering when database proxies are appropriate, required configuration adjustments, and known limitations.

**Note:** The recommendations below are based on architectural analysis and need empirical validation with representative Keycloak workloads before being finalized as official guidance.

## Key findings (to be confirmed)

### Small installations (< 5 pods): Don't use a database proxy

For small Keycloak deployments, Keycloak's built-in Agroal connection pool connecting directly to PostgreSQL is sufficient. A database proxy adds operational complexity, an extra network hop (~0.5-2ms per query), and configuration pitfalls without meaningful benefit. Setting `KC_DB_POOL_MIN_SIZE = KC_DB_POOL_MAX_SIZE` with a capacity matching your load on each pod avoids runtime pool expansion latency, and the total connection count stays well within PostgreSQL's capacity.

### PgBouncer

**Transaction mode** (`pool_mode = transaction`) is the recommended mode for larger deployments. Key requirements:

- **Prepared statements:** PgBouncer < 1.21 requires `prepareThreshold=0` on the JDBC URL, which disables server-side prepared statements. This increases PostgreSQL CPU usage because every query must be re-parsed and re-planned — significant for an OLTP workload like Keycloak that repeatedly executes the same query templates. PgBouncer 1.21+ (released October 2023) supports `max_prepared_statements`, allowing native prepared statement tracking without `prepareThreshold=0`, retaining both connection pooling and low DB CPU usage.
- **XA transactions:** PgBouncer in transaction mode does not support two-phase commit / XA transactions. These must be disabled.
- **JDBC startup parameters:** Some guides recommend `ignore_startup_parameters = extra_float_digits, search_path` in `pgbouncer.ini`. This may be unnecessary if Keycloak's JDBC URL includes `assumeMinServerVersion` (which suppresses the `SET extra_float_digits` command). Needs empirical validation.
- **Pool sizing:** Reduce `KC_DB_POOL_MAX_SIZE` per pod (e.g., 20-30 instead of the default 100). Align `db-pool-max-lifetime` to be lower than PgBouncer's `server_lifetime` and `idle_timeout`.

#### `targetServerType` and PgBouncer failover

Keycloak sets `targetServerType=primary` by default for PostgreSQL connections (see `DatabasePropertyMappers.java`). This causes problems with PgBouncer in front of Patroni-managed clusters: after a Patroni failover, PgBouncer may continue to send stale `in_hot_standby=on` ParameterStatus messages for connections that are now actually primaries. The PostgreSQL JDBC driver then rejects these connections because they don't match `targetServerType=primary`, causing connection failures even though the database is healthy. This is a known problem in pgBouncer for years, see pgbouncer/pgbouncer#859. Hopefully this will eventually be fixed.

Workaround: set `targetServerType=any` in the JDBC URL. However, this disables the driver's primary-detection safety net, so it should only be used when PgBouncer is the single entry point and is already routing to the correct primary. See #49515 for the full discussion and PRs #53355 / #53387 which added initial documentation for this.

### AWS RDS Proxy

RDS Proxy for PostgreSQL triggers **connection pinning** with Keycloak out of the box, which effectively turns the proxy into a 1:1 pass-through and eliminates its pooling benefits:

1. **Prepared statements** — RDS Proxy pins the session on any prepared statement (both SQL-level `PREPARE` and JDBC Extended Query Protocol). Since Keycloak/Hibernate uses parameterized prepared statements for virtually every query, the first query pins the connection.
2. **SET commands** — The PostgreSQL JDBC driver issues session-level `SET` commands during initialization (e.g., `SET extra_float_digits`), which also triggers pinning.

To avoid pinning, the JDBC URL must include:
```
prepareThreshold=0&assumeMinServerVersion=9.0
```
This forces simple protocol queries (higher DB CPU) and suppresses startup `SET` commands. Even with this configuration, RDS Proxy provides less benefit than PgBouncer 1.21+ because prepared statement efficiency cannot be retained.

Monitor Pinning Metrics: Monitor the `DatabaseConnectionsCurrentlySessionPinned` metric in Amazon CloudWatch. A high number of pinned connections indicates that client sessions are bypassing multiplexing and holding onto dedicated database backends.

#### AWS Advanced JDBC Wrapper and RDS Proxy

Keycloak already documents and supports the [AWS Advanced JDBC Wrapper](https://github.com/awslabs/aws-advanced-jdbc-wrapper) (`software.amazon.jdbc.Driver`) for Aurora PostgreSQL Multi-AZ failover (see `db.adoc`, "Preparing for Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL"). Keycloak automatically disables `targetServerType=primary` when the wrapper driver is detected (`DatabasePropertyMappers.java`).

However, the wrapper's plugins are designed to communicate **directly with Aurora instances**, not through RDS Proxy. When RDS Proxy sits between the wrapper and Aurora:

- **Failover plugin (`failover`/`failover2`):** Conflicts with RDS Proxy, which already handles failover at the proxy layer. The wrapper tries to detect and react to failovers independently, leading to double failover handling, incorrect host resolution, and connection errors.
- **Host monitoring plugin:** Sends probe queries to detect host health, but these hit the proxy endpoint rather than actual Aurora instances, making them ineffective or counterproductive.
- **Read/write splitting plugin:** Routes queries to reader/writer endpoints, but RDS Proxy already manages this routing. Using both results in conflicting routing decisions.

**Bottom line:** Use the AWS JDBC Wrapper with direct Aurora connections (as currently documented) **or** use RDS Proxy — but not both together. If using RDS Proxy, connect with the standard PostgreSQL JDBC driver and the pinning mitigations described above. This incompatibility should be explicitly documented alongside the existing wrapper setup instructions in `db.adoc`. Needs empirical validation.

### Traffic spikes and scaling

A common argument for database proxies is protection against "connection storms" during autoscaling. In practice:
- Agroal opens connections sequentially per instance, not as a burst.
- Kubernetes rolling updates proceed pod by pod (bounded by `maxSurge`).
- Keycloak pods should be deployed as StatefulSets, which scale sequentially (one pod at a time), further reducing any connection burst.

The more practical concern is **aggregate static pool size**: with many pods, the total number of permanent PostgreSQL backend processes grows linearly (pods × pool size), even at idle. PostgreSQL performance degrades when managing hundreds of backend processes (optimal is typically 100-200 depending on CPU cores). A proxy helps here by multiplexing to a smaller backend pool. However, deployments running at that scale (30+ pods, millions of users, tens of thousands of requests per second) are large enough to warrant dedicated database capacity planning regardless.

But during a traffic spike, the proxy itself can become the bottleneck if its backend pool is too small — you'd be better off scaling down `KC_DB_POOL_MAX_SIZE` per instance and connecting directly.

## Requested enhancement

Add a server guide section covering:
1. When a database proxy is and isn't recommended
2. Required Keycloak JDBC configuration for PgBouncer (by version) and RDS Proxy
3. `targetServerType` considerations when using PgBouncer with Patroni or similar HA setups
4. AWS JDBC Wrapper vs. RDS Proxy — use one or the other, not both
5. Connection pool sizing guidance when using a proxy
6. Known limitations and trade-offs (prepared statement CPU overhead, XA incompatibility, RDS Proxy pinning)

All recommendations need empirical validation with representative Keycloak workloads before being published as official guidance.

Relates to #49515

However, deployments running at that scale (30+ pods, millions of users, tens of thousands of requests per second) are large enough to warrant dedicated database capacity planning regardless.

But during a traffic spike, the proxy itself can become the bottleneck if its backend pool is too small — you'd be better off scaling down `KC_DB_POOL_MAX_SIZE` per instance and connecting directly.

## Requested enhancement

Add a server guide section covering:
1. When a database proxy is and isn't recommended
2. Required Keycloak JDBC configuration for PgBouncer (by version) and RDS Proxy
3. `targetServerType` considerations when using PgBouncer with Patroni or similar HA setups
4. AWS JDBC Wrapper vs. RDS Proxy — use one or the other, not both
5. Connection pool sizing guidance when using a proxy
6. Known limitations and trade-offs (prepared statement CPU overhead, XA incompatibility, RDS Proxy pinning)

All recommendations need empirical validation with representative Keycloak workloads before being published as official guidance.

### Before reporting an issue

- [x] I have read and understood the above terms for submitting issues, and I understand that my issue may be closed without action if I do not follow them.

### Area

oidc

### Describe the bug

A `POST` to the OIDC authorization endpoint (`/realms/{realm}/protocol/openid-connect/auth`) with a `multipart/form-data` body containing a **file part** causes an uncaught `java.lang.RuntimeException: Form value is a file`, returned to the caller as HTTP 500 `{"error":"unknown_error"}`. No authentication or valid client is required. A graceful HTTP 400 `invalid_request` is expected instead.

### Version

26.8.0

### Regression

- [ ] The issue is a regression

### Expected behavior

Unexpected/malformed form input — a file part where string form fields are expected — is rejected with HTTP 400 `invalid_request`, not an uncaught 500.

### Actual behavior

HTTP 500 with body:
`{"error":"unknown_error","error_description":"For more on this error consult the server log."}`

Server log:
```
ERROR [org.keycloak.services.error.KeycloakErrorHandler] (executor-thread-1) Uncaught server error: java.lang.RuntimeException: Form value is a file
	at org.jboss.resteasy.reactive.server.core.multipart.FormData$FormValueImpl.getValue(FormData.java:298)
	at org.keycloak.quarkus.runtime.integration.resteasy.QuarkusHttpRequest.getDecodedFormParameters(QuarkusHttpRequest.java:84)
	at org.keycloak.protocol.oidc.endpoints.AuthorizationEndpoint.buildPost(AuthorizationEndpoint.java:118)
```

### How to Reproduce?

1. Start Keycloak 26.8.0: `docker run -p 8080:8080 -e KC_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_USERNAME=admin -e KC_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD=admin quay.io/keycloak/keycloak:latest start-dev`
2. Send a multipart `POST` with a file part to the authorization endpoint:
```
echo 'dummy' | curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' \
  -X POST 'http://localhost:8080/realms/master/protocol/openid-connect/auth?response_type=code&client_id=account&redirect_uri=http%3A%2F%2Flocalhost%2Fcb&scope=openid%20profile&state=test' \
  -F 'evil=@-;filename=x.txt;type=application/octet-stream'
```
3. Observe HTTP 500 and the `Form value is a file` stack trace in the server log. (The OAuth query params are incidental — the file part alone triggers it.)

### Anything else?

Discovered when a generic web-vulnerability scanner POSTed `multipart/form-data` to a production authorization endpoint and generated a burst of 500s. Impact is availability/log-noise only — no auth bypass, no data exposure.

Follow-up of https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/issues/53170 .

This task is for removal of deprecated client switch 'Use refresh tokens for client credentials grant' .

After this change, the service-account (OAuth2 client credentials grant) will never use refresh tokens and hence will never create new user session.

The related documentation should be updated as well (Upgrading guide, some pieces in Server-admin guide like `transient.adoc` file) etc.

### Description

This is follow-up of https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/issues/53219 .

Deprecated client registration providers others than OIDC provider should be removed in KC 27.

It may also affect some client-registration policies and client policies. For example, client registration policies like `ProtocolMappersClientRegistrationPolicy` are likely not applicable for the OIDC client registration as injecting custom protocol-mappers was only the feature specific to registering client of Keycloak JSON representation (class `ClientRepresentation`). So maybe this client-registration policy can be removed as well? There are likely more such cases. With client-policies, it is more tricky as those might be also used during REST API requests, but this may be checked as well.


This will affect documentation and testsuite as well.

### Description

There are some workarounds added around hibernate that will no longer be necessary with Hibernate 7.4.11 / 8. 

https://hibernate.atlassian.net/browse/HHH-20826
https://hibernate.atlassian.net/browse/HHH-20861
https://hibernate.atlassian.net/browse/HHH-20863

At the time of writing this, Quarkus 3.40.1 is using Hibernate 7.4.7

The workarounds have been part of the following commits: 

6d5d3c0c3032c9ff846f8b1ed8b4db0edf48ee32 - log suppresion should no longer be necessary
24523a296b2387d969efbf95242dafd117f66651 - log suppresion should no longer be necessary 
0e9b3f70e8afec3c7e79599b7a0605f66c4f5a15 - the custom dialect should no longer be necessary

Note that https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/issues/54240 introduced one more fix/workaround that is not yet present in 7.4.11  - so the custom dialect might stay, and would need another follow-up issue.

body_text: ### Before reporting an issue - [x] I have read and understood the above terms for submitting issues, and I understand that my issue may be closed without action if I do not follow them. ### Area login/ui ### Describe the bug The message `clientDelegationScopeConsentText` is "Allow {0} to act on your behalf?" and takes the actor client as its parameter. `keycloak.v2/login/login-oauth-grant.ftl` passes the parameter: ``` ${advancedMsg(clientScope.consentScreenText, clientScope.parameterizedScopeParameter)} ``` `base/login/login-oauth-grant.ftl` — used by the `keycloak` (v1) login theme and by any custom theme whose parent is `keycloak` or `base` — was not updated and still renders: ``` ${advancedMsg(clientScope.consentScreenText)}: ${clientScope.parameterizedScopeParameter} ``` so the placeholder is never filled in. ### Version 26.8.0 ### Regression - [ ] The issue is a regression ### Expected behavior "Allow agent-x to act on your behalf?" — the same sentence the `keycloak.v2` theme shows. ### Actual behavior "Allow {0} to act on your behalf?: agent-x" ### How to Reproduce? 1. Start Keycloak 26.8.0 with the preview feature `token-exchange-delegation` enabled. 2. Set the realm's login theme to `keycloak` (v1), or to a custom theme with `parent=keycloak`. 3. Use a client with consent required and request `scope=openid delegation:client:agent-x`, where `agent-x` is another client in the realm. 4. Sign in. The consent page shows the raw `{0}`. ### Anything else? The fix looks like the same one-line change already made in the `keycloak.v2` template. If the v1 template is no longer maintained, a note in the delegation documentation would spare custom-theme authors the surprise.

# Description
In Eclipse Parsson published Maven Central artifacts before version 1.1.8, the JSON parser did not enforce a default maximum on the number of characters consumed while parsing a single JSON document. Applications that parse attacker- controlled JSON can be forced to consume excessive CPU and memory by processing very large documents, including large arrays, objects, strings, numbers, whitespace, or nested structures, resulting in a denial of service. Eclipse Parsson 1.1.8 introduces a configurable maximum parsing limit with a default limit of 15 million parser-consumed characters.

### Before reporting an issue

- [x] I have read and understood the above terms for submitting issues, and I understand that my issue may be closed without action if I do not follow them.

### Area

identity-brokering

### Describe the bug
When logging out from my application, the user ends up on an error page. Even though the logout browser flow is interrupted, the user is actually logged out from everywhere.

The server log when the error happens:
```
ERROR [org.keycloak.broker.oidc.OIDCIdentityProvider] (executor-thread-10) no valid user session
WARN  [org.keycloak.events] (executor-thread-10) type="LOGOUT_ERROR", realmId="7fee4e8a-97aa-4aab-ac92-e7400270f4f1", realmName="main", clientId="null", userId="null", ipAddress="xxx.xxx.xxx.xxx", error="user_session_not_found"
```

It seems like the backchannel logout terminates the session before the front channel logout finishes. Then when the front channel logout comes back, the session cannot be found anymore.

IdP-initiated logout from the external IdP works as expected.

### Setup
Application --(OIDC)--> `main` realm --(Keycloak OIDC)--> `broker` realm --(SAML)--> external IdP

- App OIDC client in `main`:
  - Front channel logout: off
  - Backchannel logout logout URL: application logout url
  - Backchannel logout session required: on
- Broker realm Keycloak OIDC IdP in `main`: 
  - Backchannel logout: off
  - Logout URL: `https://my-idp.example.com/realms/broker/protocol/openid-connect/logout`
- Main realm OIDC client in `broker`: 
  - Front channel logout: off
  - Backchannel logout logout URL: `https://my-idp.example.com/realms/main/protocol/openid-connect/logout/backchannel-logout`
  - Backchannel logout session required: on
- External SAML IdP in `broker`:
  - Backchannel logout: off

We need broker realms for external identity providers, because we have several of them and they all need separate signing and encryption keys.

### Version

26.5.3

### Regression

- [ ] The issue is a regression

### Expected behavior

The user is logged out from all realms and the external IdP and redirected back to the application without any errors

### Actual behavior

The user is logged out from all realms and the external IdP but the browser ends up on an error page when redirecting back to application

### How to Reproduce?

1. Log in to the application with the IdP of the broker realm
2. Log out from the application

### Anything else?

If I set `Backchannel logout session required` off, then the error goes away, but then the IdP-initiated logout does not work.

body_text:
### Description

When migrating from legacy V1 token exchange (external-to-internal) to the new V2 JWT Authorization Grant (urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:jwt-bearer), identity provider mappers configured on the external IdP are ignored.  This is affecting some customers who are trying to migrate to v2. 

In V1 token exchange, Keycloak ran the Identity Provider's configured mappers on incoming external tokens. In V2 (JWT Authorization Grant), Keycloak ignores all mappers and only looks for an existing linked user. Because no mappers run, several critical customer use cases are broken:I

1. Customers cannot dynamically link incoming external identities to existing Keycloak user accounts at request time. If the link does not already exist, the request simply fails with "User not found".
2. Assigning roles or attributes (e.g., Hardcoded Role Mapper): Standard IdP mappers configured in the Admin Console (such as assigning default roles or mapping claims to user attributes based on the external IdP) do not execute.
3. Subject and alias transformation: In environments where the external token's subject identifier needs to be transformed or sanitized before matching the local account, there is no way to adapt the identity.

### Value Proposition

Enables customers with external identity federation workflows to migrate from deprecated V1 token exchange to the standards-based RFC 7523 JWT Authorization Grant without losing essential user provisioning, auto-linking, and role/attribute mapping capabilities.

### Goals

Support running Identity Provider mappers during the JWT Authorization Grant flow.
Allow dynamic matching/linking of external identities to existing Keycloak users.
Ensure configured IdP mappers (e.g., role, attribute, and claim mappers) apply when exchanging external JWT assertions.

### Non-Goals

Changing the deprecated V1 token exchange flow.

### Discussion

_No response_

### Notes

_No response_

### Before reporting an issue

- [x] I have read and understood the above terms for submitting issues, and I understand that my issue may be closed without action if I do not follow them.

### Area

storage

### Describe the bug

Adding a group supplied by a `GroupStorageProvider` to a local user fails when the group's federated storage ID exceeds 36 characters.

This is not specific to service-account users. It affects any local user whose membership is persisted through the JPA `UserAdapter`.

### Version

26.7.4

### Regression

- [ ] The issue is a regression

### Expected behavior

A valid group returned by `GroupStorageProvider` should be assignable to a local user, and the user should be returned when listing the group's members.

If this relationship is unsupported, Keycloak should reject it before attempting the database write instead of returning HTTP 500.

### Actual behavior


The request returns HTTP 500. PostgreSQL reports:

```text
ERROR: value too long for type character varying(36)
insert into USER_GROUP_MEMBERSHIP (MEMBERSHIP_TYPE, GROUP_ID, USER_ID) values (?, ?, ?)
```



### How to Reproduce?


1. Configure a `GroupStorageProvider` that returns a group whose ID uses the standard `StorageId` format:

   ```java
   new StorageId(component.getId(), externalGroupId).getId()
   ```

2. Create the component without explicitly supplying an ID, and create a local user.
3. Add the provider-backed group to that user through the Admin REST API:

   ```text
   PUT /admin/realms/{realm}/users/{local-user-id}/groups/{url-encoded-group-id}
   ```

`StorageId` renders a federated ID as:

```text
f:<component-id>:<external-id>
```

A component created without an ID receives a 36-character UUID. Therefore even a one-character external group ID produces a 40-character group ID:

```text
f:<36-character-component-id>:g
```

### Anything else?


### Relevant Implementation

This remains present in the latest release, Keycloak 26.7.4.

`StorageId` defines the `f:<provider-id>:<external-id>` representation:

https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/blob/26.7.4/server-spi/src/main/java/org/keycloak/storage/StorageId.java#L46-L60

When no component ID is supplied, the JPA realm implementation generates a standard 36-character UUID:

https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/blob/26.7.4/model/jpa/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/jpa/RealmAdapter.java#L2131-L2151

The local JPA user path accepts any `GroupModel` and persists `group.getId()` as the membership's `GROUP_ID`:

https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/blob/26.7.4/model/jpa/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/jpa/UserAdapter.java#L461-L481

However, the Liquibase schema limits `USER_GROUP_MEMBERSHIP.GROUP_ID` to `VARCHAR(36)`:

https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/blob/26.7.4/model/jpa/src/main/resources/META-INF/jpa-changelog-1.7.0.xml#L50-L57

`FED_USER_GROUP_MEMBERSHIP.GROUP_ID` has the same 36-character limit, so the equivalent JPA federated-user membership path appears affected as well:

https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/blob/26.7.4/model/jpa/src/main/resources/META-INF/jpa-changelog-2.1.0.xml#L121-L132

### Suggested Fix

Add a database migration that widens `GROUP_ID` in both `USER_GROUP_MEMBERSHIP` and `FED_USER_GROUP_MEMBERSHIP` to a length compatible with federated `StorageId` values, such as `VARCHAR(255)`. Consider widening the related group-ID fields above as part of the same audit.

A regression test could use the existing `HardcodedGroupStorageProvider`, add its group to a local user, and verify that listing the group's members returns that user.

### Before reporting an issue - [x] I have read and understood the above terms for submitting issues, and I understand that my issue may be closed without action if I do not follow them. ### Area storage ### Describe the bug Keycloak 26.8.0 breaks support for multi-tenancy in custom persistence units defined in `META‑INF/persistence.xml` (which is the recommended/supported way). The root cause seems to be that Quarkus 3.40.1 (on which Keycloak 26.8.0 is based) hardcodes the multi-tenancy setting to `none` here: [HibernateOrmProcessor.java:535](https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/blob/3.40.1/extensions/hibernate-orm/deployment/src/main/java/io/quarkus/hibernate/orm/deployment/HibernateOrmProcessor.java#L535). However this code path is only taken for persistence units defined in `META‑INF/persistence.xml`, notably it is _not_ taken for persistence units defined in Quarkus properties. Having no other choice (and encouraged by the fact that Keycloak's own persistence unit is now defined in Quarkus properties too), we set out to do just that: Refactor our custom PU definition to Quarkus properties. Here is a brief summary of the things we tried and the problems we encountered: | Attempt # | Attempt highlights | Issues encountered | | :-- | :-- | :-- | | 1 |
  • our custom PU defined in Quarkus properties
  • no `quarkus.hibernate‑orm.*.packages` property defined
|
  • `kc.sh build` fails with the following error:
    Multiple persistence units are defined but the entities are not mapped to them. You should either use the .packages Quarkus configuration property or package-level @PersistenceUnit annotations.
| | 2 |
  • added `quarkus.hibernate‑orm."our‑pu".packages` property
|
  • `kc.sh build` fails with the following error:
    Packages must be configured for the default persistence unit.
| | 3 |
  • replaced the `quarkus.hibernate‑orm."our‑pu".packages` property with the `@PersistenceUnit("our‑pu")` annotation
|
  • `kc.sh build` issues warning:
    Could not find a suitable persistence unit for model classes/packages:
    followed by a list of all Keycloak entity classes
  • Keycloak fails to start with the following exception:
    org.hibernate.UnknownEntityTypeException: Unknown entity type 'org.keycloak.storage.configuration.jpa.entity.ServerConfigEntity'
| | 4 |
  • revreted to defining the `quarkus.hibernate‑orm."our‑pu".packages` property
  • additionally defined the `quarkus.hibernate‑orm.packages=org.keycloak` property
| None, `kc.sh build` finishes without errors/warnings, Keycloak starts, our custom PU works, yay! | While we were eventually able to make it work, the process was not smooth and we are still not happy about having to provide additional configuration for the Keycloak default persistence unit - namely the: ``` quarkus.hibernate‑orm.packages=org.keycloak ``` setting. In our opinion this should be the responsibility of Keycloak. ### Version 26.8.0 ### Regression - [x] The issue is a regression ### Expected behavior Multi-tenancy for custom PUs is supported (at least for PUs defined in Quarkus properties). Defining custom PUs in Quarkus properties is officially supported. ### Actual behavior Multi-tenancy for custom PUs defined in the recommended/supported `META‑INF/persistence.xml` is not possible. Multi-tenancy for custom PUs defined in Quarkus properties is possible, but adding a custom PU this way (irrespective of its multi-tenancy setting) hinges on providing additional configuration for the Keycloak default PU, which makes the process cumbersome. ### How to Reproduce? 1. In your provider define a custom PU in `META‑INF/persistence.xml` and configure it for multi-tenancy by setting its `hibernate.multiTenancy` property to an appropriate value. (We use `DATABASE`.) 2. Integrate the provider to Keycloak, then try starting Keycloak and exercising the multi-tenancy. (Keycloak doesn't start for us complaining about a missing datasource, a datasource which is not supposed to be used in the multi-tenancy setup.) ### Anything else? From what I can see, the issue may already be fixed on the Quarkus side, but it still makes a strong case for adding official (hassle-free) support for custom PUs defined in Quarkus properties. A major prerequisite for that is fixing the configuration of the Keycloak default PU so that it doesn't cause problems when a custom PU is added.

### Description

We frequently have merge conflicts due to the fact that any PR updating the release docs, upgrade docs, or migrations, modify the same file as other PRs. This frequently results in merge conflicts, especially in the keycloak-private repository.

When backporting PRs to release branches it also requires modifying the files as for example upgrade guide changes for `26.8.0` would go into `26.7.5`. Same applies to release notes and migrations.

Ideally we would have all changes into files like `changes-next-<change id>.adoc`, and at the time of release we would rename these to whatever release is happening. For example `changes-next-mychange.adoc` could go into upgrade guide 27.0.0 from main when the release/27.0 branch is created, and go into 26.7.5 when the 26.7.5 tag is created.

This process would have to be fully automated, as we can't expect release coordinators to do this manually.

### Description

When a custom identity provider extends `OIDCIdentityProvider` / `OIDCIdentityProviderFactory`, creating it in the admin console opens the generic `AddIdentityProvider` page instead of `AddOpenIdConnect`. 

Because of this, the create form for a custom OIDC provider is missing:
- The **Discovery endpoint** field, so the endpoints can't be imported from `.well-known/openid-configuration`
- The **Client authentication** field
- The **Client assertion signature algorithm** field

After the provider has been created, the details page does show the full OIDC settings, because `DetailSettings.tsx` checks the provider ID with a substring match:

```tsx
const isOIDC = provider.providerId!.includes("oidc");
```

The create flow, however, only uses `AddOpenIdConnect` for the exact provider IDs `oidc` and `keycloak-oidc`.

### Value Proposition

- Custom OIDC-based providers are a common extension point. Their admins should get the same create experience as the built-in OpenID Connect provider, including discovery.
- It removes the current workarounds: creating the provider first and configuring it afterwards, re-implementing discovery and endpoint fields in `getConfigProperties()`, calling `/identity-provider/import-config` by hand, or changing `provider_id` in the database.
- It makes the create page consistent with the details page, which already treats any provider ID containing `oidc` as OIDC.

### Goals

- When the selected provider is OIDC-based, the Add flow renders `OIDCGeneralSettings`, `OpenIdConnectSettings` (including the Discovery endpoint) and `OIDCAuthentication` for custom provider IDs too.
- Custom config properties from the factory (`getConfigProperties()`) are still rendered on the OIDC Add page, so custom fields keep working.

### Non-Goals

- Doing the same for custom SAML or OAuth2 providers. That could be a follow-up using the same approach.
- Adding a general-purpose plugin mechanism for replacing admin UI pages.

### Discussion

### Description

Follow-up for the https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/issues/52792

Move the Authenticator Reference property definitions entirely server-side and expose them through `authentication/config-description/{providerId}`.

The Admin UI currently hardcodes `default.reference.value` and `default.reference.maxAge` in `ExecutionConfigModal.tsx`. Because these definitions were absent from server-side metadata, secret masking incorrectly treated their values as secrets, causing #52792.

PR #53361 introduces server-side common property definitions to fix masking. It deliberately leaves exposing those definitions through `config-description` and removing the UI duplication for a follow-up, keeping the regression fix suitable for backporting.

### Value Proposition

Use the same server-side property definitions for configuration discovery, UI rendering, and secret masking. This removes duplicated metadata and makes the common properties discoverable by Admin REST API consumers.

### Goals

- Include the common Authenticator Reference properties in configuration descriptions alongside provider-specific properties.
- Remove the hardcoded property definitions and merging logic from the Admin UI.
- Preserve access to these fields for non-flow executions whose factories report `isConfigurable() == false`, such as Cookie.
- Preserve existing field order, translations, configuration keys, and save/reopen behavior.
- Avoid duplicate property names and preserve explicit provider definitions when names overlap.
- Update API coverage and verify UI behavior for configurable and non-configurable authenticators.

### Non-Goals

- Change AMR claim generation or reference expiration behavior.
- Change stored configuration values or require a data migration.
- Change factory `isConfigurable()` semantics.
- Add Authenticator Reference fields to subflows.
- Expand the scope of the backportable masking fix in #53361.

### Discussion

_No response_

### Notes

The configuration-description endpoint currently returns only `getConfigProperties()`. It could combine those properties with `ConfigurableAuthenticatorFactory.COMMON_CONFIG_PROPERTIES`, handling null provider lists and resolving duplicate names consistently with secret masking.

The Admin UI currently fetches descriptions only when `execution.configurable` is true. It would need to fetch them for every non-flow execution so that authenticators without provider-specific configuration still expose the common fields.

Existing translation keys can remain in the Admin UI message bundles, since the dynamic form components already translate server-provided labels and help text.

Coordinate the server and UI changes: an older UI would inject duplicate fields against the updated endpoint, while an updated UI would need a fallback if support for older servers is required.

### Before reporting an issue

- [x] I have read and understood the above terms for submitting issues, and I understand that my issue may be closed without action if I do not follow them.

### Area

docs

### Describe the bug

The latest upgrading guide (the 26.8 guide, since 26.8.0 was released on 2026-10-01) lists only 2 of the 4 upgrade notes for 26.7.5. The 26.7.5 guide has all 4.

- Latest: https://www.keycloak.org/docs/latest/upgrading/index.html#migrating-to-26-7-5
- 26.7.5: https://www.keycloak.org/docs/26.7.5/upgrading/index.html#migrating-to-26-7-5

| 26.7.5 upgrade note | 26.7.5 guide | latest guide |
|---|---|---|
| Client policy source groups condition matches the full group path (breaking) | yes | yes |
| `OrganizationProvider#getByAlias` no longer has a default implementation (breaking) | yes | yes |
| Disabled clients are no longer added to the token audience (breaking, CVE-2026-93999) | yes | **missing** |
| Certificate Common Name truncated to 64 characters (notable) | yes | **missing** |

In the latest guide, the two missing items appear only under "Migrating to 26.8.0".

Cause: `docs/documentation/upgrading/topics/changes/changes-26_7_5.adoc` on `main`, `release/26.8` and the `26.8.0` tag comes from fca8fe793d (2026-09-22, "Release notes and upgrading guide for 26.8"). The two missing entries were added to the 26.7.5 notes only on the 26.7 release branch, on 2026-09-30:
- 76e0e7637b "Ignore audience for disabled and removed clients (#53244)"
- 9ac6c30f0a "BACKPORT: Truncate certificate CN to 64 characters per RFC 5280 (#51779) (#53360)"

On `main` and 26.8 they were added only to `changes-26_8_0.adoc`.

### Version

26.8.0 (latest docs); 26.7.5

### Regression

- [ ] The issue is a regression

### Expected behavior

The latest guide's "Migrating to 26.7.5" section contains all 26.7.5 upgrade notes, the same as the 26.7.5 guide.

### Actual behavior

Two of the four notes are missing, one of them a breaking change tied to a CVE. Someone upgrading within 26.7.x (e.g. 26.7.4 → 26.7.5) who reads the latest guide won't see that disabled clients are dropped from the token `aud` claim.

### How to Reproduce?

1. Open https://www.keycloak.org/docs/26.7.5/upgrading/index.html#migrating-to-26-7-5 and note the 4 entries.
2. Open https://www.keycloak.org/docs/latest/upgrading/index.html#migrating-to-26-7-5; only 2 entries are there.
3. Compare `changes-26_7_5.adoc` at tag `26.7.5` with the same file on `main` or at `26.8.0`.

### Anything else?

Probably related to #53581, which discusses how upgrade docs should handle backports. Whatever is decided there, the latest guide currently shows a 26.7.5 section that looks complete but isn't.

There's also drift in the opposite direction for 26.7.1: the `<TODO>` placeholders from #52940 are gone from the latest guide but still in `changes-26_7_1.adoc` on the 26.7 branch, so `/docs/26.7.5/` still shows them.

body_text:
### Description

Many identity provider support some concept of tenants. 

For example Google allows sending the `hd` param in the auth request, which will also be included in the returned tokens. Keycloak supports the `Hosted Domain` option for Google, but does not have a generic mechanism that can be used with other providers.

There's a [draft specification](https://openid.github.io/connect-enterprise-extensions/main.html#name-tenant) around this, but it's been draft for a while and even if it was made final it would take some time before all providers would support it.

It should be possible to configure a tenant when setting up any IdP that supports a tenant concept. In reality that means providing 3 configuration options:

* The tenant id
* An optional query parameter to send the tenant id when doing an auth request to the provider
* The claim name to verify in the tokens issued by the provider

Specific providers that we have like Google would set hard-code these so only the tenant id would have to be configurable.

When adding support for tenants we would need to make sure that all use-cases such as user federation, client federation, and authorization grants, verify the claim.

### Value Proposition

In many use-cases only a specific tenant should be permitted to authenticate with Keycloak, by limiting this to the required tenant it prevents other users/clients in the provider from authenticated with Keycloak, which increases security.

### Goals

* Support a configurable tenant concept for the generic OIDC provider
* Leverage the above in all specific providers that have a tenant concept where the parameter name and claim name is known, allowing only configuring the tenant id.

### Non-Goals

* Add generic support for verifying any claim; this will be limited to a single claim aka tenants use-case.

### Discussion

### Description

Hello,

I’m working on OAuth authentication for my company’s MCP server. While customizing Keycloak’s OAuth consent page, I found that the stock FreeMarker context does not expose the validated redirect URI or its hostname.

The [MCP authorization security considerations](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/authorization/security-considerations) state that authorization servers:
- **MUST** clearly display the redirect URI hostname during authorization.
- **SHOULD** display additional warnings for localhost-only redirect URIs.

The consent page receives an OAuth-specific `oauth` object and a `url` object, but neither appears to provide the active redirect URI. The URI may be present in the `client_data` query parameter, encoded as base64 JSON (for example, in its `ru` field). However, I’m not sure that value is bound to the redirect URI validated and stored for the active authentication session. Reading it directly from the browser URL could therefore show a value that does not match the session.

Could Keycloak expose the **validated redirect URI**, or at least its hostname, to the OAuth consent template? This would let themes display the callback host and warn users when the callback uses localhost, without relying on an unverified query parameter.

Relevant Keycloak source:
- [Base OAuth grant template](https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/blob/26.8.0/themes/src/main/resources/theme/base/login/login-oauth-grant.ftl)
- [FreeMarker login forms provider](https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/blob/26.8.0/services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/forms/login/freemarker/FreeMarkerLoginFormsProvider.java)
- [Authentication session model](https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/blob/26.8.0/server-spi/src/main/java/org/keycloak/sessions/AuthenticationSessionModel.java)

### Value Proposition

Exposing the validated redirect URI would let consent themes show users which host will receive the authorization response. It would also let themes warn users when the callback uses localhost, without trusting an unverified query parameter.

### Goals

- Make the active, validated redirect URI available to the OAuth consent template.
- Let themes display its hostname and identify localhost-only callbacks.

### Non-Goals

- Change how Keycloak validates redirect URIs.
- Change OAuth consent, approval, or redirect behavior.

### Discussion

https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/discussions/53792

The [MCP authorization security considerations](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/authorization/security-considerations) state that authorization servers:
- **MUST** clearly display the redirect URI hostname during authorization.
- **SHOULD** display additional warnings for localhost-only redirect URIs.

The consent page receives an OAuth-specific `oauth` object and a `url` object, but neither appears to provide the active redirect URI. The URI may be present in the `client_data` query parameter, encoded as base64 JSON (for example, in its `ru` field). However, I’m not sure that value is bound to the redirect URI validated and stored for the active authentication session. Reading it directly from the browser URL could therefore show a value that does not match the session.

Could Keycloak expose the **validated redirect URI**, or at least its hostname, to the OAuth consent template? This would let themes display the callback host and warn users when the callback uses localhost, without relying on an unverified query parameter.

### Non-Goals

- Change OAuth consent, approval, or redirect behavior.

### Before reporting an issue

- [X] I have read and understood the above terms for submitting issues, and I understand that my issue may be closed without action if I do not follow them.

### Area

dist/quarkus

### Describe the bug

`kc.sh build` writes different bytecode into `lib/quarkus/generated-bytecode.jar` each time it runs with the same inputs. Images that run `kc.sh build` get a new digest on each build.

Two recorded classes change between runs:

- `KeycloakProcessor$configureKeycloakSessionFactory*.class`: the order of SPIs and providers changes. The `factories` and `defaultProviders` maps in `KeycloakProcessor` are `HashMap`s with `Spi` and `Class` keys. These keys use identity hash codes, which change in each JVM.
- `KeycloakProcessor$prepareKeycloakLogFilter*.class`: the order of the Hibernate property names changes. `KeycloakLogFilter.collectAllDefaultUnsupportedHibernateProperties()` uses `Collectors.toUnmodifiableSet()`. The iteration order of this set changes in each JVM.

The Quarkus [reproducibility guide](https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/blob/main/REPRODUCIBILITY.md#use-collections-with-a-stable-iteration-order) gives both patterns as causes of unstable recorded bytecode.

### Version

26.8.0

### Regression

- [ ] The issue is a regression

### Expected behavior

With the same inputs, `kc.sh build` writes the same `lib/quarkus` files.

### Actual behavior

`generated-bytecode.jar` is different after each build. Two builds of the Dockerfile below:

```console
$ diff -rq g1 g2
Files g1/io/quarkus/runner/recorded/KeycloakProcessor$configureKeycloakSessionFactory1939554146.class and g2/io/quarkus/runner/recorded/KeycloakProcessor$configureKeycloakSessionFactory1939554146.class differ
Files g1/io/quarkus/runner/recorded/KeycloakProcessor$prepareKeycloakLogFilter2020436198.class and g2/io/quarkus/runner/recorded/KeycloakProcessor$prepareKeycloakLogFilter2020436198.class differ
```

### How to Reproduce?

1. Save this Dockerfile. The two `-D` options make the jar timestamps fixed, so that only the bytecode differs.

   ```dockerfile
   FROM quay.io/keycloak/keycloak:26.8.0 AS build
   ARG RUN
   RUN JAVA_OPTS_APPEND="-Dquarkus.package.output-timestamp=2000-01-01T00:00:00Z -Djava.properties.date=2000-01-01" \
       /opt/keycloak/bin/kc.sh build --features=docker,authorization

   FROM scratch
   COPY --from=build /opt/keycloak/lib/quarkus /quarkus
   ```

2. Build it two times and compare the generated classes:

   ```sh
   for i in 1 2; do
     docker buildx build --build-arg RUN=$i --output type=local,dest=out$i .
     mkdir g$i && (cd g$i && unzip -q ../out$i/quarkus/generated-bytecode.jar)
   done
   diff -rq g1 g2
   ```

### Anything else?

The same code is on `main`.

### Description

Sub-task of #53271.

#### Problem

The logic to list, search, and remove role mappings exists twice in the server. The Admin API implements it in `RoleMapperResource`, `ScopeMappedResource`, `RoleByIdResource`, and `RoleContainerResource`, subject to `RolePermissionEvaluator`. The Admin Console does not use those endpoints when assigning roles to users, groups, clients, client scopes, and composite roles; it uses a parallel set of internal `ui-ext` endpoints (`available-roles`, `effective-roles`, `effective-roles-all`, `role-mappings/roles/{id}`, `role-mapping-delete`) with their own permission checks and their own query logic (`AvailableRoleMappingResource`, `EffectiveRoleMappingResource`, `AllEffectiveRoleMappingResource`, `RoleMappingDeleteResource`).

Duplicated endpoints and code make this area hard to maintain and error-prone: every authorization fix has to be applied in two places, with two different permission models and two sets of tests, and the `ui-ext` side has no `tests/base` coverage for fine-grained admin permissions. In practice the two drift apart:

- #53480 added the `canViewScopeMapping` filter to the scope-mapping listings, and #52399 the `canView` filter to `/role-mappings/realm`, but neither touched `ui-ext`, so `EffectiveRoleMappingResource` and `AllEffectiveRoleMappingResource` still return roles the caller cannot view (#50581, #52753).
- `AvailableRoleMappingResource` only lists client roles when the caller has `manage-users` (users, groups, composite roles) or `manage-clients` (clients, client scopes). Otherwise it falls back to `ClientPermissions.getClientIdsByScope` / `RolePermissions.getRoleIdsByScope`, which return nothing for RBAC admins and do not understand FGAP V2 type-level grants.
- `role-mapping-delete` for groups accepts `manage-membership`, while the Admin API requires `manage` on the group.

The user-visible symptom that surfaced this: an administrator with `manage-authorization`, `view-clients`, `view-users`, and the `query-*` roles can see a client and its roles in the Admin Console, but the *Add roles* dialog of a role-based authorization policy shows no client roles when filtering by clients (realm roles do show up). The same administrator can list those roles through `GET /clients/{id}/roles`. Which permissions apply depends on whether roles are managed from the Admin Console or through the Admin API.

#### Value proposition

- **One permission model for roles.** Whether roles are listed, assigned, or removed through the Admin Console, the Java/JavaScript admin clients, or the REST API directly, the same `RolePermissionEvaluator` checks apply. Administrators get consistent behaviour, and FGAP policies written against the documented Admin API also govern what the console shows.
- **Fixes work once.** Role visibility and mapping fixes such as #53480 and #52399 no longer need a second implementation in `ui-ext`; there is a single code path (`RoleMappingAwareResource`) and a single test suite (`tests/base`) to update.
- **Less code to maintain.** About 1,600 lines of `ui-ext` resources, models, and helpers are removed in favour of roughly 600 lines in `services`, all of them covered by RBAC and FGAP V2 tests.
- **Public, documented API.** The console-only capabilities (effective roles, inherited roles, searchable and paginated assignable roles) become part of the Admin API with OpenAPI metadata and client bindings, so integrators can build the same experiences the console has.
- **Prepares the ground for a single role mapping place.** Today role mapping is spread over `RoleMapperResource` (users, groups), `ScopeMappedResource` (clients, client scopes), `RoleByIdResource` and `RoleContainerResource` (composites), `ClientsResource`, and the `ui-ext` resources, each with its own query and permission code. This task collapses the query and permission logic into `RoleMappingAwareResource`, implemented by every resource that lists or assigns roles, and aligns the endpoint shapes (`/composite`, `/inherited`, `/available`, same `MappingsRepresentation`) across all of them. With the logic already in one place and the contracts already uniform, consolidating the endpoint declarations themselves into a single sub-resource (see Follow-up) becomes a mechanical refactor instead of a behavioural change.
- **Unblocks #53271.** Hardening role permissions under FGAP V2 is only meaningful if the console enforces the same rules; this task removes the parallel permission logic that would otherwise have to be hardened separately.

#### Goals

1. The Admin Console performs all role mapping operations exclusively through the Admin API; no `ui-ext` role endpoints remain.
2. An administrator who can view a role through the Admin API can see it in every role mapping view of the console, and one who can map it can assign it. In particular, the reported scenario (`view-clients` + `manage-authorization`, no `manage-users`) lists client roles in the role policy dialog.
3. Listing never leaks roles the caller cannot view, including under FGAP V2 resource-specific denials of a type-level grant, and pagination remains correct after that filtering.
4. Existing console behaviour is preserved where it is intentional: direct and inherited roles are both shown (#50687), search covers role names and client IDs, and `manage-users` alone still lists client roles.
5. Every changed or new endpoint has `tests/base` coverage for RBAC and FGAP V2, and every console consumer of the role mapping components has a Playwright test on its own data path.
6. Behaviour changes are documented in the upgrading guide with the removed and new endpoints.

#### Non-goals

- Reshaping the resource layout of `RoleMapperResource`, `ScopeMappedResource`, and `RoleByIdResource` (see Follow-up).
- Changing the permission semantics of the existing Admin API endpoints beyond the visibility filters already introduced by #53480 and #52399.
- Touching the non-role `ui-ext` endpoints.

#### Plan

Make the Admin Console use only the Admin API and move the role search logic to `services`, where it is subject to `RolePermissionEvaluator`:

1. Add Admin API endpoints returning only the roles the caller can view in the relevant scope:
   - `GET /clients/roles?search&first&max` → `List<ClientMappingsRepresentation>`: roles of all clients, grouped by client. Gated on `clients().canList() || manage-users` (so `manage-users` alone keeps working as with `ui-ext`), then filtered per role with `canView`.
   - `GET /users|groups/{id}/role-mappings/composite`, `/inherited`, and `/available`: effective mappings (composite expansion, group inheritance for users), the roles obtained only through composites and groups (so the Admin Console can list a role both as direct and as inherited, see #50687), and roles not yet mapped that the caller can map (`map-role`).
   - `GET /clients|client-scopes/{id}/scope-mappings/composite`, `/inherited`, and `/available` (`map-role-client-scope`, the client's own roles excluded).
   - `GET /roles-by-id/{id}/composites/composite`, `/inherited`, and `/available` (`map-role-composite`, the role and its current children excluded).
   - All return `MappingsRepresentation` with brief role representations. `/available` paginates and searches client roles (by role name or client ID); realm roles are returned unpaged.
2. Centralise the search in a `RoleMappingAwareResource` interface in `services` implemented by `RoleMapperResource`, `ScopeMappedResource`, `RoleByIdResource`, and `ClientsResource`. Besides holding the shared logic as default methods, it acts as a marker for every resource that lists or assigns roles, so that future changes to role visibility or mapping permissions have a single place to look at. It dispatches to the existing `canView`/`canMapRole`/`canMapComposite`/`canMapClientScope` primitives (no new methods on `RolePermissionEvaluator`), narrows the store query with `getRoleIdsByScope`/`getClientIdsByScope` when the admin is not granted the scope on all roles, and always applies the per-role check afterwards so that FGAP V2 resource-specific permissions can deny a type-level grant (the resource server is `UNANIMOUS`) and admin role conflicts are honoured. Paging is applied after that check, so pages are never shortened by roles the store returned but the caller cannot see.
3. Un-deprecate `GET /clients|client-scopes/{id}/scope-mappings`, which the Admin Console now uses, and return a `MappingsRepresentation` built with the same `canViewScopeMapping` filter introduced by #53480.
4. Update the Admin Console `role-mapping` components to consume the new endpoints (and the public `DELETE …/role-mappings/*` endpoints), fixing the "Filter by clients" view which leaked realm roles when using the composite-role flow. The role mapping tab keeps listing a role both as direct and as inherited (#50687) by combining `/{realm|clients}` with `/inherited`, and the *Add roles* dialog only paginates server-side for client roles, since realm roles are returned unpaged. Expose the endpoints in the Java and JavaScript admin clients.
5. Remove the `ui-ext` role endpoints and `ScopeMappedUtil`.
6. Add `tests/base` coverage (`RoleMappingSearchTest`, `RoleResourceTypeEvaluationTest`) for RBAC and FGAP V2, including role-specific overrides of type-level grants, and a Playwright test for the role-based policy dialog with a `view-clients` admin.
7. Document in the upgrading guide: the new endpoints, the removed `ui-ext` endpoints, and the behaviour changes below.

#### Endpoints

Legend: **New** = added by this change; **Changed** = existing endpoint whose contract or visibility changed; **Reused** = existing endpoint, unchanged, now used by the Admin Console. The last column lists the removed `ui-ext` endpoint the Admin Console used instead.

**`/clients`**

| Endpoint | Change | Visibility filter | Replaces (`ui-ext`) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /clients/roles?search&first&max` | New | `clients().canList() \|\| manage-users`, then `canView` per role | `GET /ui-ext/available-roles/roles/{id}` (role policies, `type=realms`) |

**`/users/{id}/role-mappings`** and **`/groups/{id}/role-mappings`**

| Endpoint | Change | Visibility filter | Replaces (`ui-ext`) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GET …/role-mappings` | Unchanged | `canView` | — |
| `GET …/role-mappings/realm` | Unchanged (filtered since #52399) | `canView` | — |
| `GET …/role-mappings/composite` | New | `canView` | `GET /ui-ext/effective-roles/users\|groups/{id}` |
| `GET …/role-mappings/inherited` | New | `canView` | `GET /ui-ext/effective-roles-all/users\|groups/{id}` |
| `GET …/role-mappings/available?search&first&max` | New | `canMapRole` | `GET /ui-ext/available-roles/users\|groups/{id}` |
| `DELETE …/role-mappings/realm`, `DELETE …/role-mappings/clients/{client}` | Reused | `manage` + `canMapRole` | `POST /ui-ext/role-mapping-delete/users\|groups/{id}` |

**`/clients/{id}/scope-mappings`** and **`/client-scopes/{id}/scope-mappings`**

| Endpoint | Change | Visibility filter | Replaces (`ui-ext`) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GET …/scope-mappings` | Changed: un-deprecated, returns `MappingsRepresentation` | `canViewScopeMapping` | `GET /ui-ext/effective-roles/clients\|clientScopes/{id}` (direct part) |
| `GET …/scope-mappings/realm`, `GET …/scope-mappings/clients/{client}` | Unchanged (filtered since #53480) | `canViewScopeMapping` | — |
| `GET …/scope-mappings/composite` | New | `canViewScopeMapping` | `GET /ui-ext/effective-roles/clients\|clientScopes/{id}` |
| `GET …/scope-mappings/inherited` | New | `canViewScopeMapping` | `GET /ui-ext/effective-roles-all/clients\|clientScopes/{id}` |
| `GET …/scope-mappings/available?search&first&max` | New | `canMapClientScope` | `GET /ui-ext/available-roles/clients\|clientScopes/{id}` |
| `DELETE …/scope-mappings/realm`, `DELETE …/scope-mappings/clients/{client}` | Reused | `canMapClientScope` | `POST /ui-ext/role-mapping-delete/clients\|clientScopes/{id}` |

**`/roles-by-id/{id}/composites`**

| Endpoint | Change | Visibility filter | Replaces (`ui-ext`) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GET …/composites/composite` | New | `canView` | `GET /ui-ext/effective-roles/roles/{id}`, `GET /ui-ext/role-mappings/roles/{id}` |
| `GET …/composites/inherited` | New | `canView` | `GET /ui-ext/effective-roles-all/roles/{id}` |
| `GET …/composites/available?search&first&max` | New | `canMapComposite` | `GET /ui-ext/available-roles/roles/{id}` |
| `DELETE …/composites` | Reused | `canMapComposite` | `POST /ui-ext/role-mapping-delete/roles/{id}` |

**Removed (`/admin/realms/{realm}/ui-ext`)**

`GET available-roles/{users|groups|clients|clientScopes|roles}/{id}`, `GET effective-roles/{…}/{id}`, `GET effective-roles-all/{…}/{id}`, `GET role-mappings/roles/{id}`, and `POST role-mapping-delete/{…}/{id}`, together with `ScopeMappedUtil` in `services`.

#### Follow-up

The `/composite`, `/inherited`, and `/available` endpoints are still declared separately by `RoleMapperResource`, `ScopeMappedResource`, and `RoleByIdResource`, each repeating the JAX-RS and OpenAPI metadata and the view check. A follow-up should replace them with a single sub-resource (for example `RoleMappingQueryResource`, mounted through a sub-resource locator like `getRoleMappings()` does today) parameterised with the mapping scope, the effective roles, the exclusions, and the view predicate, so that `RoleMappingAwareResource` can be dropped and the endpoint declarations exist once.

It is deliberately left out of this task. This change already removes the `ui-ext` endpoints, adds new Admin API endpoints with their Java and JavaScript client bindings, rewires the Admin Console, and changes the permission semantics that are being hardened under #53271. Reshaping the resource layout at the same time would enlarge the diff, mix a behavioural fix with a structural refactor that reviewers need to assess separately, and widen the surface where a regression could hide, particularly in the OpenAPI output and the generated clients. Landing the fix first, with the logic already in one place, keeps this change reviewable and backportable and makes the follow-up a pure refactor on top of a stable, tested API.

#### Behaviour changes to call out

- Direct callers of the removed `ui-ext` endpoints must switch to the Admin API.
- Removing a role mapping from a group in the Admin Console now requires `manage` on the group under FGAP V2 (`ui-ext` accepted `manage-membership`).
- Listing assignable roles in the Admin Console follows `view` permissions instead of requiring `manage-users`/`manage-clients`, which is strictly more permissive for listing; assigning still requires the corresponding `map-role*` permission.

| Endpoint | Change | Visibility filter | Replaces (`ui-ext`) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GET …/composites/composite` | New | `canView` | `GET /ui-ext/effective-roles/roles/{id}`, `GET /ui-ext/role-mappings/roles/{id}` |

`GET available-roles/{users|groups|clients|clientScopes|roles}/{id}`, `GET effective-roles/{…}/{id}`, `GET effective-roles-all/{…}/{id}`, `GET role-mappings/roles/{id}`, and `POST role-mapping-delete/{…}/{id}`, together with `ScopeMappedUtil` in `services`.

#### Follow-up

The `/composite`, `/inherited`, and `/available` endpoints are still declared separately by `RoleMapperResource`, `ScopeMappedResource`, and `RoleByIdResource`, each repeating the JAX-RS and OpenAPI metadata and the view check. A follow-up should replace them with a single sub-resource (for example `RoleMappingQueryResource`, mounted through a sub-resource locator like `getRoleMappings()` does today) parameterised with the mapping scope, the effective roles, the exclusions, and the view predicate, so that `RoleMappingAwareResource` can be dropped and the endpoint declarations exist once.

It is deliberately left out of this task. This change already removes the `ui-ext` endpoints, adds new Admin API endpoints with their Java and JavaScript client bindings, rewires the Admin Console, and changes the permission semantics that are being hardened under #53271. Reshaping the resource layout at the same time would enlarge the diff, mix a behavioural fix with a structural refactor that reviewers need to assess separately, and widen the surface where a regression could hide, particularly in the OpenAPI output and the generated clients. Landing the fix first, with the logic already in one place, keeps this change reviewable and backportable and makes the follow-up a pure refactor on top of a stable, tested API.

#### Behaviour changes to call out

- Direct callers of the removed `ui-ext` endpoints must switch to the Admin API.
- Removing a role mapping from a group in the Admin Console now requires `manage` on the group under FGAP V2 (`ui-ext` accepted `manage-membership`).
- Listing assignable roles in the Admin Console follows `view` permissions instead of requiring `manage-users`/`manage-clients`, which is strictly more permissive for listing; assigning still requires the corresponding `map-role*` permission.

### Description

When a realm has **Email as username** (`registrationEmailAsUsername=true`) and **Login with email** (`loginWithEmailAllowed=true`), the username field on `login.ftl` and `login-username.ftl` is labelled "Email". But the input is still `type="text"`:

```html
<input tabindex="1" id="username" ... name="username" value="..."
       type="text" autofocus
       autocomplete="username" .../>
```

([base/login/login-username.ftl](https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/blob/main/themes/src/main/resources/theme/base/login/login-username.ftl), and the same in `field.ftl` → `<@field.input>` of `keycloak.v2`, which always renders `type="text"`)

I propose to render `type="email"` for this field when the label is "Email", i.e. with the same condition the templates already use for the label:

```ftl
<#if realm.loginWithEmailAllowed && realm.registrationEmailAsUsername>type="email"<#else>type="text"</#if>
```


### Value Proposition

- **Mobile keyboards** show the email layout (`@` and `.` keys) for the email field.
- **Browser validation**: input like `foo`, `foo+` or `foo@` is rejected before the form is sent, with a localized browser message. There is no server round trip and no `invalid_user_credentials` / brute force count for an obvious typo.
- **Semantics and accessibility**: the input type matches the visible label "Email", so assistive technology announces an email field.
- **Custom authenticators** that use `login-username.ftl` for email-only flows (e.g. magic link or email OTP extensions) get a consistent email input without a theme override. One such extension, [p2-inc/keycloak-magic-link](https://github.com/p2-inc/keycloak-magic-link), creates users from the form input. Browser validation helps there, but it does not replace server-side validation.


### Goals

- `type="email"` for the username field of `login.ftl` and `login-username.ftl` when `realm.loginWithEmailAllowed && realm.registrationEmailAsUsername`.
- `type="text"` in all other cases (username only, or username or email), as today.
- The same behavior in `base` and in the default login theme. The `field.input` macro needs an optional `type` parameter (default `"text"`).


### Non-Goals

- Server-side email validation of the username field. The authenticators validate as today.
- The `required` attribute. That is #44912 / #45119.
- Changes to registration, update-profile or other user profile forms. They already render `html5-email` input types from the user profile configuration.


### Discussion

_No response_

### Notes

### Discussion

- **Users without an email.** In a realm that switched to *Email as username* after users were created, a user can have a username that is not an email address and no email attribute. With `type="email"`, the browser would block that username. Is this a supported case that needs a fallback (e.g. a theme property to keep `type="text"`)? Or does *Email as username* already imply that all users log in with an email?
- **Which themes.** #52371 plans to replace `keycloak.v2` with `keycloak.v3` (PatternFly 6) in 27.0.0. Should this change go into `base` and `keycloak.v3` only, or also into `keycloak.v2`?

### Notes

Related:

- #44912 / #45119: `required` attribute on mandatory login fields (keycloak.v2)
- #34091: `autocomplete="username"` for the username form (fixed in 26.0.8 / 26.1.0)
- #52371: PatternFly 6 login UI (`keycloak.v3`)

Proposed change in `base/login/login-username.ftl` (same pattern in `base/login/login.ftl`):

```diff
                                 <input tabindex="1" id="username"
                                        aria-invalid="<#if messagesPerField.existsError('username')>true</#if>"
                                        class="${properties.kcInputClass!}" name="username"
                                        value="${(login.username!'')}"
-                                       type="text" autofocus
+                                       type="<#if realm.loginWithEmailAllowed && realm.registrationEmailAsUsername>email<#else>text</#if>" autofocus
                                        autocomplete="${(enableWebAuthnConditionalUI?has_content)?then('username webauthn', 'username')}"
                                        dir="ltr"/>
```

For the `field.input` macro:

```diff
-<#macro input name label value="" required=false autocomplete="off" fieldName=name error=messagesPerField.get(fieldName) autofocus=false>
+<#macro input name label value="" type="text" required=false autocomplete="off" fieldName=name error=messagesPerField.get(fieldName) autofocus=false>
   ...
-        <input id="${name}" name="${name}" value="${value}" type="text" autocomplete="${autocomplete}" <#if autofocus>autofocus</#if>
+        <input id="${name}" name="${name}" value="${value}" type="${type}" autocomplete="${autocomplete}" <#if autofocus>autofocus</#if>
```

I can provide the PR once the scope (themes, fallback) is agreed.
