### Describe the bug

Since #35822 the server treats a missing `exact` flag as `true` for custom attributes. The admin console user list only sends the flag when the box is checked (`if (activeFilters.exact) params.exact = true;` in `UserDataTable.tsx`), so with "Exact search" unchecked the attribute search is still exact.

### Version

26.6.4

### Regression

- [ ] The issue is a regression

### Expected behavior

Unchecked "Exact search" sends `exact=false`, so `custom` = `94` also finds a user with `94#381`.

### Actual behavior

Only users with exactly `94` are found, checked or not.

### How to Reproduce?

1. Create user A with attribute `custom=94` and user B with `custom=94#381`.
2. Users > Attribute search: `custom` = `94`, "Exact search" unchecked, Search.
3. Only user A is listed.

### Anything else?

Fix: send `params.exact = activeFilters.exact` instead of only `true`.

### Description

With the default `jdbc-ping` stack there is no supported way to tune JGroups heartbeat failure detection (`FD_ALL3` `timeout` / `interval`, and `VERIFY_SUSPECT2` `timeout`).

`jdbc-ping` is built in code on top of the `tcp` stack, so a custom `cache-ispn.xml` can't change it:

- `<stack name="x" extends="jdbc-ping">` fails with `ISPN000540: No such JGroups stack 'jdbc-ping'`.
- Redefining `tcp` fails with `ISPN000539: Duplicate JGroups stack 'tcp'`.
- A custom stack with another name turns off Keycloak's JDBC_PING discovery and the mTLS wiring.

There's also no `--cache-embedded-*` option for it, and these `FD_ALL3` attributes have no system-property placeholders.

When a member disappears without closing its connections (node loss, network partition, or a killed pod whose packets are dropped), `FD_SOCK2` doesn't fire. The member then stays in the view for the full `FD_ALL3` timeout of 40 s, plus the check interval and suspect verification. On a 2-node cluster on 26.7.5 we measured 46 s locally and about 50 s on Kubernetes.

During that window, every write to a distributed cache that the dead member owns waits `remote-timeout` (5 s) for its ack and then fails. For example, `authenticationSessions` fails with `ISPN000427: Timeout after 5 seconds waiting for acks`. So most sign-in page loads on the surviving node return a 500 until the view changes.

### Value Proposition

Shorter, configurable detection makes an abrupt member loss cost seconds of sign-in errors instead of most of a minute. Operators can then trade detection time against tolerance for GC pauses and network jitter for their own environment.

In a local test, setting `FD_ALL3` to 15 s / 3 s at runtime on both nodes of 26.6.3, 26.7.5 and 26.8.1 dropped a cut-off member from the view in 16 to 18 s. With the defaults it took 46 s.

### Goals

- Options such as `--cache-embedded-network-heartbeat-timeout` and `--cache-embedded-network-heartbeat-interval` (names illustrative) applied to `FD_ALL3` in the `jdbc-ping` and `jdbc-ping-udp` stacks. Possibly also the `VERIFY_SUSPECT2` timeout.
- Or: let a `cache-ispn.xml` stack extend `jdbc-ping`, so `stack.combine` overrides work as they do for the Infinispan stacks.
- Validation: the timeout must be at least 2 × the interval.

### Non-Goals

- Changing the defaults.
- Changing `FD_SOCK2` behaviour (it already catches a member whose connections close).

### Discussion

_No response_

### Notes

Related, different symptom: https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/issues/46298

body_text:
### Description

I would like to be able to limit the amount of OfflineSessions for each User. Analog to the already existing `UserSessionLimitsAuthenticator`.

### Value Proposition

For one of our customers, we want to limit the amount of OfflineSessions per User. They have approx. 10 million users and rising. Their lifetime is 1 year for now.(I know...) Their Users are mostly on mobile(offline_access). In the past, they had problems with old unused OfflineSessions dangling around.


I think it would be a nice feature to limit those OfflineSessions and terminate the oldest one.

### Goals

Implement one of the 2 implementation options. 

1. Add options for OfflineSessions on `UserSessionLimitsAuthenticatorFactory`.
2. Create a new Authenticator analog to `UserSessionLimitsAuthenticatorFactory` -> `OfflineUserSessionLimitsAuthenticatorFactory`



Option 1. could include a bool toggle, which is "Target OfflineSession"
I can also think of just duplicating the existing Settings to target OfflineSessions

### Non-Goals

Change the existing behavior for `UserSessionLimitsAuthenticator`. Which is only targeting normal UserSessions. What can be observed on function `Stream<UserSessionModel> getUserSessionsStream(RealmModel realm, UserModel user);` in `UserSessionProvider` 

### Discussion

_No response_

### Notes

For design ideas, please see "Goals". If you have any better idea, please tell me. 

Im happy to create a PR for any of the two proposed solutions.

### Before reporting an issue

- [X] I have read and understood the above terms for submitting issues, and I understand that my issue may be closed without action if I do not follow them.

### Area

dist/quarkus

### Describe the bug

Stopping the Keycloak Windows service (`net stop <name>`) does not shut down Keycloak gracefully. The documentation and the `--stop-timeout` option describe a graceful stop, but the service is stopped by terminating the process tree.

The service is installed with Apache Commons Daemon Procrun in `exe` mode: `kc.bat start` is the start image, and `kc.bat stop` is the stop image. There is no `stop` command in `kc.bat` or in the Keycloak CLI, so the stop image only starts a JVM that prints an unknown command error and exits. Nothing tells the running Keycloak process to shut down.

Based on the Procrun source, the service stop then works as follows:

1. Procrun waits for the start process (`kc.bat`, running `cmd.exe`) to exit, for up to the stop timeout (30 seconds by default). `kc.bat` exits only when its `java` child exits, so this waits for the full timeout.
2. Procrun then ends the start process and walks its process tree, terminating every process it finds using `TerminateProcess`. This does not run JVM shutdown hooks, so Quarkus and Infinispan are not shut down in an orderly way.

As a result, every stop of the service takes at least the stop timeout, and ends with a forced kill. The walk of the process tree is limited (it handles at most 32 processes, and finds children by the parent process ID of a snapshot), so a server process that is not found would not be stopped. In a CI run the service stayed in the `STOP_PENDING` state for more than two minutes after the stop request.

The documentation of the Windows service lists `StopParams: stop` as a Procrun setting that is applied, uses `--stop-timeout=60` as an example for a longer stop timeout, and the option is described as the time to wait for the service to stop gracefully.

### Version

main

### Regression

- [ ] The issue is a regression

### Expected behavior

Stopping the service shuts down Keycloak in an orderly way, as if `kc.sh` had been stopped with a termination signal: the JVM shutdown hooks run, and the Keycloak process has exited when the service is reported as stopped.

### Actual behavior

The Keycloak process is terminated forcefully after the stop timeout has elapsed. A forceful shutdown does not gracefully leave an Infinispan cluster, and does not gracefully shut down HTTP requests. 

### How to Reproduce?

1. Install the service using `bin\kc.bat tools windows-service install` and start it.
2. Run `net stop <name>` and observe that it takes at least the stop timeout.

### Area

dist/quarkus

### Describe the bug

Stopping the Keycloak Windows service (`net stop <name>`) does not shut down Keycloak gracefully. The documentation and the `--stop-timeout` option describe a graceful stop, but the service is stopped by terminating the process tree.

The service is installed with Apache Commons Daemon Procrun in `exe` mode: `kc.bat start` is the start image, and `kc.bat stop` is the stop image. There is no `stop` command in `kc.bat` or in the Keycloak CLI, so the stop image only starts a JVM that prints an unknown command error and exits. Nothing tells the running Keycloak process to shut down.

Based on the Procrun source, the service stop then works as follows:

1. Procrun waits for the start process (`kc.bat`, running `cmd.exe`) to exit, for up to the stop timeout (30 seconds by default). `kc.bat` exits only when its `java` child exits, so this waits for the full timeout.
2. Procrun then ends the start process and walks its process tree, terminating every process it finds using `TerminateProcess`. This does not run JVM shutdown hooks, so Quarkus and Infinispan are not shut down in an orderly way.

As a result, every stop of the service takes at least the stop timeout, and ends with a forced kill. The walk of the process tree is limited (it handles at most 32 processes, and finds children by the parent process ID of a snapshot), so a server process that is not found would not be stopped. In a CI run the service stayed in the `STOP_PENDING` state for more than two minutes after the stop request.

The documentation of the Windows service lists `StopParams: stop` as a Procrun setting that is applied, uses `--stop-timeout=60` as an example for a longer stop timeout, and the option is described as the time to wait for the service to stop gracefully.

### Version

main

### Regression

- [ ] The issue is a regression

### Expected behavior

Stopping the service shuts down Keycloak in an orderly way, as if `kc.sh` had been stopped with a termination signal: the JVM shutdown hooks run, and the Keycloak process has exited when the service is reported as stopped.

### Actual behavior

The Keycloak process is terminated forcefully after the stop timeout has elapsed. A forceful shutdown does not gracefully leave an Infinispan cluster, and does not gracefully shut down HTTP requests. 

### How to Reproduce?

1. Install the service using `bin\kc.bat tools windows-service install` and start it.
2. Run `net stop <name>` and observe that it takes at least the stop timeout.
3. Check the Keycloak log, which does not show the messages of an orderly shutdown.

I did not verify this on a Windows machine. The analysis is based on the logs of a CI run and the Procrun source.

### Anything else?

The test `WindowsServiceDistTest` is flaky because of this, see #54223.

The feature was added in #44496, its request is #37704.

### Before reporting an issue

- [x] I have read and understood the above terms for submitting issues, and I understand that my issue may be closed without action if I do not follow them.

### Area

admin/ui

### Describe the bug

Running `npm create keycloak-theme my-theme -t admin` fails with:

```
error: too many arguments. Expected 1 argument but got 2.
```

npm treats `-t` as its own `--tag` flag, so the create script receives `my-theme admin` as two positional arguments. Commander only accepts a single `<name>` argument, so the command fails. The documented example in the package README uses this form.

### Version

nightly

### Regression

- [ ] The issue is a regression

### Expected behavior

`npm create keycloak-theme my-theme -t admin` (or an equivalent documented form) creates an admin UI theme project. If the type is omitted, the CLI should ask which type to create instead of silently defaulting to account.

### Actual behavior

The command fails with `error: too many arguments. Expected 1 argument but got 2.` because npm strips `-t` and forwards `admin` as a second positional argument.

### How to Reproduce?

```bash
npm create keycloak-theme my-theme -t admin
```

### Anything else?

Workaround today: `npm create keycloak-theme my-theme -- --type admin`

Proposed fix: accept an optional positional `[type]` argument (so the common `npm create` invocation works), and prompt for the type when it is omitted.

### Description

When client is created/modified by CIMD, it should possibly use just standard fields provided by OIDC client representation. Ideally, there should not be a support for setup any Keycloak-specific custom fields (like for example various client switches specific to Keycloak `ClientRepresentation` or switches like `full scope allowed` switch or `defaultRoles` of the client etc).

This issue is to track this and make sure that any such things are removed.

Related note: The `default` provider of dynamic client registration is deprecated and will be removed in Keycloak 27. So the only way for dynamic client registration in 27 would be standard OIDC client representation.

### Before reporting an issue

- [x] I have read and understood the above terms for submitting issues, and I understand that my issue may be closed without action if I do not follow them.

### Area

admin/fine-grained-permissions

### Describe the bug

When Fine-Grained Admin Permissions (FGAP) v2 is enabled, a delegated administrator granted view-members access to a specific group can't view LDAP-backed members in the global Users search list

This occurs even though:
- Import Users is toggled ON on the LDAP provider
- Local (non-LDAP) users in the exact same group display properly in the Users list
- The delegated administrator can view the LDAP users when navigating directly to the group's Members tab

This contradicts the [FGAP v2 documentation](https://www.keycloak.org/docs/latest/server_admin/#users-resource-type):
"This feature does not support enforcing access to federated resources. Users from external storage providers (such as LDAP with import disabled) are not visible in search results when access is controlled through fine-grained permissions. To include federated users in search results, grant the administrator the view-users role, or enable user import on the federation provider."

### Version

v26.8.0, v26.8.1

### Regression

- [ ] The issue is a regression

### Expected behavior

Imported federated users belonging to an authorized group should appear in the global Users search list, consistent with local users. If FGAP v2 architecturally isn't able to support search resolution for LDAP_ONLY group mapping, the documentation should clarify that both User Import and IMPORT / READ_ONLY group mapper modes are required or if it is even possible to achieve at all.

### Actual behavior

The global Users search returns 0 results (or omits LDAP users while displaying local users).

### How to Reproduce?

1. Configure an LDAP user federation provider with Import Users set to ON.
2. Add a group-ldap-mapper with Mode set to LDAP_ONLY.
3. Create a delegated admin user and assign the query-users and query-groups roles from the realm-management client.
4. Create a Group-level permission granting the delegated admin view-members on an LDAP-synced group.
5. Assign at least one local user and one imported LDAP user to that group.
6. Log in as the delegated admin:
    - Navigate to Groups -> Members: Both local and LDAP users appear.
    - Navigate to Users and search (*): Only the local user appears (the LDAP user is omitted).

### Anything else?

This creates a functional blocker for deployments requiring live write-back of group memberships to LDAP (which requires LDAP_ONLY with WRITABLE mode).

Attempting to work around this by switching the mapper mode to IMPORT or READ_ONLY currently fails due to bug #54054 (ModelDuplicateException caused by FGAP filters running during internal LDAP group resolution).

body_text:
Running Liquibase at runtime would allow us to keep using Liquibase and follow the latest releases with the non-open source license. The idea is to exclude Liquibase from the distribution but instead use it to generate some static resources which would then be applied at runtime to migrate the DB.

#### Scope of this spike
* Double check CNCF Policies if this approach would be truly permitted. There might be some niche nuances like whether Liquibase is ran automatically and it's included in the project as a dependency, or whether it needs to be ran as a independent offline tool a developer uses and is never committed to the repo.
* Create a prototype to estimate the effort required to migrate Keycloak to this approach.
   * The aim is to keep using the Change Set files but use Liquibase to generate some static resources (SQL files?) using it. Open question (also based on the compliance with the CNCF Policies) is whether those resources can be generated at build-time, or whether they'll need to be created at "dev-time" and committed.
   * Consider the Custom Changes in the Change Sets that require Java code. That will need to be resolved somehow as they're often DB vendor dependant.
   * Research the tooling need for applying the generated static resources at runtime. This might be either a custom logic living in Keycloak, or existing tools like [Flyway](https://www.red-gate.com/products/flyway/community/).

### Before reporting an issue

- [x] I have read and understood the above terms for submitting issues, and I understand that my issue may be closed without action if I do not follow them.

### Area

admin/api

### Describe the bug

The server admin guide describes the Verify Email required action as: "The user must verify their email account. An email will be sent to the user with a validation link that they must click."

When an administrator adds Verify Email to an existing user whose email is already marked as verified, in the Admin Console (Users > user > Details > Required user actions) or through `PUT /admin/realms/{realm}/users/{id}`, no email is sent. At the next login the action is marked as completed and removed, and the user signs in without verifying anything. Until then the Admin Console shows Email verified On next to the pending Verify Email action.

### Version

main (nightly), reproduced at commit b617a625f5

### Regression

- [ ] The issue is a regression

### Expected behavior

Adding Verify Email asks the user to confirm the email address again: the verification email is sent at the next login, and Email verified shows that the address is not verified until the link is used.

### Actual behavior

The login continues without the verification page. The events show `CUSTOM_REQUIRED_ACTION` with `custom_required_action=VERIFY_EMAIL` and no `SEND_VERIFY_EMAIL`. The action is removed from the user, no email is sent, and Email verified stays On.

### How to Reproduce?

### Before reporting an issue

- [x] I have read and understood the above terms for submitting issues, and I understand that my issue may be closed without action if I do not follow them.

### Area

admin/ui

### Describe the bug

The Admin UI E2E test `realm-settings/client-profiles.spec.ts` "Realm settings client profiles tab tests › Edit client profile › Check deleting the client profile" intermittently fails in the Admin UI E2E (chromium) CI job with `Test timeout of 30000ms exceeded` while waiting for `getByRole('menuitem', { name: 'Delete this client profile', exact: true })`. The failure did not reproduce on a re-run of the same job.

A Playwright trace of a failing run shows that the test clicks the "Edit" link in the client profiles table and then clicks `action-dropdown` only about 57 ms later, while the lazy-loaded client profile page is still loading. At that moment the Realm settings page is still shown, and it has its own `action-dropdown` in its header. The test therefore clicks the toggle of the previous page, and the menu disappears as soon as the client profile page replaces it. The menu item "Delete this client profile" never appears, and the test runs into the timeout.

The `beforeEach` of "Edit client profile" doesn't wait for the client profile page before the test uses the `selectActionToggleItem` helper in `test/utils/masthead.ts`. Other tests that navigate and then use this helper (it is used by around 30 tests) can fail the same way.

### Version

nightly

### Regression

- [ ] The issue is a regression

### Expected behavior

The test passes reliably, independent of the timing of the dropdown rendering.

### Actual behavior

```
Error: locator.click: Test timeout of 30000ms exceeded.
Call log:
  - waiting for getByRole('menuitem', { name: 'Delete this client profile', exact: true })

   at utils/masthead.ts:14
   12 | export async function selectActionToggleItem(page: Page, item: string) {
   13 |   await getActionToggleButton(page).click();
 > 14 |   await page.getByRole("menuitem", { name: item, exact: true }).click();
```

### How to Reproduce?

The failure happens only sporadically in CI under load, for example in the Admin UI E2E (chromium) job.

### Anything else?

The helper is identical on `main`, `release/26.8`, `release/26.6` and `release/26.4`.

body_text:
Investigate the effort required to fork and maintain a stripped-out version of Liquibase 4 - the last open source release. The fork should be the bare minimum required for Keycloak to be used at runtime with minimum changes required at the Keycloak side. Ideally it should be a drop-in replacement for current Liquibase. While the fork would be public, it might be a bit "dirty" - serving only Keycloak's purpose, not meant for general community usage.

#### Scope of this spike
* Investigate what features we can remove from Liquibase.
   * Estimate the effort needed for removing the features.
* Estimate the maintenance costs.
   * How complex is the codebase with the not needed features removed?
   * How do we handle CVEs? Can we cherry-pick some fixes from upstream Liquibase 5 - does the license allow that? How do we determine which fixes are relevant?

#### Other considerations
See also https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/issues/43391#issuecomment-5456619739.

<!-- Please use this template while reporting a bug and provide as much info as possible. Not doing so may result in your bug not being addressed in a timely manner. Thanks!

If the matter is security related, please disclose it privately via https://kubernetes.io/security/
-->

## What happened

I was cleaning up my configuration files, and decided to add the [`%YAML 1.1` directive](https://yaml.org/spec/1.1/current.html#id895631) to the top of all of them, so that I could get better syntax highlighting in Visual Studio Code (which defaults to YAML 1.2, not currently supported by `kubectl`).

After adding the directive, `kubectl` stopped being able to parse the files, instead returning the following error, despite the file being valid, as reported by both `yq` and other online tools:
```text
error: error parsing file.yml: error converting YAML to JSON: yaml: line 1: did not find expected <document start>
```

## What you expected to happen

I expected my configuration files to be processed successfully, as they are valid YAML. 

## How to reproduce it
<!-- Please make sure you are able to reproduce the bug using a supported version and version skew of Kubernetes. See https://kubernetes.io/docs/setup/release/version-skew-policy for which versions and are currently supported.
-->

After some experimentation, I created the following minimal YAML file to reproduce the issue:
```yml
%YAML 1.1
---
```

That file is equivalent to the following YAML 1.1 file:
```yml
null
```

The former returns:
```log
error: error parsing directive-test.yml: error converting YAML to JSON: yaml: line 1: did not find expected <document start>
```

While the latter correctly returns:
```log
error: no objects passed to apply
```

### Environment

[`kubectl`](https://archlinux.org/packages/extra/x86_64/kubectl/) installed via Arch Linux repositories.

Cluster set up via the [`kubeadm`](https://archlinux.org/packages/extra/x86_64/kubeadm/) provided by the Arch Linux repositories.

**Is this a BUG REPORT or FEATURE REQUEST?**: 

- /kind feature 

- /sig node

**Motivation**:
Currently, Kubelet sets `cpu.shares` to `2` for the top-level BestEffort QoS cgroup. The goal is to allow BestEffort tasks to utilize free CPU cycles (improving node utilization) while minimizing the impact on Guaranteed and Burstable workloads.

However, relying solely on `cpu.shares` (even with a minimal value) provides "weight-based" isolation. In high-load scenarios, this can still lead to latency interference for high-priority tasks.

Since Linux Kernel 5.4, significant improvements have been made to `SCHED_IDLE` (Reference Patch: `sched/fair: Improve the scheduling of SCHED_IDLE tasks`).
* **Better Isolation**: `cpu.idle` (SCHED_IDLE) ensures that tasks are treated with truly "idle" priority. They only run when there is absolutely no other higher-priority task to run. This offers significantly better isolation for Guaranteed/Burstable pods compared to simply lowering `cpu.shares`（cgroup v2 `cpu.weight`）.
* **Safe Colocation**: It allows safe colocation of BestEffort batch jobs with latency-sensitive services without the risk of performance degradation for the latter.

**Current Barrier (The Conflict)**:
We are currently attempting to utilize `cpu.idle` for BestEffort pods using external agents/extensions on  nodes. However, this conflicts with Kubelet's current initialization logic, causing Kubelet to fail to start.

In Cgroup v1, when `cpu.idle` is set to `1`:
1.  The kernel forces `cpu.shares` to `1` (minimal weight).
2.  The kernel locks `cpu.shares` from being modified.

In Cgroup v2, when `cpu.idle` is set to `1`:
1.  The kernel forces `cpu.weight` to `0` (minimal weight).
2.  The kernel locks `cpu.weight` from being modified.
 
Because Kubelet hardcodes the enforcement of `cpu.shares = 2` or `cpu.weight = 1`   for BestEffort, it crashes during startup if `cpu.idle` is already enabled by an external tool or previous configuration:

For Example in Cgroup v1: 
> "Failed to start ContainerManager" err="failed to initialize top level QOS containers: failed to update top level BestEffort QOS cgroup : failed to write \"2\": write /sys/fs/cgroup/cpu,cpuacct/kubepods.slice/kubepods-besteffort.slice/cpu.shares: invalid argument"



**What you expected to happen:** Kubelet should start successfully even if `cpu.idle` is enabled for the BestEffort cgroup. Kubelet should either detect that `cpu.idle` is enabled and skip setting `cpu.shares` or `cpu.weight`, or handle the write error gracefully.

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible):**

1. On a node with a Kernel supporting `cpu.idle` interface (Linux).

2. Manually (or via an external agent) set `cpu.idle` to `1` for the BestEffort slice:

```
Bash

echo 1 > /sys/fs/cgroup/cpu,cpuacct/kubepods.slice/kubepods-besteffort.slice/cpu.idle

```
3. Restart Kubelet.
4. Observe the startup failure.

5. Manual verification of the conflict:

```
Bash

# echo 2 > /sys/fs/cgroup/cpuacct/kubepods.slice/kubepods-besteffort.slice/cpu.shares
-bash: echo: write error: Invalid argument
```
**Anything else we need to know:**

- **Context:** We use `cpu.idle` (SCHED_IDLE) for BestEffort tasks to utilize the enhanced scheduling isolation provided by Linux Kernel 5.4+ (Patch: `sched/fair: Improve the scheduling of SCHED_IDLE tasks`). This is often a superior alternative to low `cpu.shares` for maximizing node utilization without interfering with high-priority workloads.

- **Kernel Behavior:** When `cpu.idle` is configured to `1`, the kernel forces `cpu.shares` to `1` and `cpu.weight` to `1` and forbids modification, leading to the Invalid argument error when Kubelet tries to write min shares(or weight)

- **Workaround:** Setting `cpu.idle` back to `0` allows Kubelet to start.

**Proposed Solution:**

1. **Short-term fix (Resilience)**: Modify the Kubelet `qos_container_manager` logic. Before attempting to set `cpu.shares` for the BestEffort cgroup, check if cpu.idle is configured (if the interface exists).

    If `cpu.idle == 1`: Skip setting `cpu.shares` and `cpu.weight` (accept the kernel's forced value).

    If `cpu.idle == 0` or file does not exist: Proceed with setting `cpu.shares` to `2`and `cpu.weight` to `1`.

2. **Long-term feature**: Add native support in Kubelet configuration to support `cpu.idle` (SCHED_IDLE) for BestEffort pods, allowing users to opt-in to this scheduling policy directly via Kubelet rather than relying on external agents.

**Benefits:**

**Superior QoS**: Provides strict priority isolation for Guaranteed/Burstable pods, reducing tail latency in colocation scenarios.

**Resilience**: Prevents Kubelet startup failures for users attempting to use SCHED_IDLE via custom tuning agents.

This offers significantly better isolation for Guaranteed/Burstable pods compared to simply lowering `cpu.shares`（cgroup v2 `cpu.weight`）.
* **Safe Colocation**: It allows safe colocation of BestEffort batch jobs with latency-sensitive services without the risk of performance degradation for the latter.

**Current Barrier (The Conflict)**:
We are currently attempting to utilize `cpu.idle` for BestEffort pods using external agents/extensions on  nodes. However, this conflicts with Kubelet's current initialization logic, causing Kubelet to fail to start.

In Cgroup v1, when `cpu.idle` is set to `1`:
1.  The kernel forces `cpu.shares` to `1` (minimal weight).
2.  The kernel locks `cpu.shares` from being modified.

In Cgroup v2, when `cpu.idle` is set to `1`:
1.  The kernel forces `cpu.weight` to `0` (minimal weight).
2.  The kernel locks `cpu.weight` from being modified.
 
Because Kubelet hardcodes the enforcement of `cpu.shares = 2` or `cpu.weight = 1`   for BestEffort, it crashes during startup if `cpu.idle` is already enabled by an external tool or previous configuration:

For Example in Cgroup v1: 
> "Failed to start ContainerManager" err="failed to initialize top level QOS containers: failed to update top level BestEffort QOS cgroup : failed to write \"2\": write /sys/fs/cgroup/cpu,cpuacct/kubepods.slice/kubepods-besteffort.slice/cpu.shares: invalid argument"



**What you expected to happen:** Kubelet should start successfully even if `cpu.idle` is enabled for the BestEffort cgroup. Kubelet should either detect that `cpu.idle` is enabled and skip setting `cpu.shares` or `cpu.weight`, or handle the write error gracefully.

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible):**

1. On a node with a Kernel supporting `cpu.idle` interface (Linux).

2. Manually (or via an external agent) set `cpu.idle` to `1` for the BestEffort slice:

```
Bash

echo 1 > /sys/fs/cgroup/cpu,cpuacct/kubepods.slice/kubepods-besteffort.slice/cpu.idle

```
3. Restart Kubelet.
4. Observe the startup failure.

5. Manual verification of the conflict:

```
Bash

# echo 2 > /sys/fs/cgroup/cpuacct/kubepods.slice/kubepods-besteffort.slice/cpu.shares
-bash: echo: write error: Invalid argument
```
**Anything else we need to know:**

- **Context:** We use `cpu.idle` (SCHED_IDLE) for BestEffort tasks to utilize the enhanced scheduling isolation provided by Linux Kernel 5.4+ (Patch: `sched/fair: Improve the scheduling of SCHED_IDLE tasks`). This is often a superior alternative to low `cpu.shares` for maximizing node utilization without interfering with high-priority workloads.

- **Kernel Behavior:** When `cpu.idle` is configured to `1`, the kernel forces `cpu.shares` to `1` and `cpu.weight` to `1` and forbids modification, leading to the Invalid argument error when Kubelet tries to write min shares(or weight)

- **Workaround:** Setting `cpu.idle` back to `0` allows Kubelet to start.

**Proposed Solution:**

1. **Short-term fix (Resilience)**: Modify the Kubelet `qos_container_manager` logic. Before attempting to set `cpu.shares` for the BestEffort cgroup, check if cpu.idle is configured (if the interface exists).

    If `cpu.idle == 1`: Skip setting `cpu.shares` and `cpu.weight` (accept the kernel's forced value).

    If `cpu.idle == 0` or file does not exist: Proceed with setting `cpu.shares` to `2`and `cpu.weight` to `1`.

2. **Long-term feature**: Add native support in Kubelet configuration to support `cpu.idle` (SCHED_IDLE) for BestEffort pods, allowing users to opt-in to this scheduling policy directly via Kubelet rather than relying on external agents.

**Benefits:**

**Superior QoS**: Provides strict priority isolation for Guaranteed/Burstable pods, reducing tail latency in colocation scenarios.

**Resilience**: Prevents Kubelet startup failures for users attempting to use SCHED_IDLE via custom tuning agents.

The `selector.matchLabels` field was made immutable some years back and since then I've just seen so much friction for users dealing with this part of the spec.

Mostly because people just copy other labels, such as org data (as [suggested in the docs](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview/working-with-objects/labels/#motivation)) into `matchLabels`, then later need to change those label values and are then faced with a resource they cannot update due to the dreaded `field is immutable` error. There are solutions for this, e.g.deleting a deployment with the `--cascade=orphan` option, but this is risky and messy. We just faced an incident where the newly orphaned replicaset was adopted by another deployment and scaled down.

This leads me to question why does this field even exist in the spec? In what world are people wanting to manually specify the relationship between parent/child resources?

If someone has a custom resource which does not create pods but does have a scale subresource, it would be nice to be able to scale it based only on a custom metric. Currently this is not possible with HorizontalPodAutoscaler since it needs to list pods and does not just trust what the scale subresource tells it.

This would mean ignoring the implementation details of whatever the custom resource controller creates under the hood and just use the status of the scale subresource.

(obviously this means the "pod" in the hpa name wouldn't make much sense, but raising this so it could be considered if other changes happen around the area of counting pods)

/sig autoscaling
/cc @adrianmoisey

### What happened?

`ParseQuantity("1.001").String()` returns `"1.001"` instead of the canonical form `"1001m"`.
This affects any decimal input where the number of decimal places is a multiple of 3 (3, 6, 9).

### Root cause

In 
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/eb8032bb8313640f57d32560b90269618524e9c6/staging/src/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/api/resource/quantity.go#L278
 the fast-path caching check:
    `if scale%3 == 0 && !strings.HasSuffix(shifted, "000") && shifted[0] != '0'`
incorrectly caches the raw input string as canonical when the input contains a decimal point.
The fix is to add `len(denom) == 0` to ensure only inputs without a decimal point are cached.

**Kubernetes version:** v1.35.x


### What did you expect to happen?

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/eb8032bb8313640f57d32560b90269618524e9c6/staging/src/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/api/resource/quantity.go#L278

`ParseQuantity("1.001").String()` should return `"1001m"`, consistent with how other decimal inputs are canonicalized (e.g. `"1.44"` → `"1440m"`).
Inputs with 1, 2, or 4 decimal places canonicalize correctly. Only multiples of 3 are affected.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Under

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/eb8032bb8313640f57d32560b90269618524e9c6/staging/src/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/api/resource/quantity_test.go#L789

Add follow testing cases
```
		{"1.001", "1001m"},

### Root cause

In 
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/eb8032bb8313640f57d32560b90269618524e9c6/staging/src/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/api/resource/quantity.go#L278
 the fast-path caching check:
    `if scale%3 == 0 && !strings.HasSuffix(shifted, "000") && shifted[0] != '0'`
incorrectly caches the raw input string as canonical when the input contains a decimal point.
The fix is to add `len(denom) == 0` to ensure only inputs without a decimal point are cached.

### What would you like to be added?

We'd like to use MemAvailable of /proc/meminfo as the only signal for memory eviction.
The existing signals that depend on `container_memory_working_set_bytes{id=~"/|/kubepods.slice"}` are not friendly to our nodes running cache(page cache and slab cache) heavy workloads.

### Why is this needed?

1. it excludes hugepages mentioned in  https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/138127#issue-4178699512
2. it excludes `vm.min_free_kbytes` that is not available for normal allocations. see https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/131319
3. it doesn't counts all the active page cache[1] against memory.available. see https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/43916

[1] https://github.com/torvalds/linux/blob/d60bc140158342716e13ff0f8aa65642f43ba053/mm/show_mem.c#L49-L57
```
	/*
	 * Not all the page cache can be freed, otherwise the system will
	 * start swapping or thrashing. Assume at least half of the page
	 * cache, or the low watermark worth of cache, needs to stay.
	 */
	pagecache = global_node_page_state(NR_ACTIVE_FILE) +
		global_node_page_state(NR_INACTIVE_FILE);
	pagecache -= min(pagecache / 2, wmark_low);
	available += pagecache;
```

### What happened?

This used to work but somewhere around 1.32 it broke. When trying to use `kubectl logs <pod>` I get an error like the following:

```
failed to try resolving symlinks in path "\\var\\log\\pods\\build-agents_repo-update-hq15wkubbamp04-29644200-ldg5d_c1d12e90-f0e4-4bda-a89e-1b5eb5b27404\\repo-update\\0.log": The system cannot find the path specified
```

### What did you expect to happen?

I expect it to show/follow the logs.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

- Create a secondary fs on a secondary drive (let's say 'D')
- Create an empty folder at `c:\var`
- mount the secondary drive at `c:\var`
- start k8s bits
- run a pod on the given node
- try to retrieve/stream the logs from the pod on that node

body_text:
The static analyzer found several potential bugs:
1. In [pkg/kubelet/pod_workers.go in the podWorkerLoop function on line 1302](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/pod_workers.go#L1302 ) there may be a potential dereference of the status pointer when passing this argument to the SyncTerminatedPod function. This section of the code is reached when the "case update" condition is met.WorkType == TerminatedPod:" and the status pointer is not initialized when the condition "case update.Options.RunningPod != nil:" [on line 1276](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/pod_workers.go#L1276 ). The update variable is defined on line 1248 as a result of calling the p.startPodSync(parentCtx, podUID) function. According to the function definition [p.startPodSync](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/pod_workers.go#L1132 ) when the condition ["if update.Options.RunningPod != nil && update.WorkType == TerminatingPod {" on page 1179](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/pod_workers.go#L1179 ) the function returns update and positive Boolean flags. Thus, the execution of this code meets the dereference conditions, which means that dereference status is achievable.
2. In the function [admitVAC](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/plugin/pkg/admission/storage/storageobjectinuseprotection/admission.go#L132) the interface is converted to the *storageapi.VolumeAttributesClass type [on the line 137](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/plugin/pkg/admission/storage/storageobjectinuseprotection/admission.go#L137). In the case when the cast is not successful, that is, it is being executed !ok, then there is a potential dereference on line 140 when referring to vac.Name.
3. The writeProjectFile function performs [opening the file descriptor f on line 268](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/volume/util/fsquota/project .go#L268). If you exit on line 274, a file descriptor may leak.
Could you please tell me if i am correct?

### What happened?

A pod whose only scheduling blocker is a required podAffinity term with a namespaceSelector stays Pending with no new scheduling attempt after a cluster change that makes it schedulable:

- an assigned pod matching the term labelSelector appears in a namespace whose labels match the namespaceSelector (assigned pod add), or
- labels are added to a namespace so that an existing assigned pod now matches the namespaceSelector.

The pod is only retried by the periodic unschedulable pods sweep (`--pod-max-in-unschedulable-pods-duration`, default 5m, deprecated), and it schedules successfully on the first attempt after the sweep.

A control with the same affinity term but without namespaceSelector (matching a pod in the same namespace) is requeued and scheduled within about 10s of the matching pod being added.

### What did you expect to happen?

The pod should be requeued when an assigned pod that satisfies the affinity term, including namespaceSelector evaluation, is added, consistent with the behavior for terms without namespaceSelector.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. Create namespaces ns-a and ns-c. ns-a has no labels initially.
2. Run pod worker in ns-a with labels app=worker.
3. Run pod scout in ns-c with this affinity:

```yaml
spec:
  affinity:
    podAffinity:
      requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
      - labelSelector:
          matchLabels:
            app: worker
        namespaceSelector:
          matchLabels:
            team: one
        topologyKey: kubernetes.io/hostname
```

scout stays Pending with FailedScheduling, for example `0/3 nodes are available: 3 node(s) didn't match pod affinity rules`.

4. Label the namespace: `kubectl label ns ns-a team=one`.

Expected: scout is requeued and scheduled on the worker node. Actual: no new scheduling attempt within 60s. Reproduced twice; the scheduler log shows no requeue after the namespace update.

Alternative trigger (assigned pod add): with ns-a labeled team=one from the start, create scout before worker. scout stays Pending. Then create worker. The assigned pod add event arrives (visible in the scheduler log), but scout is not requeued within 60s. Reproduced twice.

Deleting scout and recreating it schedules immediately, which shows the world is schedulable and only the event-driven retry is missing. In a longer observation the stuck pod was scheduled by the periodic sweep about 5m08s after it was parked, on the first attempt after the flush.

### Anything else we need to know?

Root cause (kubernetes/kubernetes master as of 2026-09-08, by code inspection):

- InterPodAffinity registers queueing hints only for `AssignedPod`, `TargetPod` and `Node` events. No `Namespace` event is registered, so a namespace label change cannot wake the pod.
- In `isSchedulableAfterAssignedPodChange`, the queued pod terms are matched with `podMatchesAllAffinityTerms` / `podMatchesAnyAffinityTerms` without unrolling `namespaceSelector` into `term.Namespaces`. The unrolling (`mergeAffinityTermNamespacesIfNotEmpty`) is done in the Filter and Scoring paths only. With no explicit namespaces in the term, `term.Namespaces` is empty and the `namespaceSelector` is evaluated against nil namespace labels, so the namespace half of `AffinityTerm.Matches` never succeeds and the hint returns `QueueSkip`. `podMatchesAllAffinityTerms` documents the assumption that the `NamespaceSelector` was already merged into the `Namespaces` set.
- The delete branch uses the same unmerged anti-affinity matching, so anti-affinity terms with `namespaceSelector` are likely affected for delete events as well (by code inspection, not reproduced here).

Related issues and PRs in the same family of InterPodAffinity event-driven requeue gaps: #141354 (open; pod deletion with self-affinity, plain labelSelector, different branch and term shape), #130784 (multiple required terms), #139161 (merged PR; queue hint fix for anti-affinities).

We are preparing a fix for the pod add path: unroll `namespaceSelector` before hint matching, reusing `mergeAffinityTermNamespacesIfNotEmpty`, with unit tests (the queueing hint tests currently have no `namespaceSelector` coverage), and will open a PR against master. Waking pods on namespace label changes additionally needs a `Namespace` cluster event class, which the scheduler framework does not provide today; happy to discuss whether that scope belongs in this change or a separate one. If it helps, we can also add coverage for the #141354 deletion scenario to the same test matrix.

body_text:
### What happened?

Follow-up from https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/135870, which replaced `user.Lookup("kubelet")` with a `getent passwd` shell-out.

[`getentUserExists`](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/6bb42350227f0a714f4730165e7ba622c69bd99e/pkg/kubelet/kubelet_pods.go#L188-L191) returns early when `LookPath` fails:

```go
getent, err := exec.LookPath("getent")
if err != nil {
	return false, nil // no getent: same as "not configured"
}
```

[The caller](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/6bb42350227f0a714f4730165e7ba622c69bd99e/pkg/kubelet/kubelet_pods.go#L151-L158) reads that as "no kubelet account", skips `getsubids` and returns the built-in default range. The account itself is never examined, so a local `/etc/passwd` entry is affected the same way, which is wider than the directory-service case the PR body describes.

Same node, with `getent` on PATH and then off it:

```
getent on PATH   firstID=1048576 rangeLen=8388608
getent off PATH  firstID=65536   rangeLen=4294901760
```

Before 6bb4235 the cgo `user.Lookup` resolved a local account without `getent`, so a node in this state used to get its configured range. I ran the two versions of that branch side by side against a real local account with `getent` off PATH: `user.Lookup` reports the account, `getentUserExists` reports it missing.

### What did you expect to happen?

The configured subordinate IDs to still be used when the account is in `/etc/passwd`, or something in the log saying they were skipped. Today it is a `V(5)` line and no error.

@kginonredhat suggested a fallback during review: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/135870#discussion_r3966541751

That shape looks right to me with one adjustment. I would gate it on `exec.ErrNotFound` only, since `LookPath` also returns `ErrDot` alongside a usable path, and swallowing that turns a resolvable `getent` into a missing account.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Run from anywhere inside a checkout of master. No root, cleans up after itself.

<details>
<summary>repro.sh</summary>

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
W=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$W" pkg/kubelet/zz_getent_repro_test.go' EXIT
mkdir -p "$W/with" "$W/without"

# stand-ins for a node whose /etc/passwd has a kubelet account and whose
# /etc/subuid delegates 1048576/8388608 to it
cat > "$W/with/getent" <<'G'
#!/bin/sh
[ "$1" = passwd ] && [ "$2" = kubelet ] && { echo "kubelet:x:999:999::/var/lib/kubelet:/sbin/nologin"; exit 0; }
exit 2
G
cat > "$W/with/getsubids" <<'G'
#!/bin/sh
[ "$1" = -g ] && shift
[ "$1" = kubelet ] && { echo "0: kubelet 1048576 8388608"; exit 0; }
exit 1
G
chmod +x "$W/with/getent" "$W/with/getsubids"
cp "$W/with/getsubids" "$W/without/"   # same node, only getent is off PATH

cat > pkg/kubelet/zz_getent_repro_test.go <<'T'
package kubelet

import (
	"os"
	"testing"

	"k8s.io/klog/v2/ktesting"
)

func TestGetentRepro(t *testing.T) {
	logger, _ := ktesting.NewTestContext(t)
	t.Setenv("PATH", os.Getenv("REPRO_PATH"))
	first, length, err := (&Kubelet{}).getKubeletMappings(logger, 65536)
	t.Logf("firstID=%d rangeLen=%d err=%v", first, length, err)
}
T

for d in with without; do
	printf -- '--- getent %s PATH ---\n' "$([ "$d" = with ] && echo on || echo off)"
	REPRO_PATH="$W/$d" go test ./pkg/kubelet/ -run '^TestGetentRepro$' -count=1 -v 2>&1 | grep firstID
done
```

</details>

```
--- getent on PATH ---
    zz_getent_repro_test.go:14: firstID=1048576 rangeLen=8388608 err=<nil>
--- getent off PATH ---
    zz_getent_repro_test.go:14: firstID=65536 rangeLen=4294901760 err=<nil>
```

### Anything else we need to know?

Two things a fix would have to deal with.

[`TestGetentUserExists`](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/6bb42350227f0a714f4730165e7ba622c69bd99e/pkg/kubelet/kubelet_pods_test.go#L8595-L8598) has a `"getent not installed"` case expecting `wantFound: false`, so that case has to change with the behavior. It also only asserts `found`, never the range `getKubeletMappings` ends up with, which is the part that matters here.

The second one is smaller. [The comment above the lookup](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/6bb42350227f0a714f4730165e7ba622c69bd99e/pkg/kubelet/kubelet_pods.go#L145-L150) says the account is checked first so a getsubids backend that is unreachable can be told apart from one that simply has no entry. glibc's `getent` sets exit 2 whenever `getpwnam()` returns NULL without consulting errno, while the cgo `os/user` gave `UnknownUserError` for a genuine miss and a plain error otherwise. So an account-backend error that used to stop kubelet can now arrive as exit 2 and select the default range instead. I have not reproduced a real directory-service outage, so I would treat that as a question about the contract, not a second bug.

I am happy to send the PR if the fallback is the direction people want.

<details>

```console
$ kubectl version
# N/A, reproduced by building master at 6bb42350227f0a714f4730165e7ba622c69bd99e with go1.27.1.
```

body_text:
### What happened?

kube-proxy in **iptables mode** decides whether to emit `-m nfacct --nfacct-name ...` rules based only on a probe of the **nfacct netlink subsystem** (`nfnetlink_acct`, kernel option `CONFIG_NETFILTER_NETLINK_ACCT`). It never checks that the **iptables `nfacct` match extension** (`xt_nfacct`, kernel option `CONFIG_NETFILTER_XT_MATCH_NFACCT`) is usable.

On a kernel that has the first but not the second, the probe passes, the two counters are created successfully over netlink, and every generated ruleset contains `-m nfacct` rules. `iptables-restore` is all-or-nothing, so the **entire filter+nat restore fails on every sync**, and the node ends up with **no Service rules at all** (no `KUBE-SERVICES` jump, no ClusterIP/NodePort DNAT). kube-proxy keeps running and reporting healthy to `kubectl`, retrying the identical (still failing) restore every `syncPeriod`.

Observed on an arm64 embedded vendor kernel (5.10 series) where `CONFIG_NETFILTER_NETLINK_ACCT` is enabled but `CONFIG_NETFILTER_XT_MATCH_NFACCT` is not set (`modinfo xt_nfacct` -> not found). Symptoms on that node: every pod that talks to a ClusterIP (`dial tcp <kube-apiserver ClusterIP>:443: i/o timeout`), CoreDNS / metrics-server crash-looping, namespace deletion hanging on the metrics APIService. Pods with `hostNetwork: true` were unaffected, which made it look like a CNI problem at first. The only kube-proxy log line is:

```
"Failed to execute iptables-restore" err=<...>
```

(with iptables-legacy the reported failing line is the table's `COMMIT` line, so the 3 lines of context that get logged do not even show the `-m nfacct` rule - see below.)

The workaround we ended up with is backwards: **blacklist `nfnetlink_acct`** (`install nfnetlink_acct /bin/false` + `rmmod`) so that `nfacct.New()` fails and the documented fallback ("Failed to create nfacct runner, nfacct based metrics won't be available") kicks in. Removing a working kernel feature to make kube-proxy work is not something a user should have to discover.

### What did you expect to happen?

Either of:

- kube-proxy detects that the `nfacct` iptables match is unavailable and falls back to the same behaviour as when the netlink subsystem is missing: skip the `-m nfacct` rules, keep programming Services, log once that the two nfacct-based metrics are disabled; or
- at minimum, when a restore fails while nfacct rules are enabled, kube-proxy retries **without** them instead of leaving the node with zero Service rules forever.

The nfacct rules exist only to feed two metrics (`kubeproxy_iptables_ct_state_invalid_dropped_packets_total` and `kubeproxy_iptables_localhost_nodeports_accepted_packets_total`). Losing those metrics is vastly preferable to losing all Service networking on the node.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

On any Linux node where `xt_nfacct` is built as a **module** (most distro kernels), running kube-proxy in iptables mode (`--proxy-mode=iptables`, default `conntrackTCPLiberal=false` so the `KUBE-FORWARD ... --ctstate INVALID` rule is emitted):

```bash
# make the iptables nfacct match unavailable, but leave the netlink subsystem alone
modprobe -r xt_nfacct
echo 'install xt_nfacct /bin/false' > /etc/modprobe.d/no-xt-nfacct.conf
# sanity: netlink side still works (this is all kube-proxy probes)
nfacct add probe_ok && nfacct list && nfacct del probe_ok

# restart kube-proxy on that node, then:
iptables -t nat -S KUBE-SERVICES      # -> "No chain/target/match by that name" / chain never populated
kubectl -n kube-system logs <kube-proxy-pod> | grep -i "iptables-restore"
curl -m3 https://<kube-apiserver ClusterIP>:443   # from a non-hostNetwork pod on that node -> timeout
```

kube-proxy logs `"Failed to execute iptables-restore"` on every sync and `kubeproxy_sync_proxy_rules_iptables_restore_failures_total` climbs, but the pod stays Running/Ready.

What `iptables-restore` actually returns in this situation (checked by hand with a ruleset containing one `-m nfacct --nfacct-name <counter>` rule that the kernel cannot satisfy; iptables 1.8.10):

```
# legacy backend: the failing line is the COMMIT line of the table, not the rule
iptables-restore: line 4 failed

# nf_tables backend
iptables-nft-restore v1.8.10 (nf_tables):
line 3: RULE_APPEND failed (No such file or directory): rule in chain TESTNF
```

To blame the missing match rather than a missing counter object, create the counter first (`nfacct add <name>`) - kube-proxy does this in `syncProxyRules` before generating the rules; on a kernel that *has* `xt_nfacct` the same restore then succeeds in both backends.

### Anything else we need to know?

Code on master @ `d5cbb79be9160faa3a7d7323e3294c3781c16ae7` (all in `pkg/proxy/iptables/proxier.go` unless noted):

1. [`NewProxier` L257-259](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/d5cbb79be9160faa3a7d7323e3294c3781c16ae7/pkg/proxy/iptables/proxier.go#L257-L259): `nfacct.New()`; on error the runner is nil and the fallback message is logged.
2. [`nfacct_linux.go` `New()` L66-84](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/d5cbb79be9160faa3a7d7323e3294c3781c16ae7/pkg/proxy/util/nfacct/nfacct_linux.go#L66-L84): the only capability check is a netlink `NFNL_MSG_ACCT_GET` for a dummy counter over `NETLINK_NETFILTER`. Nothing here (or anywhere else) exercises the iptables `nfacct` match.
3. [`syncProxyRules` L702-711](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/d5cbb79be9160faa3a7d7323e3294c3781c16ae7/pkg/proxy/iptables/proxier.go#L702-L711): `nfacct.Ensure(name)` for both counters; on success `nfAcctCounters[name] = true`. This succeeds on the affected kernel because `nfnetlink_acct` is present.
4. [L1015-1023](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/d5cbb79be9160faa3a7d7323e3294c3781c16ae7/pkg/proxy/iptables/proxier.go#L1015-L1023) (localhost NodePort accept rule) and [L1326-1330](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/d5cbb79be9160faa3a7d7323e3294c3781c16ae7/pkg/proxy/iptables/proxier.go#L1326-L1330) (`KUBE-FORWARD --ctstate INVALID ... DROP`) append `-m nfacct --nfacct-name <counter>` whenever the corresponding `nfAcctCounters` flag is true. The second rule is emitted on essentially every node (only `conntrackTCPLiberal=true` suppresses it), so the failure is unconditional.
5. [L1384-1394](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/d5cbb79be9160faa3a7d7323e3294c3781c16ae7/pkg/proxy/iptables/proxier.go#L1384-L1394): the single `RestoreAll` covers both `*filter` and `*nat`; on error it logs, bumps `IPTablesRestoreFailuresTotal` and returns. The deferred block at [L657-670](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/d5cbb79be9160faa3a7d7323e3294c3781c16ae7/pkg/proxy/iptables/proxier.go#L657-L670) sets `needFullSync = true`, so the next sync regenerates the identical payload and fails identically. There is no fallback path and `nfAcctCounters` is never cleared.
6. [`pkg/util/iptables/iptables.go` `parseRestoreError` L588-612](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/d5cbb79be9160faa3a7d7323e3294c3781c16ae7/pkg/util/iptables/iptables.go#L588-L612) only recognises `<cmd>: line N failed`. With the legacy backend `N` is the `COMMIT` line, so the context logged at L1387-1388 does not show the nfacct rule; with the nf_tables backend the message has extra colons and is not classified as a `ParseError` at all. So a fix cannot rely on "ParseError pointing at an `-m nfacct` line".

The nftables proxier (`pkg/proxy/nftables`) has no nfacct references and is unaffected.

Prior reports I could find are different failure modes: #126951 / #125866 / #126952 handle the case where the **netlink subsystem** is missing (that fallback works, and it is what the workaround above abuses); cri-o/cri-o#8270 was a kernel with **both** `CONFIG_NETFILTER_NETLINK_ACCT` and `CONFIG_NETFILTER_XT_MATCH_NFACCT` unset, so the existing probe caught it. I found no issue or PR covering the split configuration (netlink present, match absent).

**Proposed fix** (happy to send a PR once maintainers pick a direction):

- **(a) Probe the match, not just the subsystem.** After `Ensure()` succeeds in `syncProxyRules` (a counter must exist for the match to load), run a one-time check that the iptables `nfacct` match works - e.g. add and immediately delete a rule such as `-m nfacct --nfacct-name <counter> -j RETURN` in the existing `KUBE-PROXY-CANARY` chain via `EnsureRule`/`DeleteRule`. If that fails, set both `nfAcctCounters` entries to false and log once ("iptables nfacct match unavailable; nfacct based metrics won't be available"). Cheap, backend-agnostic, and reuses the same fallback that already exists for the netlink case.
- **(b) Defensive fallback on restore failure.** In the `RestoreAll` error branch at L1385, if any `nfAcctCounters` flag is true, clear them all, log that nfacct rules are being disabled, and return (needFullSync is already set). The next sync then succeeds. This is a heuristic (it disables the metrics on *any* restore failure) but it guarantees a node never stays without Service rules because of an optional metric.

Doing (a) with (b) as a safety net seems reasonable. A unit test can drive either path with `FakeIPTables` returning an error for rules containing `-m nfacct` and asserting the following sync succeeds with no nfacct rules and both counters disabled.

### What happened?

The resource quota controller's `QuotaMonitor` registers an event handler on the shared informer for every monitored resource (`pkg/controller/resourcequota/resource_quota_monitor.go`, `controllerFor`), but when a monitor is torn down in `SyncMonitors` (and on shutdown) it only stops the monitor — it never removes the handler:

```go
_, _ = shared.Informer().AddEventHandlerWithOptions(handlers, ...) // registration discarded
```

The informer factory caches informers per resource, so the informer outlives the monitor. When a resource such as a CRD is deleted and later recreated with the same `GroupVersionResource`, a new handler is added to the same cached informer each time and the old ones are never removed. On a started informer every handler is a `processorListener` with its own goroutines, so the handlers (and their goroutines) accumulate and kube-controller-manager memory grows.

This is the same class of bug as the garbage collector's graph builder (#114066); the quota monitor's `controllerFor` was copied from it and has the identical omission.

### What did you expect to happen?

Removing a monitored resource should also remove its event handler from the shared informer; repeatedly adding and removing the same resource should not leak handlers.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Run kube-controller-manager with `--controllers=resourcequota` and repeatedly create and delete a set of CRDs, watching the informer's per-handler goroutines (`k8s.io/client-go/tools/cache.(*processorListener).run`/`.pop`) via `/debug/pprof/goroutine`. Create 40 CRDs, wait for the quota monitor sync, delete them, repeat.

On a kind cluster (processorListener goroutines):

| step | count |
|------|-------|
| baseline | 66 |
| after creating 40 CRDs | 146 (+80) |
| after deleting them | 146 (not released — leak) |

With the handler removed on teardown the count returns to 66 after deletion.

### Anything else we need to know?

The fix follows the same approach used for the garbage collector: store the informer and the handler registration on the monitor and call `RemoveEventHandler` on teardown (in `SyncMonitors` and on shutdown). A unit-level regression test (a counting fake informer asserting no net handlers remain after add/remove cycles) is included in the PR.

### Kubernetes version

TestGrid: https://testgrid.k8s.io/sig-arch-code-organization#unit-master-golang-tip&width=20

`ci-kubernetes-unit-golang-tip` has been red since 2026-09-10. Two upstream net/http bugs, both from Go tip commit e51216de8e (CL 829984, the fix for golang/go#81404):

- golang/go#81510: readLoop reads `Response.ContentLength` after `Body.Close` returns. `k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/proxy TestRejectForwardingRedirectsOption` fails under `-race`, because `UpgradeAwareHandler` closes the backend body and then replaces `*response` in `ModifyResponse`.
- golang/go#81511: `Body.Close` after a failed Read now returns the Read error again. `k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/endpoints/filters TestPerRequestWith*` fail with `tls: bad record MAC` from `Close()`, and `pkg/server TestRequestTimeoutBehavior` fails intermittently with `unexpected EOF`. The Go authors added a test for the new behavior in the same CL, so this one may end up as a documented change rather than a fix.

Not kubernetes bugs: both reproduce with no kubernetes code (programs in the golang issues), and go1.27.1, go1.26.1 and the commit before e51216de8e are all clean. The other red on this job, the go1.27 vet check for `%d` with a pointer, is #142076. Sibling for the kind job: #141992.

Tracking here so the red canary has an explanation. Closes when both golang issues are resolved, or when this job's toolchain moves past the fixes. If 81511 becomes intended behavior, the three apiserver tests need to stop asserting `Close() == nil`.

- golang/go#81510: readLoop reads `Response.ContentLength` after `Body.Close` returns. `k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/proxy TestRejectForwardingRedirectsOption` fails under `-race`, because `UpgradeAwareHandler` closes the backend body and then replaces `*response` in `ModifyResponse`.
- golang/go#81511: `Body.Close` after a failed Read now returns the Read error again. `k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/endpoints/filters TestPerRequestWith*` fail with `tls: bad record MAC` from `Close()`, and `pkg/server TestRequestTimeoutBehavior` fails intermittently with `unexpected EOF`. The Go authors added a test for the new behavior in the same CL, so this one may end up as a documented change rather than a fix.

Not kubernetes bugs: both reproduce with no kubernetes code (programs in the golang issues), and go1.27.1, go1.26.1 and the commit before e51216de8e are all clean. The other red on this job, the go1.27 vet check for `%d` with a pointer, is #142076. Sibling for the kind job: #141992.

Tracking here so the red canary has an explanation. Closes when both golang issues are resolved, or when this job's toolchain moves past the fixes. If 81511 becomes intended behavior, the three apiserver tests need to stop asserting `Close() == nil`.

### What happened?

> Pod didn't trigger scale-up: 9 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector, 3 Insufficient cpu, 3 node(s) had untolerated taint(s), 3 in backoff after failed scale-up

### What did you expect to happen?

- When `cpu` is insufficient, the event should include the required cpu (note that this is often the sum of a number of containers, and thus something that kubernetes calculated but not something easily seen when looking at a pod)
- When `memory` is insufficient, the event should include the required memory (note that this is often the sum of a number of containers, and thus something that kubernetes calculated but not something easily seen when looking at a pod)
- When `taint` is untolerated, if there is only one (or maybe two), list it
- When `node affinity`/`node selector` isn't matched and there is only one (or maybe two), list it

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

define a pod 

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: unhappy
spec:
  affinity:
    podAntiAffinity:
      preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
      - podAffinityTerm:
          labelSelector:
            matchLabels:
              app.kubernetes.io/name: something
          topologyKey: kubernetes.io/hostname
        weight: 100
  containers:
  - image: bash
    name: main
    resources:
      limits:
        cpu: "5"
        memory: 5Gi
      requests:
        cpu: "2"
        memory: 5Gi
  - image: bash
    name: sidecar-a
    resources:
      limits:
        cpu: 700m
        memory: 1500Mi
      requests:
        cpu: 300m
        memory: 1500Mi
  - image: bash
    name: sidecar-b
    resources:
      limits:
        cpu: 630m
        memory: 1800Mi
      requests:
        cpu: 350m
        memory: 1450Mi
  initContainers:
  - args:
    - sleep 3
    command:
    - sh
    - -c
    image: bash
    name: init-1
    resources:
      limits:
        cpu: "5"
        memory: 5Gi
      requests:
        cpu: "2"
        memory: 5Gi
  - args:
    - sleep 3
    command:
    - sh
    - -c
    image: bash
    name: init-2
    resources:
      limits:
        cpu: "4"
        memory: 6Gi
      requests:
        cpu: "1"
        memory: 3Gi
  nodeSelector:
    jam: "1"
  tolerations:
  - effect: NoSchedule
    key: milk
    operator: Exists
  - effect: NoExecute
    key: node.kubernetes.io/not-ready
    operator: Exists
    tolerationSeconds: 300
  - effect: NoExecute
    key: node.kubernetes.io/unreachable
    operator: Exists
    tolerationSeconds: 300
```

create some nodes that don't perfectly match the requirements.

run:
```
kubectl events unhappy
```
trying to figure out why the pod won't work.
- Knowing which selectors/affinities were relevant would help with deciding which node(pool)s to fix
- Knowing the exact required memory/cpu would help with fixing a node(pool) to satisfy the requirements

### What happened?

`metav1.ParseToLabelSelector` rejects the `!=` operator, so the kubectl commands that build a `LabelSelector` from a user-supplied selector string fail on a selector that works everywhere else:

```console
$ kubectl create pdb web-pdb --selector='app!=web' --min-available=1
error: "!=" is not a valid label selector operator

$ kubectl set selector service web 'app!=web'
error: "!=" is not a valid label selector operator

$ kubectl get pods -l 'app!=web'     # works
```

`labels.Parse` accepts `key!=value`, but `ParseToLabelSelector`, whose comment says it "should be kept in sync with the parser in pkg/labels/selector.go", has no case for `selection.NotEquals` and falls through to the default error (only `>` / `<` are rejected deliberately):
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.37.0/staging/src/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/apis/meta/v1/helpers.go#L117-L144

`key!=value` selects exactly the objects that `key notin (value)` selects (`labels.Requirement.Matches` treats both as "key absent, or value not in the set"), so it can be represented losslessly as `LabelSelectorOpNotIn` with a single value. The reverse direction, `LabelSelectorAsSelector`, already turns `NotIn` back into a selector with the same semantics.

Callers in kubectl: `kubectl create pdb` (`create_pdb.go`) and `kubectl set selector` (`set_selector.go`).

### What did you expect to happen?

The selector is accepted and produces:

```yaml
selector:
  matchExpressions:
  - key: app
    operator: NotIn
    values: ["web"]
```

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Run either command above against any cluster, or call `metav1.ParseToLabelSelector("foo!=bar")`. A regression test that fails against the `v1.37.0` tag is in the linked PR; it also checks that every parsed `LabelSelector` selects the same label sets as the original selector string.

### Anything else we need to know?

Long-standing; the function has never handled `NotEquals`. PR to follow (one `case` in the switch plus tests).

/sig api-machinery
/sig cli

```console
$ kubectl version
Client Version: v1.37.0
```

Reproduced with a unit test against the `v1.37.0` tag; the code is unchanged on master at bc32e8eb00f.

### What happened?

`GetDiskFormat` in the staging repo `k8s.io/mount-utils` (staging/src/k8s.io/mount-utils/mount_linux.go) shells out to
`blkid -p -s TYPE -s PTTYPE -o export <disk>` and maps **exit code 2** to `("", nil)` ("disk is unformatted").

However, blkid also exits with code 2 when the device node **exists but its data cannot be read** (e.g. the storage backend is temporarily unavailable). As a result, `GetDiskFormat` returns the exact same result for two very
different situations:

1. A genuinely blank disk → `("", nil)` (expected)
2. An existing device with data whose data path is currently unreadable → `("", nil)` (misleading)

Any caller that uses an empty format to decide whether to initialize/format a device cannot distinguish the two cases.

Real-world impact: in Longhorn (a CNCF storage system using mount-utils via the CSI stack), this caused NodeStageVolume to attempt `mkfs.xfs` on existing volumes containing user data, because blkid probed them as unformatted while the engine data path was temporarily broken. The formatting only failed because mkfs itself hit read errors, so data loss was avoided by luck, not by design.
See longhorn/longhorn#14042 for the full incident log.

Relevant code:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/mount-utils/mount_linux.go#L667-L686

```go
if err != nil {
    if exit, ok := err.(utilexec.ExitError); ok {
        if exit.ExitStatus() == 2 {
            // Disk device is unformatted.
            return "", nil
        }
    }
    ...
}
```
Impact: Potential Data Loss
This bug creates a data-loss window. If the underlying data path recovers between filesystem detection and the formatting operation, mkfs.xfs -f may succeed and overwrite existing filesystem metadata, resulting in permanent data loss.


### What did you expect to happen?

`GetDiskFormat` should distinguish a blank disk from an unreadable device, for example:

- Perform a small read (e.g. first 4 KiB) on the device when blkid reports  no filesystem, and return an error if the read fails, or
- Inspect blkid's stderr/exit-code semantics more precisely so that  read failures are not reported as "unformatted".

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Using the scsi_debug module to create a device whose reads fail:

```bash
# 1. Create a scsi debug device that fails READ commands (error=3: medium error)
modprobe scsi_debug dev_size_mb=16 every_nth=1 opts=2

DEV=$(ls -d /sys/bus/pseudo/drivers/scsi_debug/adapter*/host*/target*/*/block/* | xargs -n1 basename)
echo "Device: /dev/$DEV"

# 2. blkid behaves identically to a blank disk
blkid -p -s TYPE -s PTTYPE -o export /dev/$DEV
# → no output, exit code 2 (same as a zeroed blank disk)

# 3. While a direct read fails
dd if=/dev/$DEV of=/dev/null bs=4k count=1
# → input error / I/O error
```

A consumer calling `GetDiskFormat("/dev/$DEV")` receives `("", nil)`, so it will take the "unformatted disk" path although the device is not readable.
A zeroed blank disk returns the identical value.

(Any other way of producing an unreadable block device, e.g.
device-mapper `error` target, reproduces the same behavior.)

### Anything else we need to know?

- The same `("", nil)` result is also produced for **non-block files**
  (e.g. an empty regular file), which is how the behavior was verified
  without kernel modules.
- Longhorn has worked around this at the CSI layer by re-verifying device
  readability before entering the formatting path
  (longhorn/longhorn#14042), but other in-tree and out-of-tree consumers
  of mount-utils remain exposed.
- Happy to submit a PR once the maintainers agree on the desired semantics.

<details>

  systems)
```

body_text:
### What happened?

A container still in its startup period is NotReady, as expected. Restart the kubelet on that node and the pod goes Ready within a few seconds, without the startup probe ever succeeding, and it stays Ready.

`isContainerStarted` looks up the probe workers to tell whether a container has a startup probe. `SyncPod` builds the pod status before it calls `AddPod`, so right after a kubelet restart there is no worker yet and the container is marked started. That value is kept across syncs and `worker.doProbe` stops probing once it is set, so nothing puts it back.

With a readiness probe the pod stays NotReady, but the startup gate opens and the liveness probe starts running against a container that is still warming up.

Opened #142303 with a fix.

### What did you expect to happen?

The pod stays NotReady until the startup probe succeeds. Restarting the kubelet should not change whether a container counts as started.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Create a pod with a startup probe that keeps failing and no readiness probe:

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: slow-start
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: busybox:1.36
    command: ["sh", "-c", "sleep 3600"]
    startupProbe:
      exec:
        command: ["false"]
      periodSeconds: 10
      failureThreshold: 180
```

Once it is running:

```
$ kubectl get pod slow-start -o jsonpath='{.status.containerStatuses[0].started}'
false
```

Restart the kubelet on that node, wait a few seconds, then check again:

```
$ kubectl get pod slow-start -o jsonpath='{.status.containerStatuses[0].started}'
true

$ kubectl get pod slow-start
NAME         READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE
slow-start   1/1     Running   0          5m
```

The startup probe is not run again after this.

### Anything else we need to know?

A container still in its startup period is NotReady, as expected. Restart the kubelet on that node and the pod goes Ready within a few seconds, without the startup probe ever succeeding, and it stays Ready.

`isContainerStarted` looks up the probe workers to tell whether a container has a startup probe. `SyncPod` builds the pod status before it calls `AddPod`, so right after a kubelet restart there is no worker yet and the container is marked started. That value is kept across syncs and `worker.doProbe` stops probing once it is set, so nothing puts it back.

With a readiness probe the pod stays NotReady, but the startup gate opens and the liveness probe starts running against a container that is still warming up.

Opened #142303 with a fix.

### What did you expect to happen?

The pod stays NotReady until the startup probe succeeds. Restarting the kubelet should not change whether a container counts as started.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Create a pod with a startup probe that keeps failing and no readiness probe:

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: slow-start
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: busybox:1.36
    command: ["sh", "-c", "sleep 3600"]
    startupProbe:
      exec:
        command: ["false"]
      periodSeconds: 10
      failureThreshold: 180
```

Once it is running:

```
$ kubectl get pod slow-start -o jsonpath='{.status.containerStatuses[0].started}'
false
```

Restart the kubelet on that node, wait a few seconds, then check again:

```
$ kubectl get pod slow-start -o jsonpath='{.status.containerStatuses[0].started}'
true

$ kubectl get pod slow-start
NAME         READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE
slow-start   1/1     Running   0          5m
```

The startup probe is not run again after this.

### What happened?
In `pv_controller` (`isVolumeReleased` in `pkg/controller/volume/persistentvolume/pv_controller.go:1382`), the controller inspects the local informer claim cache (`ctrl.claims.Get(claimName)`) to verify if a claim bound to a PV is released before marking the volume released or performing volume cleanup.

**Race Window:**
If a claim state changes or is updated in the API server, but the local informer cache experiences watch delay, `pv_controller` reads stale claim state from its cache and can proceed to release or delete a persistent volume prematurely.

### What did you expect to happen?
Before executing irreversible volume deletion or release actions, `pv_controller` should re-verify the live PVC object against the API server.

### Related Pull Requests
- #141891 (`pv_controller`: revalidate claim live before deleting released volume)

### Kubernetes Version
`master` / `v1.32+`

### What would you like to be added?

Right now, we fuzz the internal version, then convert internal -> external -> internal and verify the object didn't lose data.
In some cases, e.g. https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/137633, internal -> external is lossy by design (e.g. new internal fields for non-serialized types), which means we need to add fuzzer funcs to clear any such data in the internal type when fuzzing.

This leaves a little bit of a coverage gap, that could be closed by also going the other way: fuzz external, then convert external -> internal -> external, and verify equivalence.

### Why is this needed?

This would improve the coverage of some special cases of API conversion.
